Asked whether the taking of people aboard craft for examination infringes on free will, he does not dodge. We would consider that an infringement, he says. And on the Confederation's own methods, a confession. We found that we are no better than our instruments, he says. We forget that we have no right to impress even the most beautiful of gifts upon people.

The evening closes with the thought it began with, distilled. Look into your brother's eyes, he says. He is the Creator.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Sword of Not Judging
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the sword of not judging.

October seventeenth, nineteen seventy-six. A new voice enters the archive, the one known as Oxal, and his whole message is brotherhood. The Confederation, he says, is indeed a brotherhood, and our purpose is one: to share with you our understanding of love. The Confederation, he says, is indeed a brotherhood, and our purpose is one: to share with you our understanding of love. If we could share with the peoples of your planet this understanding, those troubles which each of you has with your brothers would be no more.

It is a difficult thing to give up, that judging of yourself and of others. It is a difficult thing to love yourself and others in a totally trusting way. Yet this is precisely the key to understanding, he says: that you are capable of many, many imperfect acts, yet your heart is perfect.

For brotherhood, he says, is only possible through the Creator. You will never be one with your brothers on the level of man to man, for imperfections breed discontent. Yet by the grace of the Creator within you and within your brother, there is a link so strong and so perfect that it can make the most opposite and diverse personalities one. And this transformation occurs when a brother stops seeking a brother in love, and seeks only to rejoice in the Creator who is in his brother, be he a friend or a foe.

There is such a confusion among your peoples, he says, in which you speak incessantly of right and wrong, and spend endless time in discussion. Yet harmony will never come on that level; right and wrong will never be discovered on that level. From the smallest relationship to the greatest of your nations' relationships, brotherhood can never be achieved by reason, but only, as you would call it, by prayer and meditation.

People are not alike, yet love has created them all. And the Creator within them is lovable, is love itself, and can speak to you of love in the face of the most inharmonious aspect on the outer plane. It has been written in your holy works that the master who teaches the consciousness of Christ brought not peace, but a sword. And this is the sword we ask you to accept in your lives, he says: the sword of not judging, the sword of even willing to be foolish in another's eyes.

Moreover, there is a great satisfaction in vengeance or getting even. But what you are doing, he says, when you answer those who judge you with an answering judgment, is collecting your karma, there on the spot. Far better that you allow the karma that has come to you to die, as you forgive, and in that forgiveness, the karma that is reflected from you is satisfied.

Whatever one has done to you, let it end there, my brothers. Brotherhood is never an equal partnership, for each brother will give more than half. You are your brother. Do not think of equality; think of finding more room in your heart for forgiving and understanding. You are not doing this for another. You are doing this for your brother, who is you.

Through another instrument that evening, Oxal takes up the instrument itself: you. You are the mirror of truth and of light, he says. Each individual must take upon himself the responsibilities of light: to progress spiritually, and to allow the love to take form within you, and to be shared with those around you. You should not indulge in mental activities that are harmful to you or your brother: activity such as judgment, activity such as possessing, or limiting in any way the thoughts or actions of another.

You are unlimited beings, he says, and you lead an unlimited experience. What you do unto yourself is not only done to you, but it is done to all around you. The Creator finds no separation between you and your brother, for your energy fields coincide and enmesh together.

You are instruments in many, many ways, he says, and you can choose what forms of instrumentality you desire to use. But do not block your instrumentality through lack of faith in his ability to work through you and his willingness to perfect you. Fear not, my friends, for fear is the creator of that experience.

Ask nothing in your prayers, either of us or of the Creator, that is of a selfish nature, he says. Ask to be guided as a servant and all that you need shall be provided. In order to receive the right to demonstrate to and share with others the truth that you are, you must first become that truth, and merge entirely with it. You must be one with the Creator, for he is the truth, and through him, you shall reflect that truth to others.

You are not alone, my friends. You stand with the Creator and your fellow man upon the brink of a civilization which is to be brought about in your actions: in harmony and in service to one another and in tune with your Creator. Call upon love, he says, and we are there.

Thank you for listening.

title: You Are as Harps
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: you are as harps.

October twenty-fourth, nineteen seventy-six. Your life in its entirety is an accumulation of lessons, he says, lessons which you have designed to experience, lessons through which you can learn the truths that will enable you to bring about the existence that you truly desire. And that existence may be expressed in many words, but any orthodox expression would be the existence within heaven.

Heaven, he says, is wherever you place it. It is wherever you desire it to be. It is an eternal factor. Thus, it is not to be gained, but recognized and accepted. And in order to come to the realization that you indeed exist within that heaven which you desire, you must undergo what we have called tribulations. Circumstances which test your emotional stability, your intellectual stability, and most of all, your spiritual stability and dedication.

When confronted with situations which are incomprehensible through your intellect, accept it and face it, he says, knowing that it has been desired by you as an experience for the opportunity of growth. Enter into the experience with an attitude of love, of love which contains no resentment or fear. Accept that which you have created, for indeed, you have brought it into existence. Know that, no matter how it appears, it is for the best.

We cannot stress the importance, he says, of the factor known as faith at these times. You are portion and particle of the creative force that permeates the universe. Attune yourself to that presence within you through your meditations. Your abilities are infinite. Your love is also infinite. There are no limitations placed upon you by your Creator. They are placed upon you by yourself, in your acceptance of them.

Many situations will bring you to despair. Feel not guilty, he says, for this feeling of despair is only natural upon your planet. During your trials, you shall be influenced by the mortality which you have chosen to possess. It is as the negative and positive poles, the mortal and the immortal, one knowing limitation, the other knowing infinity. Yet neither is complete without the other.

Your existence within the physical environment is vital and essential to your growth, he says, for you have desired it. The kingdom of heaven lies within you, so say your scriptures. Seek not outside of your form, deity. But know the deity that is in you. And when you come to the day that all things may be offered you that at one time were tests to you, and you no longer even need to ask yourself if they are desired, then you shall walk with the masters.

To walk with those teachers, he says, you must be above the influences of the physical level of existence, and yet remain in it. It is a long and tedious journey that you have chosen. And once again: you must have faith in your Creator, and above all, in yourself. Know that you are divine. Know that you shall succeed. You are the master of your universe.

Through another instrument that evening, Hatonn answers the question every seeker asks in the dark: if indeed I chose these tribulations, whatever was on my mind when I did that? Before you came into the physical illusion, he says, you were in an atmosphere where thoughts were as real to you as the physical objects of your illusion are now. And you asked yourself, if you were put to the test, would you still know what love was? Would you still seek the Creator with all your heart?

And so you came into this illusion. He offers the image of your armed forces, where parents hope that their child will become a man. Service under these conditions is more difficult, yet under difficult conditions, one develops more rapidly. And so it is with you, he says. Whatever else you needed to do while you were here, your basic motive was to penetrate the things of this illusion with your discrimination, so that you could see the love and the light, the heaven that penetrates all that there is. It is when things become difficult that you seek to know the reason.

In all space and time, wherever polarity of good and evil exists, he says, those entities which the Creator tossed into the void have forever and ever turned back to the Creator with an instinct that cannot be denied. We are a timeless answer to a timeless question.

In your tribulation, in your difficulty, know that this is an opportunity for you to discern, he says, to seek out that which will not rust and will not spoil, to unlock from within your heart those feelings which will long exist.

And the evening closes with the harps. You are as harps, he says. You have the power to tune yourselves to harmony or disharmony. You cannot control the wind that blows through you. You can only control the sound that you can produce when the wind touches you. The wind of experience can blow hot and cold, harshly and gently. Yet, you have the key: you may tune yourselves. You are all one. You are all in harmony. It is only a matter of finding that sweet harmony.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Way of the Masters
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the way of the masters.

October twenty-sixth, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn opens with the mission, and with the strange limit built into it. This is our mission, he says: to speak to you. We have spoken to you for many, many of your years. But we are limited. The information must be given to the peoples of your planet. It is urgently needed. Yet we cannot give it in any manner that would prove to them beyond questionable doubt that it comes from us.

It is necessary to act in this way, he says, because to act in any other way would destroy the primary benefit that each of you on Earth receives in your stay here. You are here primarily to experience a condition of voluntary choice. Each thought that you think is yours to choose. It is necessary to choose wisely if you are to progress. But the choice must always be up to the individual and not impressed from some external source.

Each of you here tonight is aware enough of what we have given you to make wise choices in your thinking, he says. All that is lacking is possibly diligence, diligence in choosing thoughts. This is the way of the masters. Your thinking is all that exists. The entire universe is thought. Make use of your present condition, for it has been chosen, it has been desired, in fact totally programmed by yourself. It is for your benefit, each of you individually. Make use of your present condition, for this is what you planned to do. Do it, to reach that goal that each of us so earnestly desires: the goal of union in thinking with our Creator.

It is, he says, a strange and devious path to this understanding. But if it were not necessary it would not exist. Become aware of each second of your existence. Know in fullest detail the motivations of each of your actions and each of your thoughts. Meditate and become aware. Use this awareness then, to act. It is only necessary to meditate. In your meditation, the understanding that you seek will be easily revealed.

It is necessary that the individual gain knowledge in this manner, he says, for only in this manner can he become able to direct his own thinking. In any other manner, he is not truly evolving, but simply reacting. And the name of this game in which you now find yourselves is evolution. That is the secret behind all the activities upon your planet: an evolution of mind.

Through another instrument that evening, Hatonn takes up the promise from your holy works that you need not ponder what your needs are, because they will be met by the Father. This is a truth which has been much misunderstood, he says. One may hold in one's hand those words which have been spoken by the master known as Jesus, one can know them by heart, and one can proclaim them to others, and yet if one is speaking them and not living them, they will not be true for him. For his consciousness is still dwelling in the precincts of the illusion.

It is only in meditation and contemplation of that presence which is more real than your very breathing, he says, that you become aware of the actual reality of the Creator. Once for one moment in a day you have touched this reality, you walk forth bearing that reality as a cup bears the life-giving fluid within it. Then the Creator will fulfill your every need. And the Creator will put his concentration upon what you need. Within the illusion, you are ofttimes mistaken about what you truly need. The Creator is never mistaken.

Therefore, he says, leave all high-sounding words and all appearances, and seek within yourself for the silence in which is that still, small voice. We are here to ask you to claim your birthright as the creator of your thoughts and therefore of your universe. Link your thoughts with the Creator, and let him think your life.

It is very, very important to know yourself, he says. This is your first mission upon this planet, to know your own thinking. There is only one way for you to do this and that is through meditation. It is impossible to analyze in a conscious manner your own thinking. For this reason, meditate each day. This is of prime importance. In no other way can you fulfill your own desire to grow into that form of thought that you have chosen for your own. For that form, my friends, is a form of total love.

And the final word of the evening. There is but one other thing that we would wish to pass through this instrument, he says, and that is that each of you will be completely successful. You cannot help but be so, for you have chosen a path which terminates in success. The only factor in the slightest question is the rate down which you travel this path. That rate is a function of but one thing: a function of your thinking.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Free Dancer
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the free dancer.

October thirtieth, nineteen seventy-six. Hatonn opens with the smallest curriculum in the archive. We are here for one purpose, he says: to bring to you that knowledge that is essential. There is only one essential knowledge. There is very, very little that is really necessary to know. But it is necessary to know this very small amount very, very well, beyond any question. Then you must use it to its fullest capacity.

And why should we give to you this gift? Because that is part of the understanding, he says. When you possess it, you desire nothing more than to give it away. For in possessing it, you can do nothing but give it away.

In this creation, there are many, many facets, many planets, many stars, many galactic systems. And yet each of these things is a part of one thing, he says. That one thing we call creation, a creation of our thought, for we are parts of the Creator. It is possible to understand the expression that created this creation and ourselves, and act so as to reflect the essence of this expression. Then you have all knowledge.

It is necessary, if the individual is to become aware of that knowledge, for him to meditate, he says. In truth, there is no complexity, there is no problem without an answer. All that is necessary is that you avail yourself in meditation to the knowledge that is part of you. It is part of you because you are the child of the one Father.

This meditation may be done at any time or any place, he says. It is not necessary that you take any particular position at any particular time of day. It is not necessary for you to be in the dark or by yourself or even to close your eyes. With practice you will be able to clear the conscious mind of the trivial daily activities which constantly beset it, and become instantly aware of the real creation.

There are many answers that can be provided through the process of meditation, he says. However, they all dissolve to a single understanding. That understanding will transcend any intellectual complexity which you may be presently aware of. Each of you may receive as much as you wish, at any time that you wish, at any place that you wish. The process of meditation is so important that we cannot overstress it.

Through another instrument that evening, Hatonn gives us the first of two images to carry. Meditation is the key to what you desire, he says. In meditation, as you become accustomed to that contact with the Creator, your identity becomes more aligned with the truth of who you really are. And in that meditation, your universe expands, for you no longer feel boxed in a little room. That furniture melts away, and suddenly you are in a very large, very beautiful, very spacious place, in which the sun is shining, and in which that peace reigns that you seek.

It is the function of the physical illusion, he says, to box you in, to make you feel crowded, to press you into a situation in which you feel pressure. In meditation, you release that pressure by changing your identity. Therefore, when you are feeling crowded, pressed by the difficulties of life, take hold of the image of yourself as being a completely free dancer in an infinite space which is filled with light. You are a creative person; you are a dancer. You do not walk; you dance. You are not in darkness; you are in light.

And the second image, the pearl. Your spirit came to the physical plane, he says, and willingly buried itself in what you may consider to be dust. Yet there was a reason. Think of how a pearl is made, a speck of sand that aggravates and pains the living tissue, and yet, in its pain, that which is added becomes a pearl. Your spirit may be polished and burnished until it gives light to others and to yourself. This will happen, and that it causes pain is simply the way the process works.

The evening turned to questions, and to the harvest. Will it occur all at once, a listener asks, or will it be spread out over a period of time? The latter is correct, he says. What has been spoken of as the harvest has already begun, and will continue for several of your years. It will not happen all at once, any more than any natural process happens all at once. It is simply that as you see the leaves upon the trees falling, although they do not fall all at the same time, there is a period when they are all on the tree, and there is a period when your trees are bare.

Asked about the basic cause of the upheavals in the Earth itself, Hatonn answers with a single image. When the thought of those upon the surface becomes unbalanced, and these peoples become fragmented and inharmonious in their thinking, these people, like germs, infect the organism of the planetary vibration. The basic cause of the disease which is known to your scientists by so many scientific terms is simply, he says, a virus of disharmony.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Cosmic Examination
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the cosmic examination.

It is Halloween night, nineteen seventy-six, and a voice calling itself Hatonn tells a small room of seekers that their entire planet is sitting down to a test. Not a punishment. An examination. And then, patiently, he tells them what the test is actually about, and what happens to those who pass it and those who do not.

I love how plain he is about it. Your planetary sphere, he says, is marking the end of a cycle of existence, and each of you will, as he puts it, take a cosmic examination. Those who pass will go on to the next level and enter the next lesson. Those who do not pass will have to repeat this Earthly grade once again. No fire. No thunder. Just school, on a scale we can barely imagine.

And what is the message they have come to give? He says it is a very simple message, and much required by your peoples at this time. One Creator, and we are that Creator. We have been created by love and we are love. In all things apparently so different there is an underlying unity, and that unity is love. In all experiences that are so difficult there is an underlying understanding that unifies the disparity, and that essence is love. At your beginning and at your ending is love.

He says the instincts of ordinary people already know this, which is where all the religions and philosophies came from. The trouble is that the illusion complicates the simple thing. Distinctions begin to be made between brothers and between understandings, and the unity is lost.

He is honest about the intellect, which is a thought he returns to like a pebble in the shoe. The intellect will, by its very nature, analyze, criticize, discern each experience with which it comes in contact. So whatever you touch with your physical fingers will forever seem to you to be this and that, and not love. The mind is a fine tool for naming parts. It is the wrong tool for seeing the whole.

This is why the voice keeps coming back to one practice. Form the habit of meditation. Only when the intellectual mind is quieted, he says, can the inner self begin to function, and you may begin to realize your connection with the infinite love of the Creator. Listen to how they put it: you may begin to feel that love flowing through you and making a mind of unity between you and your brothers, be they your friends, your enemies, or even total strangers.

There is a passage I want to stay with. It is often assumed among your peoples, he says, that in order to belong to the company of the faithful you must have some emotional experience, some sincere or insincere thrill. But with or without emotions, your birthright is not a matter of faith but of reality. You are a child of the Creator. It is a simple thing, not necessary to be believed but to be experienced. I love that line. Not believed but experienced.

Someone asks how to send energy to a person who needs help. Hatonn answers with a small instruction, and it is the kindest thing in the whole evening. Visualize the person, he says, and then visualize the white and perfect light and love of the Creator flowing from the Creator through you and to that person, so that it totally surrounds them. And here is the part I keep turning over: visualize that person in their real condition. That is, in a perfect condition. See the perfection, not the wound.

And when someone asks whether a person's special work can be done without the conscious mind ever knowing about it, Hatonn answers in two parts. First, your one primary purpose in this incarnation is to become aware of your true self, and in doing so to vibrate in harmony with love. This one vibratory thought created all that there is, and as you come into harmony with it you become a beacon of light to all those about you. Being is always more important than doing.

The second part is gentler still. Your missions need not be grand. It is impossible for you to judge, inside the illusion, the importance of what you do. The master Jesus, he reminds them, was a carpenter, and yet his mission was great. So in all humility, do that which is in front of you to do, and love. That is your first mission.

He closes with a sentence that feels like the door of the whole evening swinging open. That which you imagine fondly as heaven, he says, is nothing more than the final realization that all is truly love. You do not have to go far. You do not have to die a physical death to enter that kingdom of heaven. It is about you. Meditate, and seek thy kingdom.

The examination is not coming. It is already here. And the whole of it, according to Hatonn, is one question asked in a thousand forms. Have you remembered that you are love?

Thank you for listening.

title: The Key of Knowing Thyself
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the key of knowing thyself.

It is the first Sunday of November, nineteen seventy-six, and Hatonn begins with a sorting of people that sounds almost too blunt, until you hear where it is going. There are those who seek the truths and knowledges available to them. There are those who seek only material possessions and emotional involvements, the temporal happiness. And there are those who vacillate in the middle. No judgment, he says. But to each of these he brings the same law.

The law is one you have heard for two thousand years, and Hatonn gives it again as if it were new. To know thyself. One of the teachers your planet received, the one you call the Christ, commanded it to his disciples. If you wish to journey through this life and gain from it the greatest benefit, he says, then you must first, above all things, know thyself. Know what you desire. Know what you will do to attain it. Know how you react to all situations, and leave out nothing.

And then he names the thing that gets in the way. It is the ego. Not as a villain but as a kind of smudged glass. When you view yourself, he says, the ego interferes and disrupts a proper and fair evaluation. It continually seeks the enhancement of your opinion of yourself. It wants recognition of oneself rather than acceptance of one's true identity. And your true identity, he says, is divine. Your true identity is perfect. Your true identity is in balance.

I love how practical the voice gets here. Deep within you, he says, is the presence of the Creator, and you have gathered about that presence a density you have called yourself, or your physical body. It is within your capability to penetrate that density and enter into the presence of the Creator, which is instilled within you.

Listen to how they put it about difficulty. Many times as you travel through this life you will experience difficulties, and each difficulty is placed before you in order that you may come to a realization. As you penetrate the density and enter the presence of your Creator, you will find that you shed layer by layer those fears and doubts and anxieties that you have drawn unto yourself. And as these things are taken from you, the true existence of which you are becomes clearer and clearer. The hardship is not an obstacle to the knowing. It is the curriculum of the knowing.

Then comes the passage about the keys, and it is worth hearing slowly. There are doors within you, Hatonn says, and you contain the key to each door. The key to one door may be service to a particular individual. The key to another may be service to a group. The key to another may be the discipline of willingly accepting a profession by which to acquire material needs. And the key to another may be the acceptance of the discipline of studies. Yet the key of greatest importance, the key which opens the door of knowledge as to what other keys to use, is the key we have called many times: meditation. To his knowledge, he says, there is no greater way to come into the realization of one's true identity.

He says something else about love here that stops me cold. Love one another and you shall indeed love yourself. But love not yourself and indeed you cannot love another. For you must know what love is from within you in order to share it with others. All things lead back to the same position no matter in what direction you turn.

Then the tone changes, and the voice grows almost tender. Within your illusion, he says, although you are in a community you seem to be always alone. And your aloneness is the key to many understandings. Until you understand how to be alone you will never be able to fully be a part of a group. And yet, until one is able to share in community, one cannot totally use the time alone. It is a circular problem. To be alone is in the end impossible, for you are one with all that there is. And to be with a group is impossible, for there is only one. So you are within the physical. It is a mystery. Yet through meditation you may find the heart of being alone and the heart of being part of the community.

In your solitude, he says, realize first that you are in direct relation to love, and that this love is your whole existence and all else is the appearance of love. In your communion with others, realize that the blessings and the troubles are possible only through the relationship of love between you. That is the whole of it, laid down like a hand of cards on a table.

He leaves them with one honest sentence. To know yourself is not a task that will end. It is simply a task that will progress. And as you progress the way will be lighted. And though your load be heavy, it will be so much easier, through understanding, to carry it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Seek the Divinity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: seek the divinity.

It is mid-November, nineteen seventy-six, and Hatonn opens the evening with something like a confession of method. The Confederation usually addresses groups with philosophical viewpoints, he says, and among those viewpoints there are clues. Two of the clues matter more than all the rest. The practice of meditation. And the practice of service unto your fellow man, which is in itself the expression of love.

Then he redefines service, and the redefinition is the whole of the evening. Service comes in many forms, and it is your choice which to use. You need not lift a hand. You need not render physical assistance. All that is needed is to truly love one another. A love which is not possessive. A love that is pure from the very existence from which it has come.

He takes love further than comfort usually allows. One who truly loves, he says, can look upon disease and one who truly loves can look upon all forms of decadence and view perfection, and know that underneath that which is viewed lies the potentiality of perfect being. Love is not a feeling about the lovable. It is a kind of sight. It sees the perfection underneath the wound.

He is honest about why the wound exists at all. Within you, he says, there are both portions vital to bringing forth the balance you seek: that which you would label negative and that which you would call positive. If it were not for both poles existing, there would be no knowledge of one or the other, no recognition of balance. What seems imbalanced to you is but an experience through which you may learn.

And then he tells them what time it is. Each of you has entered this life at a vital time in the history of your peoples, he says. Lying before you is an opportunity which man has sought for innumerable generations. The opportunity of bringing about what you may call a golden era. A rebirth of consciousness. A rebirth of awareness. A rebirth of the knowledge of the divinity within each man.

Listen to how they put it about what your sitting still actually does. As you sit in meditation, as you love one another and render service to one another, from within your being are projected those energies which will flow throughout not only the sphere on which you live but throughout the universe. Energies of love attracting to itself like energies of love, each magnifying the other. With each little portion of love that you send out upon the ether waves, you have rendered service unto your fellow man.

And the instruction that follows is practical and stern at once. Seek not the discrepancies you may find within each person you view. Seek that divinity. Seek out that perfection that lies within each of us. Whatever your role in life, he says, accept it willingly, knowing you are fulfilling that minute portion which is necessary to bring into existence the heaven your peoples seek. Strive to succeed, and you succeed for all.

Later in the evening the voice takes an unexpected turn. Hatonn says they have tried many ways of reaching us. They have described their peaceful society, their government, all the desirable components of a life lived in peace and honesty. And yet, he admits, this message, while attractive, does not call many among your peoples to the practice of meditation. So they offer something humbler. They simply suggest meditation on a trial basis. Try it, is what he is saying. See what happens.

And here is the sentence I want to hold up to the light. Whatever you may seek you will find. So your choice of what you are going to seek within this physical experience is all-important. If what you seek lies within the illusion, you will have some measure of success, yet how poor you will be in those ways that even now you know exist. You pass from this brief experience leaving your bank account behind, and yet facing the spiritual banker. Seek those things of the spirit, and all else will follow as is needed.

He is disarmingly honest about his own people, too. We do not promise heaven in the sense that meditation offers an easy street. Within our brotherhood we have dissension and disagreement, discussion and argument. We are not without imperfections. We often do not see the total picture. It is simply that at least we are being honest in a way we have gained by virtue of continued seeking. We are a little more in touch with who we are than your peoples. Meditate, my friends.

Then a question about the Tree of Life, the Kabbala, draws out one of the most beautiful passages of the night. Hatonn calls it an extremely appropriate and accurate description of the spiritual paths, using symbols of positive and negative, male and female, to describe the process of seeking the Creator. Its truths are very simple. But then listen to this: the Kabbala is a structure made of words. Words are fallible and will break down, but communion with the Creator is without words and is beyond thought, and it will preserve and sustain when nothing else will.

A structure made of words will fall. The wordless meeting will hold.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mission Is Being
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mission is being.

It is late November, nineteen seventy-six, and the evening opens with a blessing from a voice the group rarely hears. Philip of the Brotherhood of the Seven Rays comes only to say his peace is with them and to leave them three words: love each other, serve each other. Then the channel changes, and a new speaker takes the floor. He calls himself Oxal. He says it is rare that he is given the opportunity to speak. And then he gives one of the most demanding discourses in the archive.

His subject is what you chose to do here, and his first move is to take every measurement off the table. Each individual upon your sphere, he says, is an instrument of the Creator, and each, before the incarnation, chose to fulfill what you would call destiny. Some chose to work with one another and love one another in simple fashion. Some chose the responsibilities of a teacher. Yet no matter what you chose, whether it seems a task of simplicity or of great magnitude, it cannot be measured. Your worth to the Creator, your worth to your fellow man, your worth to the entire universe is immeasurable, as is your existence.

Listen to how they put it: you are an infinite being. You are instilled with divinity. You are of the utmost importance. Without your existence the creation would be incomplete. I have read that passage a dozen times and it never stops landing. Not useful. Not accomplished. Not admired. Necessary. The whole thing does not close without you.

Never, he says, judge that which you are to do once you become aware of it. Seek it out, and proceed knowing you are going about being your Father's business. And then the line that undoes every activist in the room, myself included. Do not attempt to do the Creator's business. Be that business. The work is not a task laid on top of you. The work is the quality of what you are while you move through the day.

He is unsentimental about negativity. Learn to be bombarded by all negativity, he says, and meet it with your own positive energies and with the love and light which resides within you, and overcome that negativity, purify it, encase it in the light, and send it back from whence it came with your blessings. You alone, he says, are in control of your life and all the influences within it.

And then he tells them the passing grade, and it is a stunner. You cannot learn ninety-nine percent and pass, my friends. The passing grade is one hundred percent. This life, he is saying, is not a survey course. It is a full curriculum, and the Creator would not allow you to take upon yourself a greater task than what you can achieve.

I love what he says about helping people who do not want help. Give assistance to those who request it, he says. But the hardest thing for those truly dedicated is to render no assistance to those they know would not accept it. All you can do for those is to love them and to bless them and allow them to go their way.

Then Oxal gives his definition of love, and it arrives as an acrostic, of all things. Love is luminescence, the light within you. Omnipresence, everywhere vacillating and flowing forever eternally within you. It cannot be smitten. It cannot be hidden. It cannot be denied. Love is the most potent energy of the universe and it shall succeed over that which you call darkness.

When Oxal leaves, Hatonn returns with a story about humility. In your holy works, he says, the master known as Jesus knelt upon the ground and washed the dusty feet of his students. That he did as a lesson. Many among your peoples feel they are stronger than their brothers and must help them. Yet no one, my friends, is strong. Each is a collection of the strong and the weak. And in your strength you can only stay strong by giving that strength to others.

The questions that night turn to dreams, and Hatonn speaks of the spirit as a being starved by the active daily existence, refreshed in sleep, when it is free of the gross physical form. Dreaming, he says, is that being taking instruction, working out deeper difficulties, storing up energies with which to animate the body during the waking period. Without it, the physical being would soon be unable to function. The soul goes to school at night too.

And he closes with a thought about teachers and guidance. One not only can receive instruction from teachers beyond the veil, he says, one almost always does. It is simply that these contacts are not often remembered. If you work toward sensitizing your memory, you will begin to remember being given instructions by your teachers. This is the life of the soul.

So the mission, if you want it plain: not the great deed but the great being.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Thought That Creates
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the thought that creates.

It is the last Sunday of November, nineteen seventy-six, and Hatonn opens with a sentence that reverses the whole direction of the help. People ask what would bring a more advanced race to do such standoffish and unrewarding work among less advanced peoples. And the answer, he says, is that his people no longer need to spend their time and talent to gain money so that they may live. They are, as he puts it, independently wealthy. They have all that they need. And yet they have the need to grow. They cannot grow in power or riches. They can grow only in knowledge. And this growth in knowledge is only possible through sharing the knowledge they have with their brothers. We need you in order to grow.

I love that. It is only proper, he says, that we should meet each other, for all of creation is based upon giving one element to another. All of the creation, which you may observe in your daily life as the seasons change, is a balance, a harmony, and a flux, one element giving opportunity for the other to flourish.

Then he turns the mirror on us. So many of your peoples, he says, have been taught to rush blindly from one experience to another, filling in any space of time that is left empty by another experience. Thus the flow, the harmony, the balance of your own understanding is blocked, for you are constantly thinking, constantly reacting. He compares us to chain smokers. As the smoker smokes one cigarette after another, he loses the taste. The very experience he is seeking eludes him more and more.

The remedy is one word. Silence. In whatever manner you choose to practice meditation, silence holds the key to your understanding of yourself and the creation around you.

Now comes the passage that gives this episode its title, and I want to handle it carefully because it is the boldest claim in the evening. Each and every individual, Hatonn says, is nothing other than a projection of a pure thought from that source which we call the Creator. Each thought has taken upon itself forms of personal identities. And if it is true that your existence has been brought about by none other than the thought of the Creator, and if it is true, as your holy scripture states, that man is created in the image and likeness of his Creator, then it is true that your thought brings into existence the creation in which you live.

You are a thought, thinking. And the quality of the thinking makes the world. There are certain laws that are undeniable and unbreakable, he says. Yet it is your choice in which directions to go and what creations you wish to experience. It is necessary for man upon the planet Earth at this time, above all others, to learn to control the thought projections, especially those which are detrimental not only to other individuals but to your Earth sphere and its environment.

He is tender about where people look. Those upon planet Earth seek that divine intelligence they call God. They use the intellect to search for Him in books. They search for Him in dwellings called churches. And most often fail to recognize that He is working through them, from within them. The kingdom of heaven lies within, and indeed these words are true. You are not fallen angels. You are creators working together, whether you be aware of it or not.

It is so simple, my friends, he says, that man has missed the simplicity of existence. It is not within the intellectual capabilities of man to totally understand the words we speak. But it is indeed within the spiritual intellect of man to understand all things. And for the physical intellect and the spiritual intellect to work together in harmony, an attunement must be made. An attunement which takes away the barriers of limitation and judgment, and draws all knowledges together, and all is known.

What is asked for this is dedication. Dedication to service of your fellow men. Dedication to fulfillment of your Creator's will. Dedication to bringing about the most perfect being that you can be. The disciplines the masters have taken upon themselves look difficult in the eyes of mortal men. But once they are internalized, they too take upon themselves the simplicity of truth.

He closes the evening with an image I have been carrying around all week. Your group is now in harmony and at peace, he says, so let your hearts carry that peace out with you into another world that may not look like what your heart looks like right now. All of creation speaks of harmony, and it takes a very special eye to see it. That is the eye that is informed in meditation. That is the ear that is informed in meditation. That is the heart that is informed in meditation.

The thought that creates the world can also remake it. And the remake begins in the quiet.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Co-Creator's Hands
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the co-creator's hands.

It is mid-December, nineteen seventy-six, and Hatonn speaks through a new instrument with a subject he returns to again and again: free will, and what it costs to honor it. We are helpless in some respects, he says, for we can only give information in certain limited ways. That, and only that which is desired, will be given. Only that which is desired will be received. We have to offer what we understand to be a truth and beauty far beyond what is experienced upon your planet, yet we can only offer it in a very limited way. Free will must be at all times the criteria for our communicating.

I love the honesty of that. The great cosmic teachers are not all-powerful. They are waiting on our asking. Those upon your planet will be receiving, as always, precisely what they desire. And then he says the sentence that reframes every complaint about the state of the world: even though that which you experience may seem far from what you desire, it is precisely what you desire. You would not be experiencing it if you did not desire it. You desire it for purposes of growth. Join with us, he says, to improve that essence at as fast a rate as you can possibly afford.

He says the peoples of your planet are in bondage to an idea that is false, an idea they have clung to for many generations, an idea that led them down a road of confusion. The simple truths we bring, as it is said in your holy works, will set you free. And then, through another instrument, the teaching turns to the machinery underneath the freedom.

What you receive, he says, you are deserving of through the efforts that you put forth.

And here is the title passage. You are the master of your existence. You are the co-creator of your universe. And that which you do must be done completely. Whatever energies come to you, they have come due to your projection of like energy. And as they flow throughout this universe, you must be open to allow the cycles of energies to continue flowing freely so that they may be shared by all.

Then the great practical line. The greatest step toward attaining what they seek, he says, is to bring into focus the discipline of one's own thoughts and actions. To think properly is to create properly. To think unrighteously is to create havoc within your universe. These laws you cannot transmute.

He does not leave it as philosophy. He applies it to the seeker's own growth. As you develop, he says, and as you become the instrument of greater knowledge, then greater numbers shall seek from you what you have attained. Make it clear to those who come that you are willing to share, but that they also must be willing to share with others and put forth efforts of their own to gain the knowledge they seek. And as you are aware, the effort of greatest importance is the dedication to the practice of daily meditation. Through your meditation you gain the unspoken words, the unwritten wisdoms, and the strength to persevere in addressing the tests which befall you.

The greater your desire and your effort to attain the highest knowledge, he warns, the greater the test. All things have a price, even that which you seek of a spiritual nature. That is not meant to frighten. It is meant to sober the bargain. If you are going to draw energy out of the universe, be ready to pour it back.

He is honest about what the path will bring socially, too. As you proceed, your position will bring upon you from time to time the scorn of your fellow man. If you are recognized as being the opposite of what someone feels they are, they will fear you through lack of understanding. Bless these individuals, he says. Seek not to retaliate.

The evening turns, in the questions, to the difficult things happening on the planet, and Hatonn makes a distinction I want to quote exactly. That which is necessary and that which is desirable are not necessarily the same. The physical plane is most effective when the catalyst of physical problems is worked out entirely within the individual consciousness. Growth would have been much more rapid, he says, if it had been chosen on the personal level in the first place. So the fastest path through every trouble is the inner work. Chosen early, chosen daily.

And the last instruction of the night is the simplest. We have long encouraged you to think of yourselves as shepherds and channels. And certainly this is the key, for service is always the key. We are instruments of the Creator and so are you.

The universe is in your hands. That is not a burden. It is the whole of the good news.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Body as Vehicle
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the body as vehicle.

It is a Wednesday evening in April, nineteen seventy-seven, and Hatonn begins with news of a campaign. Very shortly, he says, they will be contacting many more of the peoples on the surface than in the past, through various methods. They will create what he calls an advertisement of their presence. This will alert large numbers to their reality. The second phase, as he calls it, is beginning. But the heart of the evening is not the sky. It is the body.

Through another instrument, Hatonn speaks of the balance between the physical and the spiritual, and he reaches for an image from the orchard. Do not care too much for the physical body and its needs, he says. Yet beware the opposite. Do not care too little for your physical vehicle and its needs. You must look upon your physical vehicle as just that: it is a vehicle. It is functioning well for you and like a good fruit tree, it has grown, it has come into its youth, it has borne fruit. Perhaps it has grown a little gnarled, a little bent, and as the years go on it will become increasingly gnarled and it will have served its time. All of its fruit will have been given up and it will be cut down.

I love the tenderness in that. The body is not a temple to polish and not a prison to escape. It is a tree doing tree things. It grows, it bends, it gives its fruit, it is cut down. You may accept it, he says, as a good and faithful servant. You may take your body and be of service to others. Your body has hands with which to reach out to others. A mouth with which to smile. A mind to function well for you and to think well of others. It is not you, but it is no stranger to you. It is yours for a time. Keep this in balance.

Then the turn inward. In meditation, seek your permanent identity. Within you there is a perfect body, and that body is your spirit. It is not a body as you would think of a body. And yet it is the ultimate house of your soul. Within that final center is your link with all that there is.

And then the line that made me put down my pen. The joy, the state of joy that you left to come into the physical existence is very greatly needed among your peoples at this time. And how few there are that understand that joy is the natural state of existence for each of those who dwell upon your sphere. Joy is not a reward for getting life right. It is the condition you started in.

To touch this place within yourself is all-important at this time, he says, for if you can but make contact with your higher self, you can be of great comfort and of great service to many in the days to come. For in the days to come there will be many who are afraid, and many who have put off their voyage of self-discovery until the very last minute. One person who is sure of who he is and is radiating the joy of that knowledge and who can reach out with his light will be of infinite service.

The questions that night turn to the Bermuda Triangle, and Hatonn answers with an image I cannot let go. He says some vanishings are simply wrecks on the ocean floor, but in some cases beings were bent through a dimension that interacts with space and time to form interpenetrating spheres. It is as though, he says, you take a maypole with many colors of ribbon and plait the ribbon in an infinitely yet completely regular complexity so that many realities interpenetrate. Each of these realities has many planes. The only difference, my friends, is that there is no maypole, and this we cannot explain to you. I love that he admits the limit of the metaphor in the same breath he offers it.

Then a channel asks why he loses the contact after a short time, and Hatonn gives advice that is really about faith. Those who succeed in becoming a more extended channel, he says, are those willing to build up their confidence enough to continue sustaining an image beyond the first completed thought. Spiritual reading or meditation upon a spiritual thought, he says, stimulates your higher self and provides our contact with more fuel for our thoughts to mesh with. Then relax, and have a quiet confidence that your prayer to be of service will be answered.

He leaves them with this: our voice is millions strong, and our voice is heard by more and more of your peoples. We ask you to lift up your voice also, for each voice that speaks of love and light is a voice of great worth and of great beauty. Seek that love and light within yourself, and then share it.

The vehicle will be cut down in its season. The driver goes on.

Thank you for listening.

title: Faith, the Quiet Tool
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: faith, the quiet tool.

It is a Wednesday in August, nineteen seventy-seven, and Hatonn opens with a question that sounds almost like grief. Why is it, my friends, that your peoples are often so unaware of the friends that they have? We have come from other worlds, other dimensions, other times. Any of your helpers are parts of your own real self, separated from you only by your limited consciousness while within the physical illusion.

He catalogs the helpers. Others of your helpers have been your teachers through past experiences on the soul level. You have teachers within the physical illusion with you now, whose words you may read or hear, whose music you may hear, whose feelings you may come to understand. And yet, how many of your peoples think they are alone, and the world is a jungle, and they must get by the best they can? With this kind of philosophy, every day is difficult, every decision is hard, and all brothers and sisters are met with suspicion. Yet you are truly very rich in friends, most of them unseen, most of them available only through meditation.

And the greatest friend of all is closer than all of them. Your own higher self is your greatest friend. Your own higher self retains the memory of all that you have learned, in this experience and in that great sum of experience through which your true self has traveled.

Then Hatonn speaks of the timing of it all. At the beginning of your cycle, he says, your people had to begin with total lack of memory, in the darkness of total illusion, to rediscover independently and of free will all of the truths of love and brotherhood. And those truths have become more and more acceptable to individual souls as the cycle has progressed. That acceptable year, my friends, draws nigh and is upon you. That which you are expressing at this time may well be your final expression within this cycle. It is time, as this instrument would say, to get it right.

I love the school-year image he reaches for next. It is within the awareness of each of you to understand the pressures of the one who desires to pass the test at the end of the school year. There is a studying, a caring, a desiring that one's level of understanding may be acceptable. You know that feeling. The evening before the exam, the quiet room, the hope that you are ready. That is where the planet is.

And then the passage that gives this episode its title. Perhaps while you are within the physical illusion, he says, you can never be totally sure that it is truly an illusion. It is for reasons such as these that a word known as faith was conceived. Faith is the conscious tool of the intellect used to link your intellect, which is a rather weak tool, with your intuition and your deeper awarenesses, which are very strong tools, but about which you know nothing intellectually.

He refuses to let faith be the property of the fanatic. Many have said there can be no link between the intellect and the intuition, or the heart. But this is not so. All people are aware that it is possible to believe in love, in hope, in giving, in healing. All people, even the most materialistic, are aware of the legitimacy and the worth of these unseen powers.

So he gives them a practice, plain as bread. Ask yourself what things you have faith in. What things are of worth to you. And allow those things to expand as you bring them into your conscious awareness. First through meditation, and then through the actions given to others in joy. And allow yourself to trust that intuition that tells you our words are true, for that small amount of faith will express itself to you in reflection in many privately convincing ways, so that gradually you will not have to go on faith anymore. The evidence arrives after the trust, not before.

A questioner asks the oldest question of all. What was the beginning? How did it all start? And Hatonn answers with disarming honesty: this information is beyond our understanding. It is our intuitive feeling that the Father has no beginning and no ending. The Word, my friends, was love. There was one original vibration that expressed itself out of the infinite. Love then formed, step by step, all that the individual consciousnesses could begin to create. There is no beginning and there is no ending, but our universe is love.

He closes with a sentence the whole series could be built on. We have simply been a little farther up what you might call Jacob's ladder, he says. And we know that the journey is far more beautiful and more deserving of faith than any possible journey to any possible place in space, in time, or in imagination. The journey for truth is a journey for love, a journey for yourself, for you are truth and love.

You are not alone in the jungle. You have only to ask, in the quiet, and the friends you forgot you had will answer.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Naked Spirit
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the naked spirit.

It is a Monday in late September, nineteen seventy-seven, and Hatonn spends the whole evening on one image. Clothing. He asks the group to consider themselves as physical beings dressed in many layers of attire. Your hair is arranged to make an impression. Your clothing is armored around you. With each layer, with each arrangement, you are separating yourself from the outside world. These are your defenses on a physical level against those things you do not consider part of yourself. They are your definition of yourself. Perhaps this is not conscious. And perhaps your definition is very carefree. Yet it exists.

The thought of allowing your physical being to wander naked in the physical world is not one which seems very desirable, he says. And yet all beings are naked. All beings are unified even in their body, even on the level of physical illusion, by the total naturalness and validity of all the functions of their physical form. In nakedness, those differences which seem so obvious when one begins to limit oneself by clothing and by cultural differences fall away, and one can see that we are all one.

Then he goes deeper, to the levels that are unseen. On the mental, emotional, and spiritual levels, he says, you also have clothing and limitations. But inside your clothing is the most terrible limitation of all. Like tight bandages, your unseen self is wrapped in a terrible stricture consisting of those feelings which you have toward others concerning those things for which you have not forgiven them, and your feelings of guilt for things you have done to your brothers and sisters for which you do not feel forgiveness.

You will never be whole, he says. You will always be cripples as long as you carry these bandages about your spiritual body. And then, through the instrument, comes a story so plainspoken it is almost embarrassing to hear in a sacred setting. This instrument has within her memory, he says, a story of a man who went home with a beautiful woman, and as she undressed she took off her wig, her makeup, her padded brassiere, and her wooden leg, and suddenly she wasn't very beautiful anymore.

All those that you look at, he says, within this group and elsewhere, all these are cripples. They all have wooden legs. They all have wigs. On the level of your human personality, they are wrapped in the tight bandages of those things they have not forgiven and those things for which they feel they are not forgiven. And you, my friends, manifest within the illusion in an imperfect way.

I love how he refuses to let this become an excuse for despair. As you begin to go into the silence, he says, perhaps you have games you play in which you attempt to carry your clothed spirit into the silence. Do not do this. Picture yourself, mentally, taking guilt and discarding it as you would a piece of clothing. Taking resentment, fear, putting it aside, and walking as your shining naked self into the waters of cleanliness.

Listen for those signals which will come to you in the silence. You are a whole and complete person. Within you is perfection, wisdom, and all the attributes of love. Yes, you will come out of meditation. Yes, you will begin to wrap the bandages about yourself. But as you come again and again into meditation, strip yourself clean and allow that soothing feeling of wholeness to come into your awareness. You will begin to view your brothers and sisters with something that does approach true love, for you will see, behind whatever manifestations may occur, that whole and perfect being that dwells beneath.

We have always greeted you in love and in light, he says, for that is all that there is. We can greet you in nothing else. As you go into the silence, know that you are within that which is love. There is nowhere to go. You have no outer influence to seek. All that you desire is within.

The questions that night turn to dreams, and Hatonn is precise about them. Consciousness does not cease with sleep, he says, so what you recall from your dreams is a record your consciousness has been keeping. Your consciousness is also being taught by your teachers during sleep, and if you keep records of your dreams, you will begin to consciously remember at least part of these lessons. The soul does homework too.

He closes with a word about technology that puts the whole century in perspective. We come to you not to give you technology, he says, for you would not be able to handle technology, but love. For you badly need love. When you have love, you are joyful and full of energy, and that which has been given to you to do you will do. And the breakthroughs will come.

The wigs, the wooden legs, the bandages of what you have not forgiven. Tonight the instruction is simple. Take them off at the door of the silence. What walks in is shining already.

Thank you for listening.

title: Nothing but What I Seek
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: nothing but what I seek.

It is a Thursday in late October, nineteen seventy-seven, and Hatonn tells the group a story. We will call him John. John was a fine young man, intelligent and well-loved by all who knew him. He was successful in his work and achieved all that he wished very easily. But there was one thing he could not achieve. He could not achieve wisdom. He could not achieve peace of mind. He could not achieve joy. In other words, he was not free. He was not in a state of love.

So he did what successful men do. He collected money, great quantities of money, for he knew that with money one could buy much. And he went to one teacher after another attempting to buy wisdom. He found beautiful tracts of land and bought them, and gave them to his teachers. He spent many years attempting somehow to plug himself in to freedom. And all he found in the end were many, many words, many actions. But no peace, no joy, no freedom.

For he was always conscious of himself. He was always figuring. He was always self-aware. He could not get free and into a space in which he was so completely himself that he was a channel for joy. I love that phrase. A channel for joy. Not a possessor of joy. Not an achiever of joy. A channel. Something the joy flows through.

Finally John, no longer young, no longer handsome, no longer rich, for he had given all his riches away, despaired and went into the mountains. He did not take food and he did not take bedding. And it came to him suddenly that he might pray, as he had done often in the past. But this time it was different. He had nothing to give. And so he opened himself up, just a crack, and was almost blinded by the light that came through as he opened himself, no longer proud, no longer conscious of himself, but in total honesty saying, Father, I have nothing but what I seek.

Once he had opened himself, he became suddenly joyful. And after a timeless moment on his knees in the pine needles, in the gray of evening, he arose. And he reached and hugged the trees and he capered and danced and sang. And he was totally free. And he looked around and suddenly the world was whole and he had everything.

What this man John did with the rest of his life is not important, Hatonn says. He had a mission which he had brought with him into this experience. And he was no longer blocking. He had a simple mission and that mission was to be. And by that being to give light.

I want to sit with what the story is actually saying. John did everything right on the outside. Money, teachers, land, years of effort. None of it worked, because all of it was done by a self that was watching itself do it. The light got in only when there was nothing left to bargain with. The prayer that worked was not I have so much to offer. It was I have nothing but what I seek.

And Hatonn applies it directly. Each of you has his belongings, both physical and mental, both emotional and psychic. These things are the baggage of the illusion. We ask you to meditate. And in that meditation bring nothing but the simple perfection of yourself. Do not try to offer qualities and specifics. But in meditation open your heart to wisdom. Nothing less. Nothing more.

Imagine what you brought into this experience that you call your physical life, he says, and what you will bring when you leave. And know that that and only that is what you are attempting to open within this illusion to the light of the Father. Reality is very simple. And true freedom lies not in being somebody. Not in great action. Not in great movement. But in the state of your heart at any given moment.

The questions that evening include a practical one about channeling. The main barrier in almost each and every channel, he says, is the working of the conscious, intellectual mind. It is such an ingrained habit to analyze and judge what one says before one says it that blurting out in front of other people what you are not sure may be intelligent-sounding is completely foreign to your nature. When you are sending you cannot receive. It is very simple, but it is very difficult.

And then the closing, which is for anyone who has ever been afraid of the times they live in. It is written in your holy works, he says: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil. Do not fear evil, my friends. You may be hurt, those about you may be hurt. This is part of your experience, no more and no less. Seek only to fulfill that which you came to do. The shadow of death is as bad as it will get. The sun will shine. The skies will clear.

The man on the mountain had nothing left but his wanting. And the wanting was enough.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Footprint in the Jungle
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the footprint in the jungle.

It is the first Wednesday of November, nineteen seventy-seven, and the tape is hard to hear, which somehow suits the evening. Latwii spends the opening balancing the group's energies. Hatonn speaks of reality itself. And then Oxal, whose voice the group knows as a stronger and more pointed vibration, closes with an image of aborigines finding a single footprint in the jungle. But I am getting ahead of the story.

Hatonn begins where so many of these evenings begin, and I never tire of it. Let us talk to you about reality, my friends. It is important to talk about reality. We have talked with this group many times about love, many times about meditation. We wish to talk about reality. We are giving you the same truth but through a different filter. For it is this filter that you need at this time.

The questions turn first to the coming year, and Hatonn speaks of plans. They intend, he says, to broaden direct physical communication with selected groups and individuals in the next calendar year. Not through television, not through mass media, but in direct experience. They are pleased, he says, by the upsurge of interest in life forms throughout the universe, and by the greater studies being put into process by educators and scientists. What seemed fantasy ten years ago is becoming evident reality. It brings us closer, he says, to the day that we may work with you, hand in hand, in building what you would term the new world.

Then a practical question. What should a group meditation focus on? Against natural disasters, or against war? Hatonn answers without hedging. Focus your energies upon the prevention of escalation on the physical plane of warfare. He says the desire of some nations' leaders to substantiate and incur warfare is great, and that the people of Earth are given the first opportunity to prevent the destruction of their peoples and the environment. This would be your most beneficial exercise.

Someone asks how many people around the world are in contact with them. And Hatonn's answer is worth hearing in full, because it reframes the whole contact. We are in communication with the entire population of your planet, he says, but not to all of their knowledge. This form of communication that you experience here is only one form which we utilize. Look about you, he says. Look at the information brought forth through the media, through books, movies, radios, and televisions. We communicate through your scientists. We communicate through your doctors. We communicate through your lawmakers, although they are difficult to deal with. We communicate with all of your peoples.

Even the small strange things, he suggests, are part of the conversation. A questioner asks about a digital watch that jumps ahead a few hours. All experiences understood, Hatonn says, are beneficial to your spiritual growth. The phenomena you experience are only clues and indications given to you, through what you might term the grace of God, to continually remind you of the potential that lies within you. Your life is a barometer. Utilize your life's experiences as that barometer to determine not only the Creator's magnificence but your own.

Then the channel changes, and Oxal comes through, and the evening lifts into poetry. Hatonn's vibration, the group is told, is gentle and kind. Oxal is stronger and bears more of the stark power of love. And Oxal wants to talk about love not as a feeling but as a force. That which we call love, he says, is the force, shall we say, the mathematical equation behind our force. There is no law but love.

And then the image. You remind me, Oxal says, of what you would call your aborigines, stalking through virgin jungle. They know no other tribes. They are aware of no other beings. Then one day they come across one footprint. All the other footprints have washed away thousands of years ago. Suddenly they know that in some inconceivable past, some creature like them stood where they are standing.

The tape ends before he finishes the thought, which feels exactly right. We are the aborigines. The footprint is the evidence that we are not alone in the jungle of the universe. And the footprint, if you look closely, is shaped like love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Magnet of Desire
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the magnet of desire.

It is the second Wednesday of November, nineteen seventy-seven, and Hatonn speaks a sentence that could stand as the epigraph of the whole archive. Meditation brings us the key to the universe. It is the key to the inner being that you are. It is the key to the door of the Creator's house. It is the key to the door of all truth and understanding.

He is speaking of the silence the holy works talk about. The silence that you enter into, he says, is a silence which may at times seem to be vast and at other times to be very minute. And this is as it should be, for within the universe, all things are both infinitely small and infinitely large. For every expansion there is its opposite, contraction. For every thing there is balance. And balance can only be achieved by the experience of both sides of the scale.

Within your meditations you may find that balance. For it shall provide you with the understanding of your experiences, whether they be of the positive or negative nature. Without the understanding of that which you experience, the lessons have been overlooked. The lessons have passed you by.

He gives them a practice for the daylight hours too. As you go through the duties of life, concentrate if you must. But allow your sensitivities to remain in complete function, so that you may absorb the entire experience that you encounter, and call upon that understanding in what you call your future.

Then Hatonn says something startling about the address of this planet. Man upon planet Earth is residing upon a testing ground of spiritual awareness, in which he may grow and gain all the knowledge necessary to expand into the universe and spread the love and the light. You have not been chosen idly to abide upon this planet. You have progressed for thousands of years and earned the opportunity to reside here.

And then the line that stops the room. Earth, my friends, is the training ground for what your mythology has termed as gods. Be not discouraged if your society seems to be against you. It is your opportunity to grow. For what you experience is the manifestation of your own thought patterns. So is it not logical that in order to truly know your universe, you must first know yourself?

He speaks of the teachers, and of the most successful among them. Of these, the most successful was the one you would call the Christ. Follow the words that he spoke but above all live the life that he lived. And then, listen carefully: for indeed you are the risen Christ. For each and every one of you is the risen Christ the moment that you understand yourself.

When Laitos takes over, the teaching becomes a meditation in itself. Envision the energy of love all about you, he says. You breathe it in with every breath and absorb it through the skin of your chemical body. Love is all about you. You breathe it in and you cause this love to have direction. And this love spirals up your energy centers, and leaps up like flames from each of you and becomes a beautiful white energy, moving from one to another about the circle.

Feel the unity of that movement of the love in the circle. This unity of love, my friends, is reality.

And then Laitos gives them the image that names this episode. It is almost as though your peoples think of themselves as one of your toys, he says. A doll, perhaps, or a stuffed animal that a child would pick up and play with, and then put aside. And so you treat yourselves. You say, I will play the part of a wage earner, or a man about town, or an attractive woman, or a churchgoer. And you do not believe yourselves. You do not understand the game at all.

You see, underneath the sawdust and the tinsel of everyday life, there is something in you that is real. And that reality is very precious and will outlast the tinsel and the chemical body itself. The importance of the things that happen to you comes to you depending on how you desire that it comes to you. Just as you desire your experience to be, so it will show itself to you.

Most people, thinking of themselves as little more than a sawdust doll, do not desire deeply that they may discover the truth in their existence. Therefore they do not discover the truth in their existence. But if you truly desire that each moment may teach you its lessons, then you magnetize yourself. Sawdust does not attract metal. But if you have magnetized yourself, the metal comes to you through all of the useless sand, and it attaches itself firmly to your understanding.

Do not be afraid of that word, desire. What you desire is up to you. The intensity of your desire is very much up to you. Do not be afraid to really want to know the truth. Not just now, but all the time. You are in there, my friends. You are real. And you are here to learn the truth.

The sawdust does not attract the metal. The magnet does. Become the magnet.

Thank you for listening.

title: Do Not Fear the Wilderness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: do not fear the wilderness.

It is a Saturday in March, nineteen seventy-eight, and the first part of the tape is inaudible, so we join Hatonn mid-thought, already deep in the subject that matters most to him. He is speaking of what he calls the ultimate program for any individual, and it is so simple it sounds like nothing. To be aware of the original Thought. To be aware of love.

Whether the actions that are part of your karmic programming are taking place as planned or not, he says, the primary goal of expressing the original Thought is always achievable. Each individual is free the whole time. It is your thought, your choice, your understanding. Trust that understanding.

And then comes the teaching at the heart of the evening. If the individual continually grounds himself in the original Thought, he says, a condition is thereby prepared for an interface between love and proper action. Meditate. Do not doubt, distrust, or cease in your desire to be of service. As you meditate, allow that desire to keep the antennae of your senses on the finer planes. I love that image. The desire to serve is not just a feeling. It is an instrument. It keeps the antennae up.

Then he speaks to those who feel lost, and this is where the evening becomes unforgettable. You have felt that you are in the wilderness, he says. And yet it is precisely in the wilderness that you must be alone, for you have the challenge of being aware of that which is paradise totally within yourself, rather than dwelling in paradise and attempting to remember the wilderness. The experience of wilderness is extremely important to the growth of your soul.

He describes the soul's journey like this. As the immortal soul plunges into a cycle of experience such as you have committed yourself to in this density, the darkness of not remembering the Creator's Thought falls. All senses are stilled.
