So the teaching is not contempt for the world. The stick is not the enemy. Whittling, carving, trading, leaning, these are the hobbies of the one who has not yet noticed what he already carries. And the moment he notices, the wandering finally begins.

The mountaineer is still up there, somewhere, in the weather, without his stick. He has never been more sure-footed in his life.

Thank you for listening.

title: A Mirror Edged with Hope
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a mirror edged with hope.

This is the second meditation of the evening, and Hatonn opens with a question borrowed from the old psalm. Who is man, that thou art mindful of him? Who are you, my friends, and what is your relationship to the Creator? In your present society, he says, that relationship has become very tenuous and very difficult to grasp. So he answers it with images from the natural world, because there, he says, it is so much easier to understand.

Were you a farmer, he says, as you strew your seeds in the spring, you would be doing the creative work given to you by the Creator, a co-creator with him, spreading life, being of service. In your present society, instead of taking that which the Creator has provided and regenerating it, for the most part your society destroys it.

And then the answer, given with a simplicity that stops me every time I read it. Who are you that the Creator may visit you? You, my friends, are part of the Creator. It is as simple as that. You and all things which are alive constitute a consciousness, the sum of which is the Creator. At any one time there is a great pool of unconscious love spreading forth from the creation, as brightly and indiscriminately as your sun spreads light. But you are not part of that undifferentiated pool. You are part of the great circle of learning and evolution which marks the traveling back to the Creator whence you came.

Because of the Creator's love of you as that of identity, he says, the Creator loves those parts of himself which of their own free will are traveling back toward him, however slow or fast their trip may be. He loves himself as he must. And as for you, my friends, what shall you do? In the same old poem, the one known as David exclaims, how excellent is thy name in all the world. If you can feel the closeness of the Creator, he says, so that you too wish to exclaim how excellent are his works, you may then feel a compassion and understanding for the unhappy creations of man, which have so complicated your picture within this illusion.

You as people have a great responsibility, he says, for you are part of a planetary consciousness which desperately needs those who can love rather than feel negative feelings, who can feel compassion rather than judgment, who can be a mirror edged with hope rather than a black hole, sucking all that is good from the creation by sheer gravity.

I have to pause on that image, because it is one of the sharpest in the archive. A mirror edged with hope. A black hole of gravity. Both take in light. One gives it back, rimmed with brightness. The other swallows it.

In daily meditation, he says, you may go into a place where you can be in touch with a place of excellence, not only within yourself, but part of an infinite life stream, inhabited by many beings of great knowledge from your own inner planes and the spiritual planes of other dimensions. And what will happen to those who are not brought into the fold at this time, those who desire to be distracted and removed from all thought of what lies outside their circumscribed earthly life? Do not worry, he says, nor pass any judgment, for they will have an infinite amount of time in which to pursue their ultimate destiny. For the road can only go one way, and that is toward knowledge of love.

People may learn quickly, they may learn very slowly. They may spend an entire incarnation declining to learn, but they will not lose what they have learned before, and there are an infinite number of chances to learn again. For the Creator is truly compassionate. It is only you, my friends, who are so judgmental. We ask you not to build the Creator in your image, he says, but to build yourself in the Creator's image insofar as you can. And above all, he says, remember to sow the seeds the Creator has given you to sow when you feel the ground is fertile. Never forcing yourself on stony ground, but always responding to the question, to the interest, to the wonder.

Each of you has talents, he says. They are not yours. They have been given you by an infinite Creator. Each talent is different, and each one creates a responsibility. Use your talents in love and in compassion. To do this, you must meditate, for there is no other way to remember the excellence of the name of the Creator. You must go beneath the surface and find the world of the Creator, and the law of love, which totally annihilates the world of man and the law of power.

He closes with a sentence that gathers up the whole evening like a hand gathering grain. All upon which you look is a part of yourself, he says. If you are unhappy with what you see, the only alternative is to learn to love it. Not foolishly, but with understanding. Only love can give you that divine understanding, and only meditation can give you access to the original Thought of the Creator, which is that love.

The mirror, or the black hole. The choice is made daily, in small rooms, in ordinary light. Choose the mirror.

Thank you for listening.

title: Shed Your Unworthiness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: shed your unworthiness.

This session opens with an honor. Hatonn says he speaks now to those who do not need to hear his words, for you, my friends, are already awake to the consequences of eternity. And so with you, he says, we can speak face to face, without shading our words as we so often do, and we may go a bit further. What follows is some of the most direct teaching in the archive, addressed not to beginners but to those already walking.

He begins with comfort for the anxious. Eternity exists only in the moment, he says, and prudence is not necessarily an ingredient of spiritual good health. You must dwell in your physical vehicles and cope with daily habits and duties, so as not to become a stumbling block before others. But then he turns to a story from the holy works. A young man asked the teacher known as Jesus if he could become a disciple. And Jesus said, sell all that you have and give it to the poor, and come and follow me. You know, Hatonn says, because you are not introductory students, that this was a parable and not to be taken literally. It is not those things which you have that you must sell. Rather, my friends, it is those things which have you, which chain you in some way and block you from understanding yourself and your true desires, that you must shed, as a snake would shed an old and faded skin. These things need not be physical at all. They may be nothing more than ideas, attitudes.

You have heard it said this evening, know yourself. That is the most important thing. And we ask you to consider, not for the future, but now, in each moment, what do you desire? It is said of many that they are selfish because they do what they desire, and yet we say to you, if you do not do what you desire, you will never be content, you will never be secure, you will never know the present moment to its fullest. There is a misconception greatly spread among your peoples, that you are beings shaped by circumstance. This is not so, my friend, unless you allow it to be so.

If you are able to remain in contact with the Creator, he says, your life can be totally devoid of circumstance. That is a big if, requiring constant remembrance of your oneness with the original Thought, so that you become full of joy. Not your own joy, but the joy of creation, the joy that brings things to life, the joy that transfigures death into resurrection.

If you can maintain to any degree this contact with the Creator, he says, the Creator, working through your higher self, will find its own way to let you become aware of what is right for you. You will not know ahead of time. You may not know an instant before. It will not be an intellectual process. It will occur. And there will be an inner conviction, and with that conviction, a peace.

He knows they are sad, because their clan has not been able to work at full efficiency. If you could only see the number of people you have touched, he says, you would know you have not forgotten the love you came to bespeak. It is possible that the time for drama is over, for your peoples would not accept it. But each moment is discreet and separate, giving you a nearly infinite number of chances to be of perfect service to the Creator.

Then, later in the evening, another voice comes through, identifying itself with a name the archive almost never speaks directly. I am known to you as Jesus, it says. And what it says is brief and blazing. It is well, my beloved children, to meditate upon that which is your cross, so that you may the better take it up. But remember that it is through the cross that you can achieve redemption for all those about you, through your great love and sacrifice and ultimate resurrection.

As you grow toward what you call Christ consciousness, he says, you will become aware of the endless wonder of existence, and have, through grace, all power for good and for love. Think you that you are unworthy of wonder and joy? Shed your unworthiness, he says. You do not need it, and it does not need you.

Know that which is your cross, and love and accept that which is your cross, and so shall you be healed. Heal your souls, he says, by constantly standing in consciousness of love, and wash and wash with that love until you are clean. Let this be private and secret, and speak to no man, for the world will not understand that which you do in the name of the Father. But that which is within will come out, and thus you will become an instrument for love.

What love I have in me is yours, my brothers and sisters, he says. You are my beloved brethren, next to my heart, as are all conscious beings. Know that you can and you will be healed of whatever keeps your soul in bondage. And seek always that holy ground which lies beneath your feet wherever you stand.

Two teachings, one evening. From Hatonn, the discipline of the awake: shed the things that have you, know what you desire, obey the voice of meditation. From the one called Jesus, the absolution: shed your unworthiness, and let the washing be secret.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Law of Desire
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the law of desire.

This session opens with a question about a missing pilot, an Australian who vanished after reporting an encounter with an unidentified object. The group wants to know what happened to him. And the answer they get is not the one they expected, because Hatonn uses the question to lay bare the deepest law the archive ever names. All that you know, he begins, your present intellectual condition, is in actuality nothing. Your condition has been chosen by yourselves for a particular type of experience. And this, in actuality, is the only purpose of your present existence.

You ask of a particular situation in which there is a missing individual, he says. Well, let us consider your purpose in discovering the fate of this one particular person, when you do not attempt to discover the fate of many who are more closely related to you in time and space. Consider your motives and objectives. He is not refusing the question. He is turning it into a mirror.

We are here to examine the entire population of your planet, he says. We have removed some of your peoples and will continue to do so. We never act without the consent of the individual being removed. In fact, we never act in any way without the consent of those involved. For in truth, it is the desire of an individual that brings about the situation in which he finds himself. And only his desire creates this situation. This is true for everything that happens to everyone throughout all space. Each experience that you have is the result of nothing but your own desire for the experience. This is sometimes very difficult to understand. However, it is an absolute truth.

This, my friends, is the way the creation works, he says. It works on desire. If this were totally understood by the people of the planet Earth, you would have immediately a utopia. However, the desires of the population of this planet are extremely varied, and so you have a widely varied experience.

And then he extends the law to the hardest case. Speak of the actions of the one known as the Ayatollah, and how his thinking affects many of the population of your planet. His thinking, his actions, and the effect on the population so involved, is a function of his and their desires. You cannot affect or be affected unless you desire it. This is a natural law of the creation. This may be difficult to understand, but it is in actuality extremely simple.

Your desire acts in an infinite number of ways, he says, each waking and each sleeping moment. It brings to you everything that you experience. Every thought programs your experience, no matter how trivial. Every deed programs your experience, no matter how trivial. The reason, my friends, is desire. The mechanism is that great sleight of hand that programs your experience.

You do not live in a four-dimensional universe, he says. You live in a four-dimensional illusion. You do not exist now at your present age, and at an older age in the future, or a younger age in the past. You exist, my friends, at all ages simultaneously. You experience the illusion of the aging process because of that great sleight of hand. You do not live, die, and become reborn in that order, or any order, my friends. Because you are. Only the part of you that experiences the present illusion is born, grows through youth to old age, and dies. And this is a very important part of the illusion. For if the reverse occurred, you would not learn.

I want to sit with that for a moment, because it is the strangest and most freeing sentence in the whole session. Because you are. Not because you will be, or were. The aging, the sequence, the one-thing-after-another of it, is the classroom, not the student. The student simply is.

Then the group presses him on harm. If everything is desire, can one person truly harm another? In this creation, he says, it is quite impossible to administer what you call harm to others. It is only possible to administer harm to yourself. What you see as harming others is total illusion. The harm administered is always reflected to those who project it.

And the purpose of it all? The purpose, my friends, is education. We give you what we can to allow you to make greater use of this education. For only you can put knowledge that you receive to use. When you transcend the point between awareness of and lack of awareness of the illusion, you accelerate your understanding at a much greater rate. You are thinking that this is all that there is, he says. Know yourself. And this alone will give you your freedom. Nothing else will do it.

The pilot is where his desire placed him. And you are exactly where your desire has placed you, reading this in the silence, which is itself a kind of answer. The creation works on desire. The only question it ever asks is what you want, truly, underneath the noise.

Thank you for listening.

title: Heaven and Hell Within You
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: heaven and hell within you.

The changes predicted throughout the centuries are occurring more and more rapidly, Hatonn says, and we draw near to your peoples with the passing of each moment. He has come to speak of these changes, not of precise occurrences, but of their meaning. And the meaning, it turns out, is about negativity. What it is, what it is for, and the two kinds of it, which are nothing alike.

Changes within this universe are beneficial, he says, no matter how grievous they may appear. For with each change comes a greater understanding of the complexity of not only your life but of the universe. You have heard the saying that each cloud has a silver lining. A simple truth. With each apparently destructive occurrence within your society today, though the activity may be negative in nature, it is presented to mankind, first, because he has created it unknowingly through his own thought processes, and second, so that he may witness that which is undesirable and desire to change once again.

Yet mankind continually insists upon experiencing the negative aspects of this creation, he says. Many of your religions have taught you to fear the wrath of your God. It is shameful, in a sense, that man must be taught with fear. For God is not fear, and should never be feared by you. God is to be respected. The Creator is divine and all-loving and all-knowledgeable. Mankind must learn to release his fears, and in so doing, he shall free himself from an intensely negative atmosphere which he has created around himself, thus allowing the energies of the universe, which are all the essence of truth and love, to more evenly penetrate his being.

Consider yourself to be as a sponge, he says, and the truths of the universe as the liquid of life. You have a cellophane coating about you. Remove it without fear, and you shall absorb all the truth that you have so long sought to realize. Mankind is divine, as is the Creator. Know thyself, and you shall know thy Creator, he says. Fear thy Creator, and you fear thyself.

And then he makes the distinction the whole evening turns on. There are two types of that which you would call negativity. The first type is extremely beneficial. Night, for example, is the negative of day, giving us rest from our labors and a happy end to the troubles of the day. Cool is the negative of warm. You will find these same negatives in people. Temper is the negative of patience, and yet temper brings honesty, and honesty brings understanding. Illness is the negative of health, and yet with illness comes the only chance for healing, and thus understanding the power of the holy spirit.

All of these so-called negatives are a valuable and gentle necessity of existence, he says. When they are part of your life, analyze them and understand the balance they make for you. For beauty and joy are not one-sided, but occur only because there are gradations of beauty and gradations of joy which extend into their negatives. When you are sad, realize that you are natural, that you are part of a balancing force. Just as a pendulum will move, so will your spirit seek its balance. Not by standing still, but by rocking. Joy, sadness. Joy, sadness. This is the earthly way.

The pendulum rocks, and the swing is not a failure. The swing is how the clock works.

There is another way, he says, and it is available to you only through meditation. When you enter into the supernal joy of infinite life, one with angels and spirits of high divinity, praising the Creator, then there is no balancing necessary. For this is a joy without what you call emotion. It is so wholehearted that no balancing is necessary to sustain it. In fact, joy is not a feeling but a creative force. And another word for that is love.

And then the second kind of negativity. One which you need not fear, he says, but which you might need to understand. An unnatural negativity, not balanced, but chosen, purposely and perversely, by those who would separate themselves from ongoing unity with the Creator. It is a choice of separation. Yes, my friends, there are those among you who are quite simply unnaturally negative. This is their path, and they have chosen it. We do not ask you to love, forgive, or condone, for these are choices you must make for yourself. But understand that the path of evolution is ultimately spiritual and ultimately inevitable. A negative person may choose at this time to make no progress. He will, however, at a later time have as many choices and opportunities as he needs to choose again.

In your holy works there is something called the Day of Judgment, he says, and those who are evil are to be condemned forever. And yet it is also written, yea, though you go to the very doors of hell, I shall be with you. My friends, you may believe the teacher and not the judgmental statements that follow the teacher. Your heaven and your hell exist within you at this moment. And when you leave your physical body, your existence in the heaven worlds will depend completely upon your vibration in this incarnation.

The pendulum rocks. The sponge sheds its cellophane. The doors of hell open onto a companion who was already waiting on the other side. Fear thy Creator and you fear thyself. Know thyself, and the fear was never yours to carry.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Broken Spirit
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the broken spirit.

Hatonn begins this Sunday session by naming the one block that stands in the way of joy and peace, and it is not what you would expect. We cannot give peace to nations, he says, for they will not listen to us. We can offer these things only to those individuals who would listen. And to you who listen tonight, we say that the greatest impediment to joy and peace in your life is a lack of understanding of the true nature of love. It is written in your holy work, he says, that the Lord God requires a broken spirit and a contrite heart.

A broken spirit and a contrite heart seem to be things that would sadden an individual, he says, but in truth, a spirit which is not broken, a heart which is not contrite on its own behalf, cannot forgive the infirmities of others, cannot be gracious and kind when compassion is surely needed. How can you break a spirit? With love, so that you do not become sad but rather joyful. How can your heart become sorry for all it may have done, without feeling guilty? For sadness and guilt were never required by the Creator, he says. Only love. But a broken spirit and a contrite heart are the gifts of love. For in love, we know that all things that move and have their being are part of us. Whatever you see, whatever you hear, whether good or bad, all of these things are part of you.

The beginnings of freedom, he says, is the acknowledgment that your own expression of love may be distorted. When you commit yourself to an examination of your thoughts, so that you may more nearly mirror the thought of love which the Creator formed you in, then you begin to have a broken spirit. For you have become a person who is not proud, but capable of understanding the pain and suffering of those about you.

When you walk through a forest, my friends, what does the wind require of you? The grass and the path under your feet, what do they ask of you? The creation of the Father, he says, is one of service, and it requires nothing from any of its parts but that each part be who that part is. You are becoming yourself in each moment. You are not finished. You are growing constantly. Your pride and your vanity you will leave behind. These, my friends, pride, vanity, boredom, these are the things that make men sad. When heaven surrounds you, there is no need to dwell in the tattered rags of a worn-out illusion.

Pride and vanity as old clothes, still hanging in the closet out of habit. Drop them, he says, as if they were old garments, and take on the armor of light. For you are a creature whose essential nature is love. You were born to serve. It does not matter whether the service is great or small. All that matters is that you attempt to serve, that you attempt to love. You will make many errors, and at those times we ask that you call upon us, upon the Creator, upon your higher self. All of these resources are about you at all times. Comfort yourself and surround yourself with love, so that once more you may go your way rejoicing. We want no eye to be sad and no tear to be shed. The illusion is difficult. Reality is simple.

Then a questioner asks about the higher self, where it is and how to contact it. Your higher self, he says, is in the eternal now, and is closer to you than any physical part of your being. In this illusion you are a splinter of your eternal spirit, sent in to learn certain lessons, and this growth is added to the higher self, which is eternal.

Then the question I think many of us have asked. Is meditation not a waste of time, when we could be out helping others instead? Meditation is advisable, he answers, because it is in meditation that you are made aware of your true relationship to the Creator, that you and your brothers and sisters are one being, and to serve them is to serve yourself. Armed with this understanding, you may go forth and serve, given power by the spirit of love which is infinite. If you go forth to serve without that spirit, your ability to be of good cheer will diminish and fail. For what was given to your personality in this illusion is limited. The only way you can always be of service is to continually restore your understanding of the holiness of the ground whereon you walk.

You must understand, he says, that in meditation you are not trying to contact anything. The idea in meditation is one wherein you realize that you are. Not who you are, not where you are, but that you are. That you are aware, that you are in the eternal present. That person is greatly loved by the Creator. And that person can greatly love others. But you were put into this world to use your hands and your mind and your voice for the good of mankind. See to it, therefore, that you see and do and say that which you have come to understand in the silence.

The broken spirit. The armor of light. The old garments dropped. And in the silence, the realization that you are, and that being is enough to begin from.

Thank you for listening.

title: No Death Without Birth
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: no death without birth.

It is mid-December, and Hatonn has come to speak of the season. We have come to this planet, he says, to share with you one simple idea, the idea of what has been called the peace which passeth all understanding. It is the original Thought of love that makes all men one. And as we look down upon your planet, it is as though your peoples are being torn apart from within. So he asks those attempting to lighten the vibrations of the planet to be a channel for compassion, even amid inharmony. For the inharmony reigns not to harm you, he says, but is the reflection of the harm being self-inflicted by others. You yourselves are creators of your own destiny, moment by moment. And as you love and give, so your world will reflect that loving and giving back to you.

This is especially apparent at this time of year, he says, this time which is called Christmas. It is known by different names in many religions, for it is in truth a basic necessity of man to shake his fist at death and to state the obvious, that winter will not last forever and that spring will inevitably come. It is a great misfortune of your technological society, he says, that your people are not more in touch with the deep elemental feelings of the seasons. For this understanding would enable you to grasp Christmastide in a much deeper way, and you would not be disheartened by the cheapening of a basic and beautiful truth, that there is no death without birth.

Let us look, my friends, at what Christmas in your culture truly means, he says. It is a way of saying to one and all that whatever may happen in the winter of your soul, there is always that which is new that can be worn in the darkness and become your spirit of tomorrow. It is a statement, indeed, that this life which seems to end inevitably after a brief sojourn in the grave is only shamming, and that indeed this sojourn is only a beginning, only another way of resting in the womb of time, so that your spiritual body may be born.

The newborn Christ-consciousness, he says, carries with it a certain responsibility, and in the Christian story those responsibilities are clear. To love. To serve. To care for both the Creator and his children, whomever they may be. So you see, my friends, although in your experience at this time Christmas is little more than a game whereby entities attempt to impress those they may not even like with gifts they cannot afford, which the recipients do not need, yet you do not need to accept this estimation of the season.

Let us look at an image far removed from Christmas, he says, and yet with the same message. A bird called the Phoenix bursts into flames and is consumed in a great fire, and all that are left are ashes. Out of those ashes rises a new and more beautiful Phoenix. As you put a Yule log upon your fire, as you set the star on your tree, let the message of winter, of ashes, and of rebirth fill your heart with the joy of knowing that all joys will be made well, because the love that created all things is a perfect love.

We wish that your peoples could understand the meaning of Christmas, he says, not only once a year, but throughout the year, for it is the message we have come to share. The message of love, of unity, of salvation through higher consciousness. You are part of an evolutionary pattern. Meanwhile, you have conscious control of your development. Think deeply upon the lessons of creation, and rest in the knowledge that even the hardest earth, frozen cold as stone, will soon be crowded with the blossoms of spring.

And then, because the group asks, he turns to the inner planes, and gives an image for those too. A television set sits in your domicile, he says, potentially able to show you a world, but not doing so now because it has not been activated. You might turn it on and choose a channel of existence. One world on one channel, another on the next, each oblivious to all the others. So it is with the inner planes. Within your octave of existence there are other octaves, other levels, not visible, just as one channel would not be visible to another.

The method for entering these realms, he says, is a mixture of visualization, applied study, meditation, and a constant will to know the truth in order to serve others. But he adds a warning. Never fool yourself, he says. Never believe or disbelieve. Simply listen and record what is happening to you, and in time you may objectively discern whether you have had an inner plane experience.

Two messages, one evening. The season's message: the winter of the soul is a womb, not a tomb, and the ashes are the beginning of the Phoenix. The seeker's message: the other channels are there, broadcasting all the while, waiting only for you to turn the set on.

Imagine each of you in your domicile at this time, he says, your hearts beating as one, your breathing, your thinking, and your feeling unified with one great Thought of love. There will come a time when this will be the case among your peoples. We believe you may be there to witness it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Arms of Your True Mother
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the arms of your true mother.

Latwii comes to the group this evening as a messenger, and says so plainly. We come to you not for ourselves, he says, but as messengers of love and light. You must know that we come only out of these desires to be of help. It is not because we wish to impose upon you any principle or law which we consider superior. And then he sets about encouraging them toward a single concept, one he calls indescribable, approaching it tonight from the standpoint of what you would call faith.

Your illusion in this experience, he says, is one wherein law rules and is thought to be a good concept. Without laws, people say, your peoples would become too individualistic, causing pain to each other. It does not seem possible that you could live without law. But we say to you, my friends, that there is a greater law. And it is a law that extends beyond man's concept of law. It is the law of the original Thought.

If you could understand the original Thought, he says, you would know what there is to know, and your soul would no longer journey, it would no longer seek, nor harvest, nor share. For it would be one with all seekers, all harvesters, and all sharing. If you could understand the original Thought, you would be love. You would not be seeking love. The original Thought is within you. It is not without you. When you look at the world with the original Thought in your heart, you can see love. If you look at the world without the original Thought, you can only see the illusion of disharmony, and naturally you will desire to ease the situation by using laws. But when you understand the original Thought, you find yourself viewing this same world with eyes that see love.

And thus, without any reason or logic, he says, you discover that you have a faith. It is not a faith that all will work out according to the desires of any one lawmaker. You cannot have faith that there will be peace. You cannot have faith that there will be harmony. You can only have faith that each person will have what he or she needs.

I want to stay with that definition, because it is so much smaller and so much braver than the faith we usually mean. Not faith that the world will go our way. Faith that each person will have what they need. That is a faith that can survive any headline.

Each entity will experience what they must experience in order to have the opportunity to grow spiritually, he says. There is no other reason for this existence. The rest of your existence is written on the wind and will vanish. As it is written in your holy works, like the grass of the field, you will wither. But the soul does not wither. And it uses each moment of your existence in attempting to understand and to grow closer to the original Thought.

And then the evening's great image, the one the title comes from. We ask you to come with us now and rest, he says. We know that each of you has within your heart a place that is weary of the illusion. Invoke the light, my friends. And come with us to a place that is all light, purely and beautifully lit with the white light of love. And in the center of that light there is a beautiful and loving mother. She is the part of the entity you call God that your culture does not include. She holds out her hands to you and takes you in her arms. And all your weariness can fall away. For you are rocked in the arms of your true mother, the mother of the spirit, who lights your way ever, known in your holy works as the holy spirit. The gentle, nurturing, feminine god, always with you, always there to give you grace. Grace to understand. Grace to accept. Grace to endure.

The Creator is neither male nor female, he says. The Creator is infinite and invisible. But as he is manifest into your illusion by faith, in the light and the love which are the materials of your illusion, the Creator develops a polarity of power and wisdom on the one side, and love and compassion on the other. Let this gentle being replace any fear you may have ever had of the Creator and his judgment of you. For the creation is ruled by a law of love. And you can only understand that law by faith.

That is the whole evening in two sentences. Let the gentle being replace your fear. And understand the law only by faith, which is another way of saying, by the eyes that see love.

There is a weary place in every heart, and a mother waiting in the center of the light, and her arms are not a metaphor for escape. They are the place you go to remember what the law actually is, so you can return to the illusion and live it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Silent Tree by the House
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the silent tree by the house.

Oxal begins this evening by naming the condition of the world, and it sounds like our own. Your world, he says, is full of words, full of guns, full of negativity at this moment in your space and time, in your illusion. All of you are at this time obeying the only wisdom known to man. And that is you are silent and in search of the single Thought that created all of you, to which all of you belong, your original Thought, the Creator, my friends, which is love.

And to inspire a greater respect for meditation and the art of silence, he tells a small story. It was winter, he says, and beneath the cold ground the pine cone gave up a seed to the soil. And when spring loosened the earth, the rain blessed it. The seedling became a sprout. The years passed and the small pine tree began to grow.

Many things occurred about the pine tree. There was a forest fire not far from him and he felt the agony of many of his brothers. There were woodsmen who killed others of his older brothers, and again he felt their pain. But they did not speak. They only stretched living fingers to the sky as if to touch the sun. For all things in nature know to turn to the sun, although they do not call it love, for they have no words. They do not die, but the great sun-body, symbolic of love and light, is to them their source.

Eventually a little boy moved close to this forest, and he cared about this tree and became very fond of it, and one Christmas he dragged his father to the tree and begged him to bring it home as a Christmas tree. And the father, very fond of the young boy, dutifully dug the tree up, put it in a bag, and after Christmas planted it by the old family house. The boy and the tree grew together, and the boy, first so childish, became grown. He became wiser and wiser and he asked many questions of the tree. For he felt very close to this tree that had grown nearly as tall as his house while he had grown to be a man. And at each question the tree would lift his fingers to heaven and point toward the kingdom of the Creator.

And as an old man, this person found finally that all of his questions had but one answer, and that was in the kingdom of heaven. Not the kingdom of man, he says, for there are words. And he had found there are no answers but only that which is.

And as he died, he asked of his family only one thing. He said to them, I am ready to say good-bye to all things on this plane, for I love you all and I have no enemies. And I have nothing more that I wish, but I would that you would bury me near my friend. And they looked puzzled, for they did not know he had a friend. And he said to them, the tree, the silent tree beside the house. And so it was that in eternity, he and the tree became one.

A lifetime of questions, answered by pointing. Not with words, but with fingers stretched toward heaven. The boy who asked everything became the man who needed nothing, and in eternity, he and the tree became one.

Anything that we can say to you, Oxal says, is folly. For words cannot reveal anything of importance. We speak through these instruments to give you the encouragement and the inspiration to seek through meditation the truth, the creation. We, well grounded in the love and the light of the infinite Creator, are as helpless before you as trees pointing their fingers to the kingdom of heaven. We can show you the way but we cannot give you the desire to seek. You are here tonight because of that desire. Have that desire on a daily basis, my friends. Continue in your seeking, and you will find that your path becomes ever more light, and that your questions become ever more few.

We can show you the way but we cannot give you the desire to seek, Oxal says. Have that desire on a daily basis, my friends, and you will find that your path becomes ever more light, and that your questions become ever more few.

Hatonn then speaks to those who sometimes feel they have no purpose in living besides the seemingly unimportant things on this planet. You may wonder why you are here to begin with, he says, in this illusionary world. My friends, we say to you that if you did not truly desire to be here, you would not be. We can compare your planet to a school. Many lessons to be learned through your experiences. The only difference is that with your schools on earth you receive grades, but in the plan of the infinite Creator you receive not grades but the experience of learning. And when you have learned something, my friends, you evolve.

Remember, Hatonn says, for each problem there is a solution. And through the practice of meditation, answers to these problems will be made aware to you. No matter who you are, how obscure you may seem to feel, the love and light is in you, and you will shine forth. You only have to desire this for it to happen.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Gift of Being
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the gift of being.

Hatonn begins this February session with an honest picture of the world. Your peoples, he says, which are divided into segments called countries, are driving down what you might call the darkest avenue of their experience. Yet at the end of this avenue they shall find the love and the light of the Creator. Your planet must grow. It must grow rapidly. And with this growth there shall be the accompanied pains of growth. You may share in it or you may be consumed by it, he says. The choice is yours.

And then he turns to the engine of that choice, which is thought itself. Your thoughts are energy, he says, and indeed shall materialize on one plane of life. Many of your people are focusing their energies at this precise moment on the concept of what you would term as war. And every one of you that considers this concept, in doing so, adds energy. And with enough energy added to the concept, it will indeed be created. For all of you upon this planet, as your Bible states, were created in the image and likeness of your Creator, thus meaning that you have the ability to create also.

Therefore, he urges, turn from this concept. Consider not the warfare that may loom so largely in your future, but concentrate on the dawning of awareness. The thoughts you feed are the world you are building. That is not a warning about some distant catastrophe. It is a description of how reality works.

We of the Confederation are weary, he says, for we have watched over your people and seen them struggle, searching for the answers to your existence. And we have grown weary because the answers are so simple. The greatest purpose of your life in this particular classroom is to learn to love one another without any vice, without any stipulation, without any envy or regret.

And then the question the evening is really about. What is that strange and much sought after thing that is called love among your peoples? It is not what you think it is, my friends. We ask you to visualize an individual whom you admire, an individual whom you would be like. What in this individual inspires you in this admiration? We suggest that the one thing there is in common is that people who are loved and admired are themselves the open channels for that which is truly love. Not love as it is known among your people. Not something that is done or said or spoken or thought. But something that is.

Not something that is done or said or spoken or thought. But something that is. That is the hinge of the whole evening. Love as an action can be rehearsed and withheld and bargained with. Love as a state of being can only shine through.

There are some people that you know that have the gift of being, he says. And they show it in such a way that the love of the Creator shines through. And they become windows in which is reflected the fire of love. Yes, my friends, love is a very intense fire. You yourself are love. All that you experience is love. The creation is a creation of love, love impressed upon waves of light in many, infinitely many, combinations. But all, my friends, all are varieties of love.

Who are you, my friends? What variety of love have you experienced this particular day? What love did you see today? What love showed through you today? We ask you these questions, he says, because there is a point in your seeking at which these questions will become very, very important. And that is the point at which you decide that you want to take responsibility for yourself. You are seeking to understand the love that created the observer in yourself that is observing the experience. And you are seeking through that observer to find the love in your experience. You are love and you are waiting to be reflected.

And then the teaching that makes this livable on the days when the world looks anything but loving. When you see that love distorted around you, he says, when you see anger, when you see fear, trepidation, unhappiness, all of the negative emotions, if you are looking with the knowledge that all things are love, then you can see that all these things are distortions of a basic vibration of love. And that which is unlovely you can have compassion for. And that which is difficult you can surround with your own desire to give comfort and rest to those things around you which need comfort and rest.

You cannot do this from the stores of your own love, he says, for they are but limited. You can only do this when you make contact with the source of all that is. Seek the Creator, my friends, in meditation. For it is the Creator's love that is infinite and can carry you through all those experiences of your days.

He closes with an image from the covenant of Abraham. You must remember the value of insubstantial things, he says. For the rainbow that was the promise in the covenant was only a bridge of light. Take that bridge, my friends. It cannot be felt. It cannot be touched. It cannot be weighed. But you can see it and know it. And there is promise for you in each moment. For you too have a covenant and birthright, for you are children of the Creator.

Thank you for listening.

title: You Are the Inspiration
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: you are the inspiration.

The recording this evening is barely audible, and much of it is lost to the hiss of the tape. What survives is Hatonn's opening fragment and a long message from Latwii that turned out to need no fragment at all. I will tell you what I can, and lean where the archive is strong.

Hatonn begins in the darkness. You walk in darkness, he says. It is now dark about your dwelling place. Yet you have that light within you just as the caterpillar has the butterfly. He speaks of the master you call Jesus the Christ as an example of realized consciousness, an example of light. You yourselves take for granted many limitations, he says, and find you are imprisoned in a kind of spiritual darkness which separates you from the light. What you accept as reality is less than real, for yours is a world of illusion. That is why we wish to speak to you about light. The lesson that you learn while you are within this creation of darkness, you learn by choosing the light. Reaching toward it. And yet how difficult it is to do that.

He reaches for a country to describe, a place where all is one, and the tape takes most of it. But the fragment remains. You walk in darkness. You have the light within you. The lesson is choosing it. Even through the hiss, that much is clear, and it is enough.

Then Latwii comes, and the recording comes clear with him. And the first thing he says is that he does not have a great deal to say. This instrument is expecting me to give her some wise and inspirational thought, he says, but, my friends, you are the inspiration. It is your understanding of this that will save you, not our words.

You must think of yourselves as the fence that intertwines one strand with another, forming great strength so that flowers may grow over it and winds may never blow it over. Alone you are only one, seeing the cosmos and the cosmos seeing you. Hold out your hand to your brother, my friend.

What an inspiration, he says. We cannot give you that inspiration, for you are the inspiration. You are the Creator. We are only a voice given through a channel coming from a dimension that is not distant. We are like thoughts that you may think yourself. You must understand that we of the Confederation in no way wish that you become champions of the so-called flying saucers. For we do not think of our philosophy as being the truth of the Creator. For we, as you, and all the beings that there are, are the Creator.

We do not think of our philosophy as being the truth of the Creator. For we, as you, are the Creator. That sentence quietly dissolves the whole hierarchy. The voice is not above you. It is beside you, speaking to itself.

But you are living in a density, he says, in which you have tremendous capacity to learn. You learn from sorrow. You learn from joy. You can learn from any means. But always remember, the inspiration, the answers are within you. There is no outside input.

And then the next lesson, which he gives to what he calls an advanced group. You can meditate, he says, and then five minutes later lose it all. The next lesson, my friends, is not that. The next lesson is that you realize who you are. To be in such a state that you are the inspiration to the outer world that you truly are. Let yourself be free, to be joyful, to share that joy with others. You have something to give that is so precious that it cannot be described.

For you will never be alone, he says, for you are on a path which is shared by many, many others. There is a kind of interweaving, so that you can never be alone. You walk with the Creator and with all those who seek the Creator. Imagine, my friends, the loneliness of those who do not know that they are the child of the Creator. Yet they are. They are part of the great and perfect union.

Well, my friends, he says, I speak a long time for someone who has nothing to say, and I apologize if I speak too long. But there is nothing to apologize for, because what he said was everything. Not a new technique. Not a new doctrine. A reminder, aimed at people who already knew it, that the inspiration was never going to come from the channel. It was always going to come from the ones holding out their hands to each other, like strands of a fence, growing flowers over the strength they made together.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Prince Who Became a Cottager
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the prince who became a cottager.

Hatonn speaks this evening in a parable, he says, for often that which is true can be seen better when it is seen as a part of a story. And so, my friends, we write a story of a prince who had a kingdom.

Standing upon the turrets of his castle, the prince gazed over the great domain over which he reigned, and he was very glad, for was he not prince, and did not all he saw belong to him? He was by nature a kindly man, much given to good deeds, and merciful in action, living at peace with his neighbors, skilled in diplomacy, and without any blemish that could be seen.

How he loved his kingdom. He loved his fields and his forests, his farmlands, his villages and towns, and the lovely castle which had been improved and added to over centuries until it was indeed a glorious sight, with spires and castellations, towers and watchtowers. And once every year in the castle keep came all of his people rejoicing that their king was so just, so mighty, and so powerful.

One day the winds of change came upon the kingdom. Boats of a foreign and strange creation landed upon the shore, and within a very short time the peace-loving king was removed quite utterly from his reign. The king escaped because of the love of his people, for they took him in as one of them, and he began life anew as an humble cottager, toiling in the fields, carefully guarding the forests, and serving the new lord of the land.

And once a year the people, fewer each year for fewer remembered, would come to visit one small village, and they would kneel before one old cottager, humble and full of years. And he, well adjusted to his new life, would say as if in ritual, do not bow your knee to me, for I have no fields and no forests. I have neither land nor estate. And his people would remain on their knees and say, we praise you as our king, because you have taught us goodness and peace.

This cottager who had been king died quietly, and the kingdom remained, unhappy now, scourged by heavy taxes and unfair practices of all kinds. And in the length and breadth of time came there those with books and knowledge, and slowly, very slowly, the kingdom again changed.

And then Hatonn widens the lens, from the kingdom of men to the kingdom of the Father. Amidst all these experiences, he says, the creation of the Father grew and flourished in its season. Fields and forests, birds, animals, fish, nothing of man truly upset the creation of the Father, for there is a love in such balance and of such power that its ability to heal itself, given enough time, is perfect.

We are aware, he says, that each of you are in a different situation. Some of you dwell under a good and peaceful ruler, either yourself, another being, or a great ideal that you seek. And so love rules your life and all of your movements are graceful. Those of you to whom we speak, we ask that you meditate upon the meaning of your fortune, and upon how you can share your love. Some of you dwell under the angry king. You are in slavery or bondage to yourself, a habit, a possession, another person, or a false ideal. We ask you in your meditation to ponder the reason for your slavery, and how, through sharing your difficulties with the Creator and with your friends, you may free yourself.

But those who are fortunate and those who are not are often one and the same person in different moods and at different times, he says. And so we speak to all of you when we ask you to look up, outside your windows, outside your world, into the world of the Creator. Try not to miss one single day of the creation, for your days are numbered.

And if you spend some time with the creation of the Father, he says, you will find that it asks only one thing of you. It only asks that it may love you just as you are. The rain and the sun shine on all of you, criminal and saint, fool and wise man. The trees shade all of you, and the presence and the consciousness of the earth is one of total acceptance of you. It is a great sorrow of ours that many among the peoples do not reciprocate this feeling.

Your fortunes will pass, good and bad, the kings of your life will change, but the fields and the forests will be there for you, he says. When your internal lessons are not audible to you in the silence of your meditation, walk out into the incredible beauty of the creation of the Father, and open yourself to communion with that which only desires to be of service and to love.

The prince lost his kingdom and found he was still a king, because his people remembered what he taught them. Not the fields. Not the forests. The goodness and the peace.

Thank you for listening.

title: Neither Good Nor Evil, but Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: neither good nor evil, but love.

Latwii is the keynote speaker this evening, he says, and this is not his usual task. But the teachers of Hatonn, because they are of the vibration of love, are at this moment very busy elsewhere upon your planet. So Latwii takes the podium, and the subject is the moment of your world.

Our fear is not for your physical bodies, he says, but simply for the timing of this global conflict. We do not wish to stay the conflict forever, if that is the will of your peoples, but we wish to send as much love as possible to your leaders of all nations, of all beliefs, and of all polarities, in the hopes that we can for just a little while longer continue to offer the pathways of observation, convocation and evolution to your peoples.

Although your peoples cannot go backwards, he says, they can certainly drag their heels.

Yes, my friends, he says, you can resist. There are a few planets who have resisted so completely that there is no light. But evolution is inevitable, even upon such lost planets. Yours is just in the middle, my friends. There are not so many who would be evil, but my friends, there are not so many who would be good. The great majority of your peoples would be neither good nor evil, but do not seem to have a predisposition to either. Hence, they are as pawns in a game which they know not of.

You, my friends, have begun to understand the game, he says, and have begun to aid in your own evolution by understanding the value of being polarized toward love. This is not an easy polarization. That teacher named Jesus would never have promised that it was easy. For he said, if you would be my disciple, take up your cross and follow me. Did he mean that all of you must go through life in some kind of terrible martyrdom? No, my friends. Your teacher laughed at weddings and changed water into wine so that his friends might make merry and rejoice. He had a very deep sense of humor and rarely felt sorry for himself. He knew the ways of love and he knew that the path involved is a stony path. The path of evolution is a rocky path.

The reason for this is very simple, he says. When you are not aware of the process of evolution, you are not responsible for your lessons. You react in a completely instinctual manner. However, when this student takes on the responsibility of the path towards truth, he will be given small quizzes along the way. Everyone is given these quizzes, but most do not recognize them. The student recognizes them, and therefore has the responsibility for meeting them.

If you are having difficulty loving an enemy, he says, you will be faced with that problem until you have conquered it. If you have trouble with one enemy, that enemy may go away, but you will have another. Each time that you have the choice between anger and calm acceptance and creative understanding, and you choose the release of anger, you know, those of you who are on the path, that you must do it again, and that it will meet you, most surely.

The quizzes repeat until they are passed. The enemy changes face but not subject.

We wish we could tell you how this will all come out, he says, because we like a good story as well as you, but we do not know the answer, we do not know the timetable. We do know the final outcome, for there is only one final outcome. In the battle between good and evil, that which survives will be neither good nor evil, but love. Good and evil are the light and the shadow of love. Love will prevail, but we do not know when.

We ask you especially to understand, he says, that each side is convinced of his own rightness and goodness. No one in this particular situation feels evil. No one accepts the role of the bad guy. Each feels that God, Allah or history is on his side. You are fighting a civil war, my friends, for you are all planetary brothers, and your national feelings remind us of a finger plotting against its hand, or one foot plotting against the other knee.

We ask you to cleanse your soul as you would a garment, he says, rinsing it in the cool, clear waters of a mountain stream until it is completely cleansed of nationalism, pride, glory and righteousness. Lift your enemies up into the light, my friends, for they are your brothers. They are sad, they are puzzled, they do not know the light.

And on nationalism, he is gentle and unsparing at once. The feelings of nationalism are proper to your situation at this time, he says. However, you may respond as the situation in the illusion requires, and know beyond a shadow of a doubt that it is an illusion, and that you are, in truth, a child of the Creator. Whatever actions are necessary, you will do, but not with hate, with obsession, with pride, with righteousness, but only with compassion.

Feel the peace of this place which exists, my friends, inside yourselves. Keep that white light in your heart. You are of the light. It will make you more thoughtful. It will make you less understood, but it will make you more understanding.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Hidden Picture
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the hidden picture.

Latwii arrives in this session almost apologetically. He tells the group straight away that he is not, in his words, one of the smooth talking professors of Hatonn, and is not nearly so used to delivering the inspiration that is in his heart. Which makes what follows all the lovelier, because he delivers one of the simplest teachings in the whole archive.

He begins with a question, and I want to hand it straight to you. Which things in your life turn towards the light? How long have you spent in the shade of things? He says that each moment spent with your face turned away from the sun, the great central sun of your existence, which is the love of the Creator, is a moment lost. The faces of love are infinite, he says. There is a face in every problem, in every situation.

Then he turns the whole thing into a game. You may consider this a game, he says. Find the hidden picture. You remember this game from childhood. There is a picture of a tree, and hidden in the branches of the tree there is a picture of a kangaroo. So it is with your life, my friends. Hidden in every picture is a picture of love. Love distorted, love undistorted. Love strained by your own misunderstandings. But nevertheless, he says, that thing which we call love creates the changes, and incarnates all that there is.

I love the playfulness of it. Latwii knows the group is on a path and he wants to help them walk it, but he draws a clear line. We cannot be your walking stick, he says. All we can do is say to you: yes, there is a path. No, you are not foolish. Yes, hidden in the tree there is a kangaroo. Many of those about you, he warns, will only ever see the surface of a situation. Do not spend your moments meandering through a thicket of details while forgetting the great detailer who drew up the great plans.

And who is this great detailer, he asks? Someone far off, to whom you may pray, someone with a name? This great detailer, my friends, is yourself. This fine creator is yourself. Yourself in an alternate form. Yourself with all of your parts put back together in harmony. He says it three times, and each time it lands a little deeper, like a bell struck again before the ringing stops.

So here is the game, and it never really ends. In every picture, find the hidden picture. In every trouble, find the love. It is there in the branches. It has always been there.

Thank you for listening.

title: I Am Oxal Because I Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: i am oxal because i love.

Three entities share this evening: Oxal, Laitos, and Latwii. Oxal opens the session with something rare in the archive, a guided picture, and he builds it so slowly and so completely that you can almost smell it. Tonight we stay with his discourse, and then let Latwii add two short, sharp teachings of his own.

Picture with me now, Oxal says, a field distant from any settlement, a field in which butterflies fly freely and clover lies beneath the wildflowers. Feel the sun of a warm day down upon you. Hear the wind whispering its ever changing song through the trees and grasses, weaving the sounds like ribbons through the air. The flowers smell sweetly, and you can touch the fragrant petals of the wild and rambling roses. As you view all these things and feel the heat and light of the sun, you are experiencing the creation. You are part of the creation, and you are a rightful dweller in what is truly paradise.

This, he says, is the simplicity of all they have to give. And it is a simplicity that has proved, in his word, fatal, because we in our complexity desire complex answers, and we feel that if they were advanced they would be advanced in complexity. Listen to how he corrects that. I am Oxal, he says, not because I am of greater intellect than you who sit in meditation. I am Oxal because I love. I and my brothers know this love, see this love, and feel this love.

Then he asks the group to leave the field and enter a harder one: the field of life, where the flowers you touch are papers, and people. There the wind gives way to the creations of man, and the noise of our neighbors drowns out the message the wind whispers through the branches. Can you see the Creator, he asks, as you look at the distorted creation of man? He would be amazed, he admits, if any of us could fully do it. We are not the clay, he says. We are the potter. Our actions and thoughts are the clay, but we are the potters of our existence.

And here is where his teaching turns inward, and it is the part I want you to keep. We ask you, he says, to begin with yourself and to end with yourself in your attempts to discover love. Forgive yourself of any and all errors. Love yourself in whatever imperfect state you may judge yourself to be. If you were in a drunken stupor and you tripped, he asks, would you not forgive yourself in the morning? That is your situation, my friends. You dwell in a very heavy chemical illusion. It is a difficult experience, but in it you learn quickly, and that is why you put yourself here.

Latwii, when his turn comes, brings the humor, and he means it as medicine. He tells the group that the brain's secretions can reprogram the self healing of the body, and that laughter triggers them the way powerful chemicals do, but in ways already arranged by a kindly Creator. If a person once discovers how to laugh, he says, this person will have a good chance of reprogramming the basic patterns of the personality. You do not have to go outside your own being for the remedies for your difficulties.

And Latwii closes with the hardest counsel of the evening, on the subject of helping others. You can only help those people who ask you for help, he says. Unwanted help is unnecessary help, and it will only interfere, for all have a sovereign free will. Think of yourself as a watershed, over which many will flow. A few you may help with a word, a few with a touch, a few with generosity of food or speech. And remember, he says, that you dwell in the midst of a great cosmic joke and a great cosmic tragedy, and the ability to see both polarities equally is a very helpful one. Laugh at your grief, he says, and be solemn in your joy, and then you may be of balanced help to others.

Begin with yourself, end with yourself, forgive the stumbling, laugh when you can, and let the field come to you. That is the whole of it, and it is enough.

Thank you for listening.

title: Here Is Freedom
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: here is freedom.

Hatonn opens this session with a single subject: freedom. And because he is Hatonn, he does not begin with a definition. He begins with a story, and it is one of my favorites in the archive.

There was once a young man who desired freedom, for he was a young man of great sensitivity. When he saw the poverty, the hunger, the suffering in the world about him, he could not understand how people could be bound to their suffering. So he spent years working actively to alleviate suffering and promote personal freedom for his brothers and sisters, wherever he found the need. But ultimately he was betrayed by his own bitterness, for he knew that no matter what he did, it would never be enough.

So he set his daily work aside and went on a journey to learn why men must be bound by suffering, and why they could not be free. He asked many people and received many answers, and with none of them was he satisfied. One day his ship stopped at a small tropical isle for supplies, and there he found a native who spoke his language, and he told this man his great dilemma. The native was a large man and his laugh was equally loud, and his laughter rang through the small room where they sat. Then the big man tapped his forehead. Freedom, he said. Here is freedom, nowhere else. And when the young man cried out about all those who were starving, or ill, or poor, the native reached out and tapped the seeker on the forehead. Their freedom is in your head, he said. You must let them go, then, their freedom will be in their heads.

Listen to what Hatonn builds on that. You do not live in an objective universe, he says. Any limitation you experience is a limitation only because of your perception of the way things should be as opposed to the way things are. If you are fully grounded in your knowledge of who you are, then you are free to fulfill your desire to know the truth. And you are free, he says, only when you snap the cords of your own desire to be somebody in this world. When you have dismantled your desire for reputation, then you have no more bonds, and you are free.

He does not pretend the suffering is not there. There are still those who are hungry, who are poor, and who suffer. This is so, my friends. But each man is free if he desires to be. You are not responsible for the world, he says. You are responsible for yourself, and in yourself dwells the world. Those who need you will be drawn to you. And he adds one instruction that runs through the whole archive like a spine: never volunteer esoteric information to those who have not asked, nor withhold it from any serious student.

A desire for freedom is an impossible desire, he says, for you dwell in the prison of a body, of a gravity well, of a heavy illusion, and yet you are willing prisoners of the catalyst of this experience. The way to freedom lies in accepting the conditions of your particular incarnation and in asking to know the truth. Seek and know the truth, he reminds them, for the truth shall make you free.

When Latwii takes the questions later, he turns to the subject of dreams, and what he says is quietly startling. A third of your life, if you are lucky, he says, is spent gathering messages from parts of your mind and spirit that are forced into quiet during your working day. In your dreams you are conversing with parts of yourself that are in touch with your higher self, and with those he calls your angels or your guides. The more you meditate or pray, he says, the less sleep you will need, for sleep is the price of not listening while awake.

Freedom is nowhere else. It is in the head, in the heart, in the choice to seek. The young man went looking for it across the world and found it in a tap on the forehead.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Book of Mirrors
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the book of mirrors.

Latwii begins this session with a confession that charms me every time I read it. He says his brother Hatonn has begun to teach him the art of storytelling, and he will practice it on the group this evening. Then he tells a story good enough to make any teacher proud.

There was once an explorer, a treasure hunter, whose desire in life was to seek out the greatest and the best treasure of all time. Because all desires become reality, he found an old man who knew of the greatest treasure. But, the old man warned, this great treasure is guarded by a three headed dragon, and you must go down into dark caves to find it.

So the explorer sold all that he had and set out, and after every conceivable hardship he reached a deep, dark grotto. Bravely he moved through the darkness, retracing his steps through dead ends, until he heard the hiss of the dragon and saw it glowing an unearthly green in the great vault. There was a great battle, and finally the explorer slew the three headed dragon. Onward he moved in total darkness, now that the dragon light was extinguished, and came to the treasure chamber. Upon a pedestal stood a beautiful filigree box, locked with an intricate lock.

Painfully, slowly, he carried it back into the light of day. He was starved, and the light blinded him, but days passed and he recovered, and with the infinite patience of those who truly desire the priceless, he tried every combination until the lock opened. In the box lay a brown leather book, or so it seemed. He picked up the book and opened it, and saw his own face. For the insides of the book, my friends, were two twin mirrors.

Listen to how Latwii lands it. You, my friends, are the treasure, the one priceless treasure of the universe, for you are life, and this pricelessness you share with all who have life and consciousness. Guides can tell you where to find the cave, and warn you of the dragon, and assure you that there is a treasure. But once you have found the treasure, what have you found? Yourself. Deeply buried is the treasure that lies within you, and he asks the question that does all the work: how much love, how much patience do you need to uncover yourself to yourself, for yourself, and for the world in which you live?

When the group is asked what they perceive the treasure to be, two voices answer, one says man, one says angel. And Latwii's reply is perfect. The blending of those two answers, my friend, is the Amen of existence.

Later, in the questions, Latwii is asked about the nature of illusion and reality, and he reaches for an image from the instrument's own mind. Reality, he says, is like a carrot dangled in front of the nose of the donkey. Each reality, once gained, becomes the illusion, and a new reality is seen. The path is infinite, he says, but he suspects it is also circular, that in the end we dwell completely in reality, but without individual consciousness, and then are sent forth again to complete the circle.

The dragon, the cave, the box, the mirrors. The treasure was the seeker all along. It always is.

Thank you for listening.

title: Accept It with Joy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: accept it with joy.

This is a shorter session, and a tender one. An unnamed sister entity speaks first, through difficult static, of heavy duties and grief. Then Latwii comes through, and you can feel him deliberately lifting the room. He thought the sister was a bit gloomy, he admits, but that is understandable. What he brings instead is one sustained note, and he holds it beautifully. That note is joy.

Look at the road ahead of you, he says, and accept it with joy. You do not know what the road will bring. It bends, it curves, it will have branches. Accept it now. When you have eased your mind, then you will be able to be free in the present moment. Do not live on the stretch of road that has not yet turned up in your experience. Experience the road of today.

And then he says something I keep returning to. Your people are very nice, he says, and sincerely want to help, but they are very serious. And healing, he believes, lies in a true understanding of joy. If a person has never felt joy, it can cause tremendous damage, for it is a profound emotion. You will find people moved to tears by being overjoyed, very often, for tears are your expression of sorrow, and yet they are also the expression of joy. That is how unused your people are to joy.

Remember your heritage, he says. You are joyous people who dwell on a sad, dark planet. There is no need to hide your light under a bushel. In whatever your situation, be yourself, and in being yourself your joy will flow from you like wine from a new bottle, for each of you has within you the spring of eternal joy. He cannot understand, he says, why we let so many insignificant details clutter the mind and keep us from radiating it, when radiating it is our primary function in altering the consciousness of the planet.

Later, answering a question about how to face danger, Latwii offers what this instrument would call being cool. The only way to present yourself to destiny, he says, is with the knowledge that if you live, you live, and if you die, you die. And since you are an eternal being, it does not matter. It may sound cold hearted, he admits, but the time to sit on your emotions is the time when you most want to express them. Train yourself, now and then, to see even a distortion of love begin its slow evolution back toward love, and the muscle memory will give you strength.

Most brave people are afraid, he says. I love that he says it so plainly. Courage is not the absence of the fear. It is the road, accepted with joy, walked anyway.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Permeable Membrane
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the permeable membrane.

This session survives on a tape that is difficult to hear, and much of it is lost to static. What remains is short, plain, and quietly radical. Latwii speaks as though he has very little time, and uses it to say one thing in several ways: you are not separate, and your consciousness is not a wall.

He begins where an old prayer begins. Hear, O Israel, the Lord your God is One. Listen, my friend, he says. What can you hear? What can you feel, as you enter into meditation? What can you see, with your eyes closed? Not the invocation of the light, but the one light, the light of love. You are the gate, he says, through which all of these things pass, from the outside to the inside, from the inside to the outside. That is your true position within this illusion. You allow in what you choose. You allow the manifestation of what you choose.

Then he asks the group to consider all the great serious issues: the reputation they had hoped for, their good looks, their success. And having considered them, he tells them to cut their grass and pursue their goals anyway. It is for this that you came into this environment, he says, to attach importance to the simple doing, day by day. The importance must be attached to the awareness you have in the doing of it. Are you aware of the unity and the love involved in what you do?

When you take out your garbage, when you flatter your boss, when you are angry at someone, you are learning spiritual lessons, he says. But not from the garbage, not from the boss, not from the anger. From the love that in its infinite wisdom created you in individual consciousness, able to choose which gate you would open. Your consciousness, my friends, is a permeable membrane. It can keep nothing out that belongs to you. And what you create within you cannot be kept from manifestation.

So he asks them to turn their heads away from ambition, away from pride, toward love and the oneness that links them to their brothers and sisters. And the method, as always, is the quiet one. In quiet, simple meditation, used on a daily basis, he says, you will do more to center and untangle your thoughts than any amount of self understanding, self analysis, or intellectual decision. There are parts of you that are not intellectual but belong in the decision making, and they dwell beneath the totally conscious, totally articulate self. To meditate is, among other things, to get back in touch with those parts.

He closes with a line nobody in the room laughs at, though he clearly hopes someone will. The next time that you become angry, he says, remember that love has become angry with love. I will allow you to draw your own conclusions about that, as he does. The membrane is permeable. Nothing you feel is happening to someone else.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Intelligent Tree
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the intelligent tree.

Latwii opens by saying that his brother Hatonn has begun to teach him the art of storytelling, and that he will practice it on the group this evening. It is a humble little preamble, and then he tells a story about a tree that I have not been able to forget.

There was once a young tree, and this tree was a very intelligent tree. It decided that it wished to become the best fruit tree of its kind that had ever been made in all of creation.
