Thank you for listening.

title: Love Is Folly
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love is folly.

The group asks about the companionship of money and spirituality, and Q'uo begins with a distinction. It is written in one of your holy works, they say, that the love of money is the root of all evil. They would point out that it is the love of money, as with any idolatry, which is at the root of separation. It is not the money itself which is contrary to a life led with a spiritual center, but the idolatrous love of that which is built by man in imitation of the Creator's abundance.

The love of money, they suggest, is a subtype of the idolatry of power. You designed your physical vehicles to be nearly powerless against the forces of your environment, and gave yourselves both the instinct for survival and the challenge of it. Money mimics true prosperity with a simple formula: more money equals more time. Those who have had large amounts of it, they observe, have virtually no consciousness of idolatry toward it, having learned the ramifications of artificial abundance, and seek instead a truer reality. But most souls incarnating here elect the consciousness of lack, because concern for survival creates it, and how easy, how understandable, how logical to love money when the lack of it has caused numberless discomforts.

So what is the alternative? Not poverty as a posture, but what Q'uo calls the consciousness of abundance. Through meditation it may be encouraged, and as truth drives out falsity, as love drives out fear, so true abundance drives out the false idol. The consciousness of abundance does not mean that all you wish for will come immediately, or at all. It means an awareness that that which is to be shall come to you through natural plentifulness.

Observe those who have found abundance, they say. Some may be wealthy and some quite poor, but what they have is an awareness of the excellence not only of life, but of the very life being lived by them. There are those whose happiness lies in children, those whose peace lies in love, others who find satisfaction in learning, still others who have the gift of being who they are. If you have little money, think not that you do not deserve more. If you have much, think not that you deserve less. Whatever your environment, fill it with your love of the Creator, that the light may shine through you, and you may become plenty to others.

And the second offering: a consciousness of others' needs. If stewardship of any gift and talent is expressed, they say, then the gates of abundance open and one is flooded with plenty. Seek first the consciousness of love through meditation and analysis of action and thought, and that which is needed shall be given unto you.

Then the evening turns, and Q'uo tells a story. There was once a woman whose life was too filled with luxury and too barren in all that was not physical. She hungered for the things young women hunger for: admiration, beauty, friendship, achievement. And then she found herself in love, in love with someone she knew better than her mother or father or herself, a man more real to her than flesh and blood, whom she called her savior, and for whom she would live and gladly die.

She joined a convent, worked at menial tasks, and was sent to be a nurse among the poorest of the poor, kneeling in streets where the homeless have their homes, touching faces half-eaten by pestilence, and seeing in each the face of her savior. This entity walks among you, Q'uo says. This entity could be you. And each of you knows that.

The story is told to answer a question about contacting intelligent infinity, and the answer is startling in its simplicity. If you wish to make contact with intelligent infinity, you must know what you love more than flesh and blood and your own life. Look deep for the mysterious one you may call a savior, and when you find that face that you can love wholly, then you shall find the gateway. There is no knowledge or understanding that will move you upon the journey to behold the face of the one who will save you from death, the death of limitation in consciousness.

And then the sentence that gives this episode its name. If you are not capable at this moment of falling in love, then the gateway of intelligent infinity is not yours at this moment, for you are not extravagant enough to know of love. Love is folly, for only folly could create the wonder that you see all about you. Only folly would wish to know itself. Only love can see life.

They are sorry, they say, to have no techniques to offer, save one. Seek, and seek, and seek again, patiently, persistently and extravagantly. Find ways to laugh and bless your tears. Attempt to see love in everyone and everything, and forgive yourself when you do not. Seek love, in love, for love's sake. All else will follow.

Thank you for listening.

title: Cleaning the House
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: cleaning the house.

Some of the group have taken part in a recent global day of peace, and they ask Q'uo about it. Q'uo answers generously: they will not speak of that one event, but of the mass spiritually based event in general, and its nature. And they admit a sympathy for the impulse behind every day of prayer for whatever cause that has ever been organized among your peoples.

If one were to look upon your planet as a house, they say, the special spiritually oriented events could be seen as the attempt to clean house in one day. Moreover, because of the complexities within your planetary subcultures, the belligerent actions and intentions of many served as those who caroused and destroyed the very house being cleaned. These same aggressions continue each of your days. Long in your history is the march of days in which shots have been fired in anger and hatred, whether the missiles be of lead, stone, mud, or those subtle missiles called words.

So the assessment is modest, and Q'uo does not hide it. One entity's light is visible amongst the darkness of the whole planet, and they would not wish you to think that the running sore of your planet's propensity for aggressive action can be healed by the application of one day's bandage. But there is no discouragement in it either. It is only through such events, and any other well-intentioned events whatsoever, that your people's consciousness can be transformed. Each entity which included peace, love, light and brotherhood in consciousness for one day may begin to include it in consciousness for all. For it is in the persistent turning of the perceptions toward one tenor of thought which will eventually transform consciousness.

Then Q'uo turns the image inward, and this is where the evening deepens. Yes, you seek peace for your planet, they say, but is your spiritual dwelling place strong enough for peace to reign therein? Is your heart and mind a place wherein the Creator may dwell? See yourself as a dweller within a structure which you have built so that it may contain that spirit within you which is of the Creator and which is the Creator.

You cannot legislate peace by prayer, they say, for there is more to you than the top floor. There is the first floor and the basement. You must reckon with each and every instinct, each influence of the body complex, accepting, celebrating, and becoming a proper steward of each impulse which affects your consciousness. Go within your mind into each and every corner of consciousness, examining, accepting and blessing every disharmony. Herein is the cradle of destruction: the heart and mind, when the full consciousness of your kind is not acknowledged and disciplined. You shall find peace to come more easily when the enemy within you is carefully understood.

There is a stranger interlude that night, and I want to include it, because it shows something about how this contact works. Q'uo tells the instrument they are winding her coil, though she does not understand what they are doing. Asked what it means, they explain: the coil is the pattern that intelligent energy, the love and light of the Creator, takes as it moves through your energy centers, a rhythmic spiraling of energies. When meeting no resistance, the energy intensifies as it rises through the centers. In winding the coil, they are shooting, as they playfully put it, an extra dose of energy through the spiraling centers, complementing the work the instrument has accomplished through her own tuning and prayer.

The questions turn practical. One who works among the deceased asks whether the departed feel the love sent to them, and Q'uo answers tenderly: the communication of love and good feelings to those who have passed is a blessing greatly appreciated, a reassurance to entities who may feel themselves between worlds. Send the heartfelt love and joyful farewell, that the entity might be speeded upon its way.

And one asks, once more, about money and spiritual service: must those who offer spiritual gifts charge for them, or not? Q'uo's answer is characteristically balanced. Let the desire to serve be the foundation, they say, and the way to serve shall be made clearer, with synchronistic events smoothing the path. Whether a price is set is basically unimportant, if the price is not rigid, and never becomes an obstacle to the service when one who desires it cannot pay. The service is always offered. The fee is flexible, and secondary.

Clean the house, then, but start with your own rooms, every corner of them. The peace of the planet is built the way the peace of a house is built: one dwelling at a time, one persistent turning of perception after another.

Thank you for listening.

title: The One Arena
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the one arena.

Q'uo begins this Saturday evening with a single instruction for a group circling many concerns. There is only one response to the many-sided concern of illusion, they say, and that is gently, cleanly and with grace to suggest the turning of the attention always to that which is the unity, the mystery, the love which is behind all the many scenes. Imagine each part of the illusion as a sequin sewn onto an almost unimaginably large structure, made for the delight and benefit of all, that all could walk around and behold the beauty of the illusion.

Yet how easy it is, they say, to come too close to these glittering false sides, never seeing the stitches that hold illusion to illusion, never seeing the bare chicken wire beneath the paper shapes, never seeing the hollowness of the interior. For illusion, like an onion, peels to nothing. But it cannot be assumed there is nothing beyond it. Indeed, it is the very marked nature of illusion which suggests, equally markedly, that a mystery lies beneath what is seen.

Thus, they wish to speak of love. And the first of their two points is this: there is only one arena for the true study of ultimate things, and that is one's own consciousness. Meditation remains the one discipline not to be ignored, avoided, or shortened beyond a reasonable point. Its dailiness is a majority of its virtue.

It is not known to an entity within the illusion when each moment of realization shall occur. But one who meditates daily, with intent to open to whatever transformation there may be in the silence, is expecting and seeking the opening of the doors within the consciousness, doors which open in a random manner, so that a great view might be missed entirely were meditation not to occur upon the appropriate day. He who watches shall not be surprised.

And this is true not only of the meditative state, but of the meditative view of the present moment. The very sunlight, the white-capped sea, the waving branches of summer burst with the vitality of realization, for they dwell within the consciousness of love. One who watches not the shiny face of illusion but the face of the Creator within each illusion may see that one original Thought in color after color, distortion after distortion. Some distortions may seem horrible and some wonderful, yet all are the Creator, and realization lies within each moment's burden of love, which is infinite to the discerning spirit.

Love cannot be seen, they say, by those not willing to open and call upon the consciousness of love. There is always the leap of faith: the necessary assumption that the mystery behind all the things that are not is, in the end, the one thing about the illusion which cannot be denied, and that is love. Yet there is not one honest spirit that can deny the palpable effect of love within the life experience.

The second point is quieter, and it is really a confession. Q'uo perceives a difficulty in the group, or in the instrument, and names it: the acceptance of anyone's point of view, including one's own, as being of an importance which loses sight of the perspective of eternity. So many things shall pass through your minds, they say, so many arenas entered and left. Ten things you learn will help you become of greater service, and ten million things you learn will be of no use whatsoever once the incarnation has been processed. So care less about the thinking, the rightness, the probabilities, the future. Turn instead to questions like these: what is the motive? What service am I performing? What gift may I give? What consolation may I offer?

The evening's question comes from a seeker caught in a painful tangle. She sends out what she believes is love, and it is perceived as causing harm. She cannot send more, and to stop sending feels wrong for the sender. What does one do in that space? Q'uo answers with the phrase from your holy works: bread cast upon the water. When one gives with the pure desire to be of service, the giving must be given freely, with no dedication to a particular return. And the heart of love is offered, in this way, the opportunity to give under adverse circumstances, which strengthen the desire to give.

She presses further. If you know, because you have been told, that what you give causes pain, then it is no longer a gift freely given, but pain freely given. Q'uo does not untie the knot for her. They cannot, without infringing on what she came to solve herself. Instead they suggest gaining a perspective, perhaps with time and space between the experience and its resolving, and building, in meditation, a pathway to the subconscious mind, traveled regularly for the pieces that wait there. Combine it with the dreaming state, they say: ask at night that each dream be remembered, record it, and make it the topic of the day's meditation. In this fashion the subconscious is programmed to release, piece by piece, what the conscious mind alone cannot solve.

One arena, then. Your own consciousness. The sequins glitter, the wire shows through, and underneath it all, the one thing that cannot be denied.

Thank you for listening.

title: Joy and Sorrow
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: joy and sorrow.

The group asks Q'uo to discuss the paradox of opposite emotions. Why, they ask, is there both joy and sorrow? And Q'uo begins, characteristically, by admiring the questioners. Each of you, they say, creates a beautiful harmony with all the colors and shades of emotion, thought and action with which you weave the tapestry of your lives. In meditation your energy centers flow, colorful and beautiful to our perception. Each of you is radiant, and at peace. Yet what makes you at peace is not what you have asked about.

Their answer starts with the Creator's point of view. The Creator can only become self-conscious by gazing at the infinite reflections that are consciousnesses given free choice, and each time an entity chooses to use joy productively, or to use a difficult experience productively, the greater self cheers, knowing the Creator has again chosen to express itself in a more coherent and unified manner. All of evolution, in their opinion, moves in a purposefully positive way.

But that explains joy and sorrow, not the paradox. To grasp the necessity of paradox, they say, one must first realize the profound mystery of the creation itself. Those who use words, and to a great extent those who use concepts, are completely unable to grasp truth. There is no polarity in the ultimate sense, nor is there sense. Sense is the organization of random effects so that coherence may be established.

Your conscious mind can only deal with sense. So it is extremely common among your peoples to see the Deity itself in a polarized fashion. All of your illusion depends upon polarity, and a considerable portion of the total experience of which we are aware. The either-or nature of your experience is designed to enable the decision-making process, so that as each entity moves through the density of choice, each choice has the chance of being a firm and serious one, highly polarized, making one a more conscious person.

Thus all emotions may be found to have their opposite, and indeed in some way to include and evoke the opposite shadow. For has there been pure joy without sorrow? Or unadulterated sorrow without some fond or joyful shade? As the seeker grasps the intended use of both, the seeker may balance joy with sorrow and sorrow with joy, sickness with health and health with sickness, finding in any polarity a free choice for the emotion expressed in experience.

It is rare for seekers to find this discipline easy, they admit. But the problem of polarity shall be with you for a long portion of experience, and it is well to begin. In the end, they say, if we can find joy an occasion to worship and sadness an occasion to praise, we shall once and for all have learned a central lesson of consciousness.

The questions that night turn to how one actually moves reality. Someone asks about manifesting what one desires, and Q'uo traces it to the root. Desire brought each into the incarnation. The power of desire is what moves each entity through each density in the returning into unity, for it is desire that set the creation in motion, as the one Creator expressed the desire to know itself by sending portions of itself into the far reaches of creation. Each entity carries that same power of motivation. It manifests within your illusion as will and faith. As an entity focuses the power of the will in a direction, and empowers it with the faith that what is willed may be obtained, the entity unleashes the power of desire to move itself.

And if you cannot sustain the emotion behind a desire, is that a sign you do not truly want it? Basically perceived correctly, Q'uo says. Each entity is a complex expression of desires chosen before the incarnation and during it, and they may work at cross currents in the subconscious. The realigning of choices is speeded by careful inward searching of what is truly of most value. For the most efficient fulfillment of desire, it is well to know the self, and those foundation stones which give you a base to stand on as you choose your path through the creation.

Joy and sorrow, then, are not enemies. They are the two poles between which a choosing creature learns to choose, until the choice itself becomes the worship.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Wedding Night
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the wedding night.

This evening opens with something the archive rarely gives us: a stranger's whole life, told in his own words at its very end. He gives his name as best the instrument can catch it, something like Ahbout Dey, and he is careful to say he is not a member of the Confederation, nor a social being, but an individual, as are each of you. He speaks, he says, from an icy fastness far from humankind, and he has placed himself in his final resting place. He wishes to share, before he goes, the joy of experiencing what he calls the end of the personal trail of his life.

As a very young boy he wished to be a girl, and his father, ashamed, gave him to a monastery. This may seem hard, he says, yet it was his salvation. For thirty years he held a subservient place there, and the simple things became more and more nourishing to him, and his own company became more and more desirable. At thirty-nine he was allowed to become a retreatant, one who contemplated constantly and alone. At fifty-five he woke one morning with itching feet, left his cave, and started walking, seeking to study more, seeking to be sure he was free of what he called his karmic responsibility. He walked into China and found no satisfaction, and into India, where a missionary spoke to him of redemption. And as he dies, for he is now old, he is glad in his heart, as if he were still a young man, that he has come to see redemption in all that lies around him.

For thirty-three years, he says, he lived the incarnation of a solitary man. He witnesses that the lord of his life is far more vivid than the sweetest tastes, sounds, feelings, thoughts or objects possible in the world. He rejoices at the dissolution of old bones, and awaits the freeing of his perfect spirit. Neither Buddhist nor Christian, yet loving the sun of his day and the moon of his night, he comes to his death as a bride to the wedding night, fearful yet full of gladness.

I read that line twice, and then a third time. To come to death as a bride to the wedding night. Fearful, yet full of gladness. It eased his heart, he says, to have one last human touch, and he blesses the group for hearts that respond and understand that all humans are one together. The Christ in me, he says, acknowledges and rejoices in the Christ in you. Farewell.

Latwii follows, and the evening turns to questions, but the stranger's farewell hangs over all of it. Asked about service to others, Latwii divides it in two: service that aids another spiritually, and service that aids in ordinary ways. In neither case is it acceptable to infringe upon free will. Any service not requested may be suggested, but not properly fulfilled without permission. And they emphasize always the value of communication: gauge the mood and intention of the one you would serve, and value your own free will as highly as theirs.

Someone asks, half-joking, for a shot in the arm, having found the last years full of surprises that were not mistakes but felt aggravating all the same. And Latwii answers with what one member of the group calls a two-by-four, lovingly received. Those times of difficulty, of confusion, of the totally unexpected, are those times which before the incarnation are seen as treasures. It is known before the incarnation that one shall see through a glass darkly, and that what is difficult will seem to be minimized or avoided. But the difficulties exercise a spiritual muscle which, in realms of harmony and joy, tends to grow lax and lose its tone.

So judge not the self, or another, or the progress of any, Latwii says, for as you judge, so are you judged by worldly measurements that cannot begin to encompass the illusion you move in. Keep the light touch. Accept what seems unacceptable. There is a stream of beingness that moves before, through and beyond this illusion, and it shall carry you further toward the source of all being as you are able to accept in joy each experience that comes before you. For each experience is what you had hoped for, and planned for, and girded your loins for.

And at the very end, a third voice, brief and wordless. The one known as Nona comes through the instrument to sing of love and light and healing, a vocal melody with no words at all. After all the careful answers about service and surprise and free will, the evening closes the way the stranger's life closed: not with explanation, but with music, and gladness, and farewell.

Thank you for listening.

title: No Government May Hinder
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: no government may hinder.

The question this evening is a sweeping one. What style of life makes one more adaptable to the spiritual journey: the community-oriented life where the individual is taught to think of the group's welfare, or the hermit's life of seclusion and contemplation, or the ordinary life of temptations and self-expression? And Q'uo begins by refusing the question's terms. We cannot speak to you, they say, concerning the structure of your communism as opposed to your capitalism in regards to spiritual benefits, because government is not of the ray wherein spiritual concerns are addressed.

The nature of spiritual programming, they explain, is that it overrides all other programming, changing the perceptions of the entity working within it, so that regardless of the catalyst that greets the seeker, the seeker perceives a spiritual question and attempts the spiritually motivated action in response. The communist can experience either complete freedom or complete slavery within the communistic way of life, as can the capitalist. The perceptions govern the experience, not the catalyst.

Governments, they observe, work with the tools of persuasion and force, and must rely upon the lowest possible level of excellence, the greatest possible swing of error, so that whatever action is undertaken among humans there shall be a governing principle. The law that interests the spiritual seeker is of another kind entirely: a law the seeker hopes shall become perceivable by all seekers, so that spiritual government is government by complete individual consent. This is considered unacceptably inefficient by those whose energies turn to the governing of peoples, and understandably so.

There is one element in the concepts of capitalism, they say, which is a metaphysical principle of some excellence, though not fully respected among your peoples: the concept of freedom. It is excellent that freedom is taught. Yet for spiritual seeking, remember that one is always free, for the world, indeed the creation, lies within the mind and the heart, and there is no government which may interfere with the polarizing done by the spiritual seeker, except if the government destroy the physical body of the seeker. And even that, taking the larger view, may for a particular seeker be a great aid, if by being a sacrifice to a principle the seeker inspires others, as is the way of spiritual seekers of excellence among your peoples.

Then the closing of the main address, which I think is one of the finest passages in this whole stretch of the archive. Turn your gaze at last, they say, from the creations of humankind, however lofty and beguiling, however intellectually precise and fascinating, for that which lies within you is a dimly perceived holographic representation of one great original Idea, an Idea which is a mystery. Why do you look within illusion for your true nature? Do you not wish to know the truth? The truth lies not among the fallow fields of men's imaginations and actions, nor within fine words or great governments. The truth about you lies within the mystery of the face of God. The one thing you have been taught is constant in a shifting world is light itself, and yet light is only the physical manifestation of an Idea that created all that there is. It is within the mystery of the Idea of love that the truth about you lies. There is no government that may help or hinder in the seeking of that face.

The questions afterward are smaller and more human. One, living with physical difficulties and some despair over the future, asks what can be said besides, don't do that. And Q'uo answers with unusual tenderness. Remember at all times, they say, that you move within the limitless love of the Creator, in order that through your experience the Creator might uncover its own face. The more difficult the seeking, the more deeply the revelation of love may be seated within the being. That which is cheaply bought is easily forgotten. That which bears the greater price remains, as sure foundation stones upon which further experience and service are possible.

If that is where you are tonight, take that slowly. You are not forgotten inside the difficulty. The price you are paying is laying foundation stones.

Thank you for listening.

title: Company in Silence
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: company in silence.

This is one of the shortest sessions in the archive, and one of the quietest. Laitos comes to meet a new instrument, the one known as W, and almost nothing is said. That is the service.

Laitos explains their function simply. They are members of the Confederation, and their work is with those who wish to be aided in their attempts to serve as vocal channels. For the one known as W, they wish to create a protected space of time in which she may safely dwell in silence, while being willing to be made aware of the presence of those forces and principles which lie under the shelter and shadow of the name of love. With this aid more firmly in consciousness, it is then a matter of a shorter seeking until the patiently waited-for moment occurs, and one new piece of the puzzle is added, and one more thing about the self is learned, and one more portion of life experience may be dedicated in the service of humankind and of the infinite Creator, of which all created things are but the reflection and image.

I love that long, patient sentence. The work is not hurried. One piece of the puzzle at a time. One more thing about the self. The silence is not empty; it is sheltered.

Then Laitos pauses, that W may sit in the quiet and feel the loving company of those portions of the consciousness of love available for her comfort. When they return, they are grateful. They confess they have been working, too, trying to make their first contact with the instrument a comfortable one, and they are glad she is alive to the energies of which they spoke.

And before they leave, they make an offer that stays with me. They are happy, they say, to meet with any who request their presence during meditation, but they shall not speak. Their aid in deepening the meditative process is sometimes appreciated, they say, as is the feeling of having company. And they certainly enjoy this service also.

Not every service is speech. Sometimes the service is simply to sit beside someone in the silence, and let the silence do the teaching.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Art of Challenging
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the art of challenging.

Laitos returns to the work they know best: training new instruments. Tonight there are two, the ones known as W and N, and the evening becomes a careful, practical teaching on the most important skill in vocal channeling. Not the speaking. The challenging.

The session opens with Laitos speaking through the experienced instrument, and the first thing they establish is the spirit of the whole enterprise. The service of vocal channeling is one among many, they say, and each should evaluate it honestly, not only for comfort but for its relative degree of service, for there are many, many ways to be of service in a creation of love. Love has many faces. And though the Confederation comes always in the name of love and through the manifestations of light, they treasure each new instrument whose mind and heart they may draw upon, for their message is so simple as to go almost inevitably unnoticed: that the Creator is all that there is, that each is the Creator, and thus all are holographic representations, miniature co-creators with the Father.

We are as you, they insist, seekers after truth, lovers after love. Our eye is fixed upon the ultimate. We do not know the truth, but have only approximated our opinion as to some of the truth's characteristics. If anything we offer is unwanted, reject it without further thought. We wish only to serve.

Then the practical instruction, and it is exacting. To W, who is analytical, and to N, who watches herself even as she channels, Laitos makes the same request: lay down the tools of discrimination and thought for the duration of the experiment, and become the listening ear, hearing in silence those thoughts too deep for words. The instrument's position is one of passive yet anticipatory readiness. Whatever thought occurs immediately after the contact has been recognized and challenged is to be spoken forth without thought. Thought is left at the threshold of the contact, and picked up again, in all its discriminative power, when the channeling ceases.

I find that image remarkable. Thought left at the threshold like shoes at a door, and taken up again on the way out. The contact itself is a creation of cooperation, they say, offering something that neither they nor the instrument could offer alone.

And why is the challenging so central? Because, as this instrument is fond of saying, it is a crowded universe. N has had an experience with a crowd other than the Confederation, and Laitos uses it to make the point. A name alone is not protection, for names may be repeated by others who are not of the Confederation, and it is a powerful aid to a negatively oriented entity to be accepted as an entity it is not. So the instrument must gather the self about the ideal for which one lives, and challenge the contact with the full force of belief and the core of being, that the positive may be discerned from the negative.

There are signs to watch for, they add. One characteristic of mixed contact, a negatively oriented entity channeling under a positive name, is the tendency to make a personal connection with the channel, and make the channel feel more and more important. That occurred in N's experience. Yet some positively oriented contacts have also made personal contact, so in the end it is the challenging, conscientiously done, that the instrument must rely upon.

N asks about the entity she channeled months before, in another place, and Laitos answers in general terms, as is their custom with what belongs to the seeker's own examination. Certain locations on your planetary surface, they say, have through the ages been imbued with vibratory nexi of experience by various tribes and cultures, and continue to attract entities of that frequency, in the physical and metaphysical realms alike. Her sensitivity met such a place, amplified by the group she was with, and the contact ensued from that coincidence of circumstances.

The evening closes with gratitude, and a practical boundary worth remembering. Laitos is available upon request for joining in meditation, and the deepening of the meditative state, at any time. But the work of vocal channeling itself is best reserved for the gathered circle, that the process might continue with the most efficacy and the least confusion.

Speak without thought, but only after the challenge. It is a discipline of trust built on a foundation of discrimination, and Laitos holds both ends of it at once.

Thank you for listening.

title: To Breathe Is to Sing
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: to breathe is to sing.

The question put to Q'uo this evening is one of the most human in the archive. What do you say to people who have cancer, and are facing the possibility of death? Before I go further, a gentle note. What follows is a spiritual perspective offered in a meditation circle, not medical counsel. If you or someone you love is facing serious illness, please lean on your doctors, your loved ones, and whatever professional support you need. Take from this evening what comforts you, and leave the rest.

Q'uo begins by honoring the question, and the trust it represents. Then they offer the thought at the center of the evening. When you receive the news of a known killer found within the physical body, you will naturally spend an ocean of tears, wept or unwept, railing against the cessation of life. Yet in the crisis of possible death, they say, lies a tremendous opportunity for the rededication of the life. News of a possible death is a creative disturbance, a freeing mechanism, which allows the one experiencing it to consider a wider variety of options with more seriousness than when the entity thought itself perfectly healthy. There is an opportunity not to be afraid. There is the opportunity to turn into one who celebrates the life lived in the present moment.

Such an entity, having found a center of joy and peace in the appreciation of many blessings, notes with keen accuracy the difficulties of the present moment without becoming discouraged. Inspired by possible futures to amend the attitude of the present, the seeker may begin by affirming and celebrating each day as it awakens. This is not an exercise for death, they say. It is an exercise for life. For each day may be lived far more fully, and with far more enjoyment and freedom, spontaneity and humor, than most among your peoples are able to manifest.

Then the practical matters, and Q'uo is concrete here. Do not fix your thoughts on the lacks of the incarnation, especially those beyond your control, but on its assets: the remembrance of friends, strangers who smile, individuals who unpredictably but generously may aid an unknown person. If the environment of your livelihood has contributed to the illness, it may be time to use the creative energy of the difficulty to view the true needs of your social unit. Meditate, and find out for yourself whether the lesson is to stay and learn to love, or to move toward a greater love and faith. Deep within each entity, they say, there lies a sure knowledge of the rightness of each step of the life plan.

Q'uo offers, too, a metaphysical picture of illness in general, and I want to frame it carefully as theirs, not as fact. They describe the body manifesting illness as attempting to heal itself, and suggest that illness in general follows when the body reacts to a loss of balance within the body complex. It is a mechanical rather than judgmental description, they say. The counsel built on it is plain: transform the experience of serious illness into the beginning of a new consciousness, closer to the truth of yourself, more and more an opening through which the love and light of the infinite Creator shine forth, not to impress, but to make joyful.

Someone asks whether we choose our own deaths before incarnation, even through illness, and Q'uo answers with the care this subject deserves. Those aware of the incarnative process take a more complete role in planning what is to come, but because free will is paramount, the planning takes a general form, with many possibilities and probabilities, fluid and flexible. The ending of the incarnation, what you call death, is in many instances the subject of just such planning: a variety of possible exits, presented according to how the overall plan unfolds. When an entity has achieved much of what was laid out, it may meet a potential ending and, by using the catalyst well, continue on. When the lessons grow too heavy, an earlier exit may be taken through catalyst unsuccessfully processed. Each disease, they say, is a symbolic representation of a certain kind of lesson.

And then the closing passage, which is why this episode has its title. Let us all turn, they say, to that great light that shines in the darkness of ignorance and chaos, and seize hold of the central search. Life and death mean very little compared to the song of the present, for to breathe is to sing. Each soft rustle of inhalation and exhalation makes a melody in the ether of creation, and sends motes of light in millions of directions with each breath. Each intentional prayer is a lovely song, and each silence a poem.

Who you are is not how you feel, they say, not the condition of your body, not your bank account, not where you live. In the end the seeker stands alone with the truth, and each seeker is as infinitely great, and potentially infinitely impeccable, as that great warrior, the creation itself.

To breathe is to sing. If you are carrying something heavy tonight, let that be enough: one breath, one note, one more day affirmed.

Thank you for listening.

title: Refining Compassion
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: refining compassion.

We are in a small room in February of nineteen eighty-seven, gathered for an intensive meditation, and a group of seekers is learning something very strange and very human: how to speak words that are not their own.

The teacher this evening is Laitos, a member of the Confederation of Planets, and the students are new instruments — people whose voices Laitos hopes to borrow. There is a lovely tenderness in how Laitos speaks to them. They are brothers and sisters, Laitos says, who have only walked a little further along the same road.

And here is the heart of what Laitos tells them. This is the journey that you are upon, my friends. You are discovering ever greater portions of your own being and taking those discoveries as the impetus for yet further journeying into the self. I love that image — the work of the channel is really the work of knowing yourself, and by knowing yourself, discovering a connection that is intimate and unique with everything around you.

Then comes the practical part, and it is wonderfully down to earth. A new instrument braces for contact, Laitos says, the way one might brace for a cold shower — tensing the whole body against the shock. That is exactly the wrong move. Relax the mind, relax the physical body, through mental suggestion, before and during the contact. The channel stays open only if the instrument stays soft.

There is a moment I want you to hear. One student, called W in the transcript, feels her head pulled backward, her neck locked, impossible to move. Another, called N, feels a weight pressing forward on her neck. Is this a sign something is wrong? No, Laitos says — it is simply a sign that contact is happening. And here is the beautiful part: the student can ask, silently, for the sign to be adjusted. More apparent or less apparent, more comfortable or more noticeable. It is a collaboration. The instrument and the contact learn each other, the way two dancers learn each other's weight.

One question comes up that I found charming. May a channel lie down, the student asks, to relax completely? Laitos says it is tempting — but the body has spent years associating lying flat with sleep, and the new instrument will simply fall asleep. Sit upright instead, spine reasonably straight. Meditation is not napping.

But the part of the evening that stayed with me is about feeling itself. The student asks: do you experience emotions the way we do — happiness, sadness, jealousy? And Laitos answers with something I keep turning over in my mind. They have, in their experience, greatly simplified the emotional complex, until the overriding emotion that remains is one you might call love, or compassion. Fewer veils, Laitos says. Less hidden from them, the unity of all things — and so love is not a feeling among feelings anymore. It is the whole weather.

They are refining that love even now, trying to imbue it with something purer still. Which makes me think the whole evening is really about that one word: refinement. The channel refines the voice. The student refines the self. And somewhere further along the road, beings like Laitos are refining compassion itself.

If you take one practice from tonight, take the smallest one. Before anything you do — before speaking, before listening, before sleep — relax on purpose. Soften the shoulders. Unclench the jaw. Then listen, and see what comes through.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mark of the Angels
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mark of the angels.

It is mid-February, nineteen eighty-seven, and the group has asked Q'uo about one of the strangest phrases in the Bible: the mark of the beast.

Q'uo begins with a smile you can hear. This instrument wished us luck, they say, before handing over her voice — and we do feel lucky, to be asked to speak about evil. Because the mark of the beast, Q'uo says, is only a symbol for evil itself. And the mind so often thinks in symbols instead of turning toward the essence of things.

Then Q'uo does something unexpected. They take the number apart — six six six — and walk us through the old numerology. Six is the house of mundane things: money, security, survival. Doubled, it is stronger; tripled, very strong. So the mark of the beast literally reads, Q'uo says, as the things of this world.

But here the talk turns. Lift your thoughts with me, Q'uo says, and look at this world that is supposedly full of the evil of the beast. Here a daisy, there a lark, here a thinking youth, there a smiling woman. These do not look evil. Yet anyone gazing for the beast can find its mark anywhere — because the illusion is yours, and each of you may choose how to interpret what lies before you.

I love how they put it. Describe the same scene one way and it is wonderful; describe it another way and it is terrible. Put a flower in the frame, or put a refuse heap. The choice of symbols is always yours. And the beast is not strong in the one who chooses symbols of the positive to interpret the catalyst of life.

Then comes the line I want to sit with. The essence of the beast lies within each heart and each mind, Q'uo says — and the essence of the beast is the power of denial. Just as the essence of love is the power of acceptance, the essence of evil is the perfect ability to deny what is true and believe what is false.

So it was never really about money. One who looks for advantage at another's expense, Q'uo says, is a far clearer symbol of the beast than any number. Evil has less to do with coins than with the crookedness in how they are gathered, kept, and spent.

There is also a warning here about prophecy itself. The book of Revelation, Q'uo suggests, was largely one man's coded messages to his own people about his own times — and its greatest danger is that it twists the mind to fit its eccentric symbols, keeping seekers from gazing at the essence. Whatever you think about evil, do not let the symbols do your thinking.

And then — because they have been speaking of such a heavy word, a weighty, sad word — Q'uo asks to lighten the meditation. Let us release this question, they say. And let us turn instead to gaze upon the mark of the angels.

What would that be, my children — except a smile. What is the truth and symbol of the truth — except a look of joy. For that which is, is love.

That is where I want to leave you tonight. Not with the beast and its number, but with the simplest possible counter-symbol. A smile. A look of joy. The suggestion that the real mark we carry is the one we choose to wear on the face.

Thank you for listening.

title: Harmonic Resonance
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: harmonic resonance.

Three days later, the intensive meditations continue, and Laitos is back with the two new instruments, W and N. There is a pause in the transcript where the channel simply stops — and when Laitos returns, they explain, with perfect deadpan, that the instrument was being sat upon in a most indelicate manner by a cat. Small paws, readjusted. The evening proceeds.

What I love about this session is how ordinary the holiness is. Laitos is introduced, almost in passing, as the teacher of new instruments — the one the Confederation sends when someone is learning to channel. And the teaching is patient, granular, kind.

One student asks the question every meditator asks: is there a best way to meditate? And Laitos refuses to give one. There is no best way for any particular entity, they say. What matters most is the intention — to offer the self as a receptive instrument to the instreaming of love and light, and to do it regularly. A regular time. A regular place, used for nothing else, so the place itself becomes invested with the intention. A quiet hour. A reasonably straight spine, so the energy can enter easily.

Then adapt everything else to what feels comfortable, Laitos says. The practice must nourish you, not impress anyone.

The other teaching this evening is about something Laitos does when nobody is watching. Besides training channels, they send vibrations of love and light to people on the planet who need them — with no signature, no announcement. Most of the time, Laitos says, the receiving mind never notices at all. The work is done quietly, underneath awareness.

And here is the image that gave this episode its title. A student asks: if I join my own sending of love and light to yours, does it make a difference? Laitos says your sending needs no addition — the conscious intention to give love to another is already, in their words, most propitiously potent. But all such sendings, they say, tend to attract each other like tuned strings, until a harmonic resonance builds up, and the blended sendings rise in frequency together, bathing whoever asked for help in something richer than any one sender could make alone.

Think of that the next time you sit quietly and wish someone well. You are not sending a letter into the dark. You are striking a note, and somewhere, other notes are ringing in sympathy, and the chord is bigger than any of you.

Laitos closes by describing themselves plainly: a fourth-density people, learning the compassion that is their density's great lesson, offering love to whoever calls. Not wise, not finished — just a little further along, reaching back a hand.

Thank you for listening.

title: Food for Growth
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: food for growth.

It is late February, nineteen eighty-seven, and one of the new instruments, W, has come to a painful and very human realization. She has become aware, she says, of a lack of love for herself.

Laitos does not rush to comfort her, and does not rush to fix her either. Instead they offer her a different way of seeing the lack itself. What if the lack of love for self, they suggest, is not a failure but a preparation? As you turn to work on it, you build a stronger framework of the heart — and on that firmer foundation, a greater service to others can eventually stand.

This is the turn I want you to notice, because it runs through the whole evening. Every obstacle, Laitos says, can be seen two ways: as a hindrance to your progress, or as the food for growth — the catalyst which, when processed, transforms the inner being and lets it radiate further.

Then W asks the harder question, the one underneath. When you are in the middle of difficulty — really in it, with everything you have engaged just to survive — where does the concept of letting go come in? Do you stop trying to steer and let the Creator guide instead?

Laitos answers with unusual honesty about how difficulty actually works. In real trouble, they say, you respond spontaneously, unrehearsed, sometimes out of control — and in those raw responses you can see your own limitations laid bare. There comes a point, if the test is true and intense enough, beyond which you have little effect on how things move. And at that point — in meditation, in contemplation, in prayer — it becomes possible to surrender the small view of the conscious mind, with all its analyzing of what to do and not to do, to the greater self. To the higher self. To the guides and the light that surround every seeker.

I love that Laitos does not dress this up. Surrender is not a technique you perform; it is what remains when your own strength runs out and you finally stop pretending it hasn't.

And then, almost as an aside, the physical image that makes the whole teaching land. No muscle, Laitos says — physical, mental, or spiritual — grows stronger through lack of use, but only through greater and greater use. In times of difficulty you are using everything you have. So one may, in truth, rejoice in difficulties. They are the workout. They are the food.

A gentle word, before we close, for anyone listening who recognized themselves in W's question. A lack of love for the self is an achingly common discovery, and it does not mean you are broken. If it feels heavy, you do not have to carry it alone — a trusted friend, a counselor, a quiet conversation with someone who cares can help. The archive's beings speak of this lack as the beginning of work, not its end.

And the smallest practice from tonight: when something in you feels unlovable, try asking what it might be feeding. What muscle is being asked to grow? You may find the obstacle was a doorway all along.

Thank you for listening.

title: Your Own Eden
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: your own eden.

It is the first of March, nineteen eighty-seven, and the group has asked about the story of Adam and Eve. Was it history, they want to know, or is it a story meant to show us something?

Q'uo answers the way Q'uo always answers the biggest questions: by making them bigger. The one who wishes to study creation, they say, may fruitfully study what is called the archetypical mind — the deep treasure house of images that lives in all of us. The creation stories are not about individuals, Q'uo says. They are about archetypes.

And then Q'uo says something so simple it stopped me. Each of you has an Eden. A time of untrammeled, untroubled beauty — a golden time when body and soul and mind and heart felt good, at home, and well. The sun was happy. Even the rain was hardly noticeable.

And then, somehow, through the years, you left the garden. And how alone you feel.

But listen to how Q'uo retells the rest. In the garden there is a second figure — the helper. And then the serpent, which in the old symbolic language is not a villain but the image of wisdom. It is wisdom, Q'uo says, that moves the archetypal man and woman out of unity and into experience. Wisdom individualizes. It is the force that lets the Creator know Itself through beings who have left home.

Which reframes the whole story. The fall is not a punishment; it is a departure with a purpose. And here is the question Q'uo asks that I cannot shake: does not all of your experience as individuals depend almost completely upon the serpent in your lives — those seemingly negative forces that put you outside the garden, where each day has challenges, and it is difficult to feel faith and passion, hope and joy?

Yet when you look back, Q'uo says, is it not in those difficult times outside the garden that you so often see the greatest progress made?

There is one more turn, and it is about simplicity. Q'uo warns the group not to study the archetypes into what they call mental and spiritual indigestion. The most important things to learn, they say, are simple and devoid of the complexity of language — for you seek that which is found in silence and in eternity. The language of the heart shall speak for you in the kingdom you now seek.

Later in the evening Latwii comes through to answer questions, and someone asks the obvious one: are we journeying back toward the garden, or away from it? Latwii's answer is gentle. Your people, they say, are perfecting self-consciousness to the point of choosing the path that leads back to unity — carrying home, with the return, all the experience gathered on the way out. The harvest of the journey is the journey itself, brought back as a gift.

So tonight, if you can, remember your Eden — not to grieve it, but to recognize it. You left so that you could learn what the garden could never teach. And the road home is walked one choice at a time, back toward the unity you never truly left.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Treasure That Knows
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the treasure that knows.

It is early March, nineteen eighty-seven, and a voice the group has not heard in some time is speaking. L/Leema — and the name is chanted, letter by letter, because no ordinary pronunciation will hold it.

L/Leema has come to speak of a kind of gem not found under the earth, a kind of star not found in heaven, a one-of-a-kind item which cannot be purchased. The most beautiful and rare, indeed unique, of all treasures. And then the reveal, which I adore: the treasure that knows it is a treasure. The self-conscious seeking entity. You.

All things are treasures to the Creator, L/Leema says, for all things are of the Creator. But only one kind of created thing is conscious of itself. And here is the strange part — that jewel-like quality is almost impossible to see. Look at the crowded, cluttered lives around you, look at the one living inside your own frame thinking your thoughts, and divinity is nowhere to be found. That is by design.

Why, L/Leema asks — why have you worked so diligently to place yourselves in solitude? Why is the body built to convince you that you are separate? The senses are designed, they say, to show you certain things and let you assume the unseen is not real. Separation is engineered into the vehicle.

And the answer L/Leema offers is one to turn over slowly. If you knew with certainty that all beings are one, the urgency of relationship would collapse. You would not take such care with your words, your motives, your smallest wants and desires. There would be no great activation to improve, harmonize, and coordinate two intertwined lives. Solitude, in other words, is the pressure that makes love necessary.

You have arranged, L/Leema says, to be born into an environment of perceived spiritual hunger — where what you most desire to know is unknowable, and what matters most cannot be had — so that the hunger itself moves you forward, always seeking, gazing into the face of mystery without blinking.

Then comes the image I want to leave with you. Imagine you are a gardener, L/Leema says. You plant and sow, you till and harvest, mostly by rote, without true understanding. But in touching the earth, the plant, the bloom, you touch the creation itself in its divinity. And the creation, which is not self-conscious, does not laugh at you. It feeds you with love. It touches you as you touch it. It blesses you with all of its consciousness — for it does not believe itself to be alone.

Only you believe that. And L/Leema's whole message is an invitation to experiment with breaking the chains of that solitude. Take each step, they say, with the feeling and intention of being one with the Father — whether the way is difficult or smooth. If you interpret the illusion through the eyes of the Father, you shall see a kingdom unavailable to those who see only with the eyes of the world.

Someone in the group asks the obvious, laughing question: if we are divine, how come we screw up all the time? And L/Leema answers that the falling short is itself the mechanism — the frustration draws the self forward, focusing attention, enlarging experience. The missed marks are not the opposite of the treasure. They are how the treasure polishes itself.

Thank you for listening.

title: One Note Among Many
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: one note among many.

Mid-March, nineteen eighty-seven. The question on the table is one of the oldest: do we have spiritual families? Are there groupings of consciousness we incarnate with, again and again — and how would we recognize them?

Q'uo begins with a distinction I found clarifying. The perceived spiritual family, they say, matters far more to us than the absolute one. The tools for working on incarnational life are forged inside the experience — so what you can perceive as spiritually akin to you is what actually enlarges your understanding.

Everyone starts, Q'uo says, with the smallest family: the harvest of second density, one mate and the offspring. That is the archetype printed into the physical vehicle. But across thousands of years of incarnations, patterns of association grow — a vast honeycomb of beings whose memory, could they but see it, includes each other in interlocking networks.

And how do you recognize your people? Not by thought, Q'uo says, but by feeling. Birds of a feather flock together — the comfortable sense that someone's thinking fits with your own. That is the perceived family widening.

But Q'uo keeps widening the frame. The family that may matter most, they suggest, is the family of humankind itself — the one that will one day attempt to form, on this planet, a single social memory complex, a shared mind of love and understanding. Every connection made lovingly and freely draws that future closer.

And then the passage that stopped my breath. If you wish to know your true spiritual family, Q'uo says, walk all the streets, the deserts, the jungles, the battlefields of your world — and know that there is no spirit breathing in physical form that is not your own self. Part of you. Part of creation. Part of the only heaven that is thinkable: the kingdom of wholeness.

The evening's questions wander — someone asks what we look like to Q'uo, and the answer is pure music. We perceive you as a vibration, Q'uo says. A note. Each being a single note among many, and in that note, another part of ourselves, and of the one Creator. I thought of that all week: you, as a note. What note are you sounding today?

Q'uo closes with something practical, almost stern in its gentleness. Meditate daily, they ask — if only for a few minutes. That regular opening, that dependable silence, is all-important. Not to escape the family, but to keep yourself clear enough to do the work you came to do within it.

Think of it as a reunion, Q'uo says, as well as work. The instinct to gather, to network, to find your people — that is the family calling itself back together.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Meditation of the Body
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the meditation of the body.

Mid-March, nineteen eighty-seven, and someone new is speaking. The name comes through as Quanta — and when the group asks about the name, the answer is that it reflects a great leap in conscious awareness, the kind of leap this grouping has taken together.

Who is Quanta? They describe themselves as a beginning social memory complex — a group of beings who have achieved the green-ray vibration of compassion and understanding, newly arrived on this planet from elsewhere, newly joined to the Confederation. They are, in their own lovely phrase, the advance guard: early settlers of the fourth density that is dawning here. And they have come, specifically, to help the group's new instruments learn to channel — to serve as intermediaries between inner-plane contacts and human voices still learning the art.

But before any of that, Quanta offers a teaching, and it is the teaching I want you to carry. They call it the meditation of the body.

Each element, Quanta says, has a rhythm, a dance and a song — a signature pattern running underneath all manifestation. The one who works with natural energy is the one who perceives that dance. Sit on the earth, they say. Preferably in the shade, or in a cave. Let each footstep be a rich experience in the Creator. Meditate briefly on that brother, that sister, that mother and father which is the earth beneath you — showing off, Quanta says, in all of its glory.

Your physical nature speaks to you, they say, with nothing more than dust and nothing less than the Creator. No eagle that ever flew failed to need some tiny piece of earth to sustain life and nurture its young. The body is the first meditation.

And then the geometry. Relationships between two beings, Quanta says, are not horizontal, earth to earth. They rise — from the earth upward to the Creator, back down to the brother or sister, and heart to heart between the two. A triangle. Make that triangle, they say, as tall and thin as possible — until you see each child of earth as a child of the Creator, and each cave not only as earth but as infinite sky, infinite love, infinite light.

There is a small, human moment in the session I want to keep. When Quanta first arrives, the instrument challenges them — demands to know their nature — and Quanta cannot immediately answer, because the challenge is framed in terms this new being does not fully grasp. They have to pause, examine it, set aside what doesn't fit, and answer from the heart of it. Even the teachers, it seems, are still learning the instruments.

Quanta is new here, and says so freely. We are new to this planetary influence, they admit, and will be limited for a time in speaking your language of thought. There is something deeply encouraging about a teacher who begins by saying: we do not know your customs yet, but we have come to learn them alongside you.

Thank you for listening.

title: Roots and Branches
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: roots and branches.

A week later, Quanta is back, settling in with the group — chatting, they say, so the circle can keep tuning. And they begin with a confession that I love: do not mistake us for those who are wise. We are new to love, Quanta says, and do not yet grasp the rudiments of wisdom.

What they offer instead is craft. The evening becomes a master class in the art of channeling — and, underneath it, a teaching about how any of us receive anything true.

First, the pauses. A new channel, Quanta says, hears silence between thoughts and panics, assuming the contact is lost. But the contact speaks in increments, unpredictable ones. The first train of thought carries the basic message — the bones. The next carries the next most central thing — the flesh. And onward, layer by layer, until the message has blood and breath. The experienced channel, Quanta says, simply has the patience to wait for all of it.

I keep thinking about that as a description of listening itself. How much do we lose, in ordinary conversation, by reacting to the first sentence before the second has arrived?

Then Quanta widens it further. There is a channeling process, they say, operating in every conscious entity that wants it — opening the self to the hidden resources of the deeper mind. The same clearing, the same tuning, the same challenging turned inward can make an ordinary speaking person, though conscious, yet also in an augmented state. You do not need a contact from elsewhere to practice this. You only need to become transparent to yourself.

And then the meditation Quanta gives the group — the companion to last week's meditation of the body. Picture the great eagle, they say, soaring into the sky. And then picture the meditation of sky. You who are earthbound must use imagination as eagle's wings, to mount up to the ethers that move forever toward the shining One.

Gaze with the eagle, Quanta says, upon the white heaven that flows endlessly toward the illimitable white light. The air is a clean, sharp river of good — it supports the eagle, never combating it, for the eagle meditates and does not struggle. The eagle soars and moves not one feather, but only gazes, and sees, and acknowledges.

One of the students, W, asks about the relationship between the two meditations — the cave of the body and the sky of the eagle. And Quanta answers: it is balance. The grounding must be balanced with the opening to infinity. Build the foundation within, and the expression can stand stable upon it.

W puts it perfectly, in her own words: so what you're saying is, as you grow roots, you can also grow branches. Yes, Quanta says. This is correct.

Roots and branches. The body and the sky. The bones of the message and its living blood. Tonight's teaching is that nothing true arrives all at once — it arrives the way a tree grows, and the way an eagle flies: patiently, and without struggle.

Thank you for listening.

title: After the Honeymoon
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: after the honeymoon.

Late March, nineteen eighty-seven, and the group has brought Q'uo two questions that turn out to be one question. The first: how do you know when there is still enough love — enough reason — to stay with a partner? The second: is Christianity helping or hindering the planet's movement into a new age? And Q'uo's first move is to fold them together. Are not both queries concerning relationships?

What follows is one of the most psychologically astute things I have heard in this archive. Q'uo speaks of the illness and the health of relationships — and begins, beautifully, in spring. When two entities become mated, the landscape seems beautiful, prospects unlimited, all of life as pleasant as sunshine on young leaves, forsythia and daffodil greeting the spring breeze.

The same is true, Q'uo says, when you wed yourself to a religion. There is a mating between the seeker and the face of the Creator as a particular path reveals it. And a honeymoon ensues — all that is good shared freely, the self forgotten in some realization of the holy in the other.

And then, inevitably as winter follows summer, the honeymoon ends. Two people finish the celebration and embark on some challenge, together or apart. The seeker on an orthodox path finds doubts so overwhelming they cloud the whole relationship with the organization. In both cases, Q'uo says, attention turns outward — blame the partner, blame the church — and the attempt begins to repair, mend, or replace the ailing bond.

Here is the sentence I underlined twice. In any relationship which a seeker has with anyone or anything, the fundamental dynamic in the relationship, as concerns this entity, is the entity itself.

Q'uo lays out three options for the disillusioned. The first is the most common: avoid the pain, leave, find a new relationship — which will, in time, disillusion you again, for it is the nature of the illusion that all things pass. The second: endure doggedly without thought, trusting the night will become day. The third — the one Q'uo recommends — is to withdraw for a time from decision and from company, into personal, intimate, extremely private contemplation.

Because here is what is really happening, Q'uo says. All the good and all the difficult things have been offered to you by yourself — by the deeper self that planned this incarnation — not to endure or avoid, but to learn from. And that learning cannot happen while you are busy reacting to the catalyst. There is no time when meditation is not helpful, but when you need to know where right action lies, go deep within, in faith, and wait for the still, small voice to surface.

The most difficult thing for the seeker, Q'uo says, is simply to wait. To wait for clarity to come. Clarity can come from within, yet not from without.

And if the waiting brings you into what Q'uo calls the desert experience — deprivation, want, pain, sadness, loss, disillusionment — do not take the desert for reality. It is illusion, just as the peaceful times are illusion. Trust it the way you trust winter: the desert shall give way again to plenty and peace.

The closing counsel is plain and hard. You will reach the new age, Q'uo says, when your criticisms are only of yourself, when you act because within you feel it right for you alone, and when the opinion of others is nothing more than interesting. Seek to know yourself more and more, to be yourself more and more — and let your will, your faith, your love, and your attention rest in the silence within.

Thank you for listening.

title: Beyond the Rational
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: beyond the rational.

Early April, nineteen eighty-seven. The question comes from Carla, the group's own channel, and it is personal: she lives with physical limits, and she wants to know how to tell the difference between pushing herself enough to stay positive — and pushing so far she does herself harm.

Q'uo answers with a frog.

If you have a frog in a lily pond, Q'uo says, and you encourage it to jump to another lily pad, the frog either can make it or it cannot. There are limits the frog knows in its small mind. There is a safe distance — and then there is the border, the space at the edge of ability that willpower might just cross. But notice, Q'uo says: the frog has no moral argument with its limits. It does not bargain with the Creator about the spacing of the lily pads.

We are not frogs. The self-conscious entity, Q'uo says, has many tools — and many trials that no rational point of view can resolve. That is where discernment and judgment take their place beside prudence, all of them in service to something deeper: constant, daily, disciplined communication between the human and the Creator.

And then the line that named this episode. Logic, Q'uo says, will not open this particular tin of sardines. Packed neatly though the arguments be, you must seek beyond the rational — in the land of mystery and hunch — where the greater portion of yourself, which is the Creator, knows far more than the conscious mind could ever produce.

I want to be careful with this teaching, because it touches health, and the archive is not a doctor. Q'uo is not prescribing a treatment here. They are describing a relationship — between the small self that calculates and the larger Self that knows — and suggesting that the question of how far to push is finally answered in meditation, not in arithmetic.

There is a second image I love. Like a tree growing at the edge of a forest, Q'uo says, the person who steps a little beyond what others do becomes visible, separate — no longer of the forest but at its edge, in pasture land. People watch. They expect vigor. And that expectation, Q'uo warns, can distort the whole question, pulling you away from the will of the Creator and toward the will of the audience.

Whether you press hard or accept with grace, Q'uo says, what makes the life valuable is the offering of the self in thanksgiving. Do not regret any portion of what occurs. Go into meditation, and wait in hope and faith, alert for the call that may seem like nothing — a small sound, a slight movement — yet subjectively is everything.

The closing counsel is a small paradox to carry: let the courageous become more sensible, and let the over-prudent go forth rejoicing in an abandon long denied. Twin values, Q'uo says, are sometimes antithetical — and the wise seeker honors both.

A gentle note, since this session brushes against grief as well — Carla speaks here of her beloved companion Don, gone two years, and the sadness that still visits her. If you are carrying a loss that will not set down, be patient with the weight. Grief has its own lily pads, its own safe distances. You do not have to jump further than you can.

Thank you for listening.

title: More Real Than the Illusion
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: more real than the illusion.

Mid-April, nineteen eighty-seven. The question is large and a little frightened: as the harvest approaches — as difficult times come with it — how can each person be of service to others, and still walk their own path?

Q'uo answers in two movements, and the first is about what is real.

Each of you wakes and sleeps, they begin. Waking life is called reality; dreams are called illusion. But from the metaphysical standpoint, Q'uo says, it is hard to say which is richer — for both are portions of a greater illusion enfolding you. The physical world seems so regular, so solid, that you allow yourself to be less real than the world around you.

Then the turn. Growth, Q'uo says, does not lie in reacting to the circumstances around you, but in becoming more real than the illusion you see all about you.

Why are you more real than the rest of it? Because consciousness itself is the original Thought of love — the Logos — dwelling within you, speaking subjectively to your awareness. The source of reality must lie within the self, Q'uo says, because reality is subjective, as consciousness is subjective.

And here is the image I cannot forget. Without the pilgrim's awareness, Q'uo says, you sit in the audience — reacting, laughing and crying as the scenes pass and the flat painted scenery slides up and down. But the one who remembers becomes something else: an actor, a dramatist, and a critic. Not swept by the play, but awake inside it.

The second movement is about service in hard times. Q'uo does not offer strategy. They offer presence. In the difficult days to come, they say, people will remember the one who smiled — the one who exhibited the lively grace of peace and joy. Simple lovingness, Q'uo says, is perhaps the greatest gift one being can give another.

So the counsel for harvesters in the valley of the shadow is startling: behave, within limits, as you would if there were no valley, no shadow, and no death — for all these are illusions, and only beingness actually exists. Your eyes, your mouth, your hands manifest that beingness to others. Every look, every smile, every word and touch carries the thread of consciousness singing its true song between two people.

And in the sensitive one — the one ready to be harvested — that simple song, Q'uo says, shall be the gift of infinite meaning. Too dear for any price.

Meditate, then. Find the center. And be who you are. The rest, Q'uo promises, shall occur one moment at a time.

Look upon all things spiritually, they say in closing — which is to say, without prejudice and with humor. For if consciousness delights in one thing, it is itself.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Windows of Opportunity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the windows of opportunity.

Mid-April, nineteen eighty-seven. Quanta — the new fourth-density group-mind, still learning Earth's customs — is taking questions. And the questions this evening turn out to be about knowledge itself: how it is stored, how it is reached, and what it is worth.

Carla asks how the group mind forms. Is it a hierarchy — individual minds, then the racial mind, then the planetary mind? Quanta's answer is patient and precise. Each entity, they say, records its significant experience in its own conscious and subconscious mind. Those roots reach down and harmonize with like minds — the cultural mind, the racial mind, groupings by philosophy or geography — and those serve as reservoirs between the individual and the planetary mind: the great storehouse many call the Akashic record.

That record, Quanta says, will one day open to all of fourth density as their ancient heritage. Imagine that: the whole history of a planet's seeking, available as inheritance.

Then W asks about something she heard from another channel — the Wesak moons, times when the new moon acts as a mirror, reflecting greater energy from the source to the planet. Quanta admits they know nothing of Earth's festivals. But the principle, they say, they do understand.

There are alignments, Quanta says — of planetary and celestial influences — that provide windows of opportunity for the seeker. It is as though the student's efforts are increased by a lever: at certain moments, the alert and persevering seeker may experience a heightened perception of the art they seek to master.

And then the sentence that gave this episode its title, and its warning. With greater opportunity, Quanta says, comes the balance of a greater responsibility to use it along the chosen path. The magnification cuts both ways. Power borrowed from the alignment must be spent purely — or not at all.

W asks, practically, what she should do to prepare for the contact seeking her. And Quanta's answer is almost disappointingly simple: persevere. Keep the daily meditation. Do not chase additional sittings to force a contact; let the calming of the conscious mind be the goal. The foundation first, then the meeting.

And then — the tape gives us a gift. A new voice barrels through Carla, mangling its consonants, laughing at itself, refusing to behave. This is Yadda, and Yadda has come to speak about skepticism.

Open your eyes, Yadda says. What do you know? You know nothing! Look at a tree. You see root, bark, branches, bird's nest — and leaves! But tell me how it grew there. Tell me how it began. Tell me anything about the tree except its name and its location. Nothing!
