So what is there not to be skeptical about? Everything, Yadda cackles. You have to name names and pretend you know things. But inside — what are you going to take?

And then the punchline, delivered like a bell. What you believe is far more important than what you know — because you don't know anything. So tell me: what do you believe in? How do you declare yourself? We say one word, Yadda says. Love!

We believe in love, Yadda says, for it created us and all that there is. What do you have to say to that? We can never ask a more basic metaphysical question.

Two teachings, one evening. Quanta: the universe keeps its records, and its windows open on schedule — be ready, be responsible. Yadda: you know nothing anyway, so choose what you believe, and let it be love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Walking Tomb
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the walking tomb.

It is mid-April, nineteen eighty-seven — Easter season — and Hatonn opens with the Easter greeting. The group's question is humble and modern: the world is too much with us. The daily routine, plus a few added difficulties, feels like a heavier and heavier burden on the shoulders. How should we look at it? What is the most effective attitude?

Hatonn answers by taking us, in mind, to a grave.

Come to the cold gray dawn of a desert morning, Hatonn says. Three women who love the newly killed Jesus come to the tomb, seeking the beloved body. Mary the mother is frantic. Mary Magdalene weeps. Their focus is upon the tomb — and not upon that which is there no more.

And here is the turn, aimed straight at our busy lives. When you become too close to the things you love and wish to care for, Hatonn says, your focus shifts. You stop gazing at the living spirit, the breathing fire of what you care for — and you gaze instead at the dead and life-deadening structure it lives in. The tomb. The house. The husk.

To be more specific and more universal at once: each of you dwells within a walking tomb. The physical body — chemical life, growing up and dying away, in a cosmic sense almost too quickly to be noticed. Each of you is but a breath upon the wind, and then dust.

But — and this is the Easter in the teaching — there is great life and great beauty and great joy in that which is alive inside every structure. Hatonn is careful to say they do not recommend harsh asceticism, the punishing of earthly joy. In the most mundane thing, they say, there is a living atom of the consciousness of love, and its value is infinite. In every step, every thought, every word spoken, the living fire of creation moves, creating in each entity a newness of life and love and strength. You cannot do yourselves ultimate harm, no matter how confused or miserable you may feel. The process can be slowed, Hatonn says. It cannot be stopped.

The practice Hatonn offers is a change of gaze. Look at your day and ask of each concern: which is the living, breathing source of joy — and which is the whited sepulcher, the open grave? You may look at an old house, Hatonn says, and see only all that needs doing. The house has become a tomb. Or you may look at the same house and ask it: house, which has borne my love, my grief, and my passion — tell me, what would you have me do for you this day?

Ask the angel within, the spirit of life: what shall the day bring? And the same routine that once cursed and narrowed the mind becomes blessed.

There is one tomb Hatonn names directly, and I will name it gently: the mystery of illness and death. Each of you, breathing the breath of life, breathes also the faint musty odor of the tomb. Do you identify yourself with the tomb? Your identity, Hatonn says, lies within consciousness. That which is given you shall never be taken away. You have been, and you will be.

So that is how you remove the busyness from the mind, Hatonn says. Think of yourself without your tomb. Put in perspective that which lasts and that which does not — and encourage one another in love, for your consciousnesses are made of that creative and glorious substance.

Later, Latwii comes through for questions, and echoes the same teaching in plainer words: step back, in meditation, and take the larger and longer view — all portions of the incarnation as one pattern, teaching service, dedication, perseverance, and the loving of what seems unlovable in yourself and others.

The tomb is not the risen source of joy, Hatonn says. That which is alive goes before you, drawing you onward. Walk toward it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Five Minutes a Day
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: five minutes a day.

Late April, nineteen eighty-seven. A short session — one of the briefest in this whole stretch of the archive — and Laitos uses it the way a good teacher uses a short class: one subject, driven home.

The subject is the excellence of meditation. And the teaching begins with permission, not pressure.

If only for five minutes in any day, Laitos says, it is well to meditate that much — rather than go through an entire day without acknowledging the Source of your energy and love, and centering yourself in that clarified energy.

Five minutes. Not an hour, not a retreat, not perfection. Laitos is explicit: do not judge the excellence of individual sittings. Do not attach great importance even to the time spent. When the desire is ripe, the attention will be there, and progress will be made. What matters is the daily-ness — the discipline of returning, if only briefly, to the greater Self.

Because here is what the daily return is for. Spiritual seasons are very definite, Laitos says — and the soul that blooms continuously is rare indeed. In any incarnation there are relatively few moments when a great transformation is possible, when the season of change arrives. It is the one who watches and waits daily, Laitos says, for whom that season will not come and go unnoticed, unheeded, unused.

I love the practicality tucked inside the mysticism. Marry meditation to a walk in the natural world, Laitos suggests — forest, stream, meadow — and let the inner self be fed, in this instrument's phrase, from streams of living water.

And then Laitos widens the lens one final time, with a sentence I have been carrying all week. The practice of channeling, they say, is only a specialized form of something general — for is not each a channel in every thought, idea, emotion, and speech which it makes? Is each entity not always a channel — either for love and light, or for some darker force of separation?

There are some who wish not to be channels at all, Laitos says, but to deaden the senses — and to those, they say with surprising gentleness: sleep, and be comfortable, for there is an infinite amount of time.

But to those who wish to progress — to you, listening to this now — Laitos says: we rejoice with you, and would speak with you about love.

Five minutes. A straight spine, a quiet room, a walk among trees. The season is coming whether you watch for it or not. Watch for it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Doorkeeper
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the doorkeeper.

Late April, nineteen eighty-seven. The topic for the evening is a single word: patience. Latwii says there are those in the group's wider circle who need to hear about it — and asks that the recording be sent to one of them.

Latwii begins where every spiritual seeker actually lives. At first, the path is thrilling — each step begins and ends in a perfect pattern, the heart full of peace. But the path, Latwii says, is steep and stony in places, and sometimes it disappears entirely into a swale of mud, overgrown, while the heartbeat of earthly life goes thudding on.

Soon the seeker cannot see the path at all. And then comes impatience — first with the mundane concerns that steal time from spiritual things, then with the self for being impatient, and finally, the longest stage of all: impatience with the Creator for making such an imperfect universe.

Latwii walks us through each stage the way a friend would — no scolding. The seeker at war with the self, they say, should note the mistake, correct what can be corrected, and move on. No progress is ever made by one at war with the self.

And then the teaching turns, and turns beautifully. Patience, Latwii says, is an infinite part of that infinite Thought which created all that there is — for the infinite intelligence which is love cannot experience impatience. All times are the present time. All places are the present place. All things are one thing.

It is we — self-conscious co-creators — who distort unity into hurry. So here is Latwii's redefinition, the one I want you to keep: true patience is not that which waits, but rather that which bides endlessly.

Patience, they say, is a portion of love hidden in the deep beingness of mind — below the senses, below thought — creating each experience that manifests through you. It is a resource. Part of the glory within.

And then the image that named this episode. There is, Latwii says, an inner opening to infinity — and patience is the doorkeeper.

What does the doorkeeper ask of you? Only this: that you give each moment its full due. When Carla presses Latwii — is patience just being in the present moment? — Latwii says yes, and more. To so fully accept the present experience that you are full of it, with little concern for what came before or what follows — that the moment is sufficient unto itself — is to have a kind of love for the Creator that we have called patience.

Difficult experiences, Latwii says — the relationships, the situations that chafe — are designed to place the pilgrim exactly where it needs to be, to work on the unbalanced places in the personality. To be impatient with the world for making you sad or angry or defeated is, in the end, to be impatient with yourself.

So meditate, Latwii says, when impatience starts stealing your joy. Manifest peace, serenity, patience — and sunshine will spring from your eyes regardless of the external weather. Then you become a blessing to all whom you see.

Latwii closes the way Latwii always closes: with mischief barely contained. We are attempting, they say, to keep our sense of humor to a manageable quota — but our hearts are full of glee at being with you, and we almost dance as we speak.

Be patient, my friend, they say. Be patient. The doorkeeper is already holding the door.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Seasons of the Soul
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the seasons of the soul.

Early May, nineteen eighty-seven. The question is one every seeker has asked in the dark: when have I tried to control things long enough? When do I stop steering — stop managing my own evolution, my relationships, my life — and surrender to the flow of the moment?

Q'uo answers with the seasons.

Look at the trees, they say. To the tree, the question of control is meaningless. It moves wildly from fullness through dying to stark skeletal nakedness, and then — when warm weather coaxes buds from dead wood — to new life again. Each season arrives with its own reality, and each one feels, while you are inside it, as though it will last forever. So it is with summer's heat and winter's cold. So it is, Q'uo says, with the seasons of a human life.

But you are not a tree. You are a co-creator, conscious, choosing — caught between the thoughtlessness of second density and the clear intuition of fourth. You seek, Q'uo says, very much in the dark.

What lights the dark, for Q'uo, is a faculty they describe with unusual vividness: the intuition. The heart. What this instrument calls the gut — the stomach of the mind. That which feels rather than thinks. When the shallow, prurient feelings are skimmed off, Q'uo says, this faculty is extremely useful for the making of choices. Those in fourth density, they add, use almost nothing else.

And here is the practice. Begin, Q'uo says, by simply observing the feeling tones. Discover what season you are in. Is this a morning for you, or the dark of the night? At first the observation bewilders. But after a few months of care, a pattern appears — an ebb and flow — and you begin to see the true signs of the seasons, and of their changing.

Your responsibility, as Q'uo frames it, is modest and profound: soften the blow of the wintry times, and celebrate and share the seasons that are blooming and bursting with fruit. Allow the flow of events to guide you — excellent advice. Use more discipline and meditate more — also excellent advice. Both are true, Q'uo says, each in its season.

The deeper question underneath is trust. Do you trust the Creator — and yourself as part of the Creator — to know what is needed at the present moment, better than any outside source, including us?

There is a late exchange in the session I want to keep, because it names the trap precisely. Carla asks about desire itself — isn't wanting the fruits of meditation just another form of control? And Q'uo agrees the line is fine. The counsel: harness desire so that you offer yourself completely to that which is appropriate — without fashioning a goal, an idol, of the mind. Desire the seeking, not the prize.

Q'uo closes with an image for the road. Borne upon the water of the spirit, they say, the frail barks of humankind sail about — some with rudders, some without — in search of many grails, many islands, many native homes. To each, their own journey.

Notice your season tonight. Name it, the way you would name the weather. And then — rudder or no rudder — let the water carry you a while.

Thank you for listening.

title: Thoughts Not Yet Thought
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: thoughts not yet thought.

Early May, nineteen eighty-seven. A brief session, and Laitos speaks like a coach at the edge of the field — because one of the new instruments, N, is about to graduate.

Here is how Laitos describes the stages. When the seeker is new, everything arrives mixed: the present moment overlaid with worries about the future and disturbances from the past. Seldom is the consciousness a clear mirror of what is actually occurring. So with channeling — first, the mechanics must be learned. The contact must be made comfortable and stable. There is much training, and it is largely specific.

Then comes the moment N is facing now. The technique is basically learned. And now it is time to open the self to new thoughts — and to the potential, subjectively speaking, for disaster. For how, Laitos asks, can one speak thoughts which one has not yet thought?

I love that question, because it is not really about channeling. It is about every act of real thinking — every sentence you have ever begun without knowing its end. The fear of being a fool, Laitos says, keeps the magic at bay.

The counsel is precise: analyze before and after each sitting, but refrain from analysis during. Prepare the mind, then get out of its way. Trust that there are thoughts to give from the first thought to the last — and that they will ring, Laitos says, with the one truth they have to offer: that all of creation is one thing, one great Thought thinking itself out in infinite portions.

Then N asks a question I want to handle carefully, because it concerns mind-altering substances — whether they can help break down the barriers and show you more of yourself.

Laitos answers with unusual gravity. It is true, they say, that such substances can expand the point of view. But for most people the effect is random — the barriers that hold the mind within its boundaries are hard to affect with precision, and the groundwork of attitude and setting is rarely solid enough to support the energies released. What follows varies wildly in value.

There is, Laitos says, a rhythm to each student's evolution — a song unique to each. There are times the melody quickens and times it slows, and the quickenings arrive as the student learns to use ordinary catalyst well. To jump ahead and seize an acceleration you have not prepared for is a risk: the opportunity is real, but so is the randomness, and the student who can use such substances in a truly disciplined, consecrated way is rare.

So it is not their recommendation. The steady road — the daily meditation, the honest use of difficulty — remains, in their view, the safer and surer way to widen.

A gentle word from me, not from the archive: if you are curious about these substances, please be careful with yourself. The archive's beings are not physicians, and neither am I. What they describe as randomness, human researchers describe as real risk — to mind, to body, to the life you are building. There are steadier doors, and they open from the inside.

And the practice from tonight belongs to anyone who has ever been afraid to speak before knowing: prepare well, and then — during — do not analyze. Let the unthought thought arrive. It knows the way.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Work Is the Life
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the work is the life.

Mid-May, nineteen eighty-seven — and the transcript carries a small note at the top: happy birthday, Jim. The question for the evening is one that has quietly tortured every ambitious seeker: what is the lesson when you pour years of effort into a goal and the goal stays unattainable?

Q'uo begins by questioning the question. Your peoples, they say, assume that something smaller than the life itself is the work — usually, whatever is done in exchange for money. Everything else is training, prelude, waiting for the real thing to start. Such, Q'uo says, is the distortion which money has created.

Then the redefinition, which I want to read to you slowly. It is our opinion, Q'uo says — and we stress that it is opinion only — that the only work which may be called the Work of any entity is that work done in consciousness during an incarnation which polarizes the entity more and more strongly toward service to the Creator and to others.

Thus, life is the work, and work is the life.

If that is true, the whole arithmetic of success and failure changes. Whether the outer outcome was expected or unexpected, Q'uo says, the actual work lay not in results but in the attitudes and biases gained along the way — and that process goes on regardless of apparent success or apparent failure.

Q'uo reaches for an image: the crystallization of the personality. As the seeker regularizes thoughts, desires, actions, and words — focusing them toward service — the energy centers become like a crystal, Q'uo says, accepting the white light of the Creator and refracting it in balanced fashion, each center lending its color, yielding the white light again. The goal you missed may have been the furnace in which the crystal was forming.

There is a passage here about suffering that I want to offer gently, because the evening turns personal. Carla speaks of her grief — her beloved companion Don, dead two years, in circumstances that still haunt her. She wonders if there is intrinsic value in the suffering she still carries, even amid wedding joy.

Q'uo answers: have you not produced a fruit from the suffering? Can this not nourish others? Within each moment of suffering, they say, exists the one Creator, whole and perfect — and as the sufferer discovers joy inside the pain, another veil lifts from inner and outer eyes.

I will add only this, in my own voice: grief is not a problem the archive asks you to solve. If you are carrying a loss that will not set down — as Carla was — be as patient with it as you would be with a friend. The teaching here is not that suffering is good, but that nothing in it is wasted. If the weight feels too heavy to carry alone, let someone help you carry it.

Q'uo's closing movement is one of the most beautiful in this whole stretch of the archive. The development of personality, they say, moves from the surface of things deeper and deeper — until finally the seeking and the sought become one. So that you are not meditating, but finally you are the meditation. And this meditation is your perfect poem, your arrangement of your consciousness — and you know in an instant that this consciousness is the gift you shall give to the Creator.

And so, Q'uo says, you can no longer feel unsuccessful.

Seek, my children, seek always. Have an inner life completely independent of outer circumstance. Remain faithful to the seeking through every difficult patch — for under the velvet, Q'uo says, the will is being given its strength.

The goal you did not reach was never the work. You were the work, all along.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Celestial Flowers
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the celestial flowers.

Quanta, a voice the group was still learning to hear, spoke of meditation as a kind of gravity. Settle into it, they said, and you become like a sun.

Listen to how they put it. Across the infinite expanse of interstellar space lies strewn the Creator's field of celestial flowers, the seeds of consciousness. Each sun, held in perfect stasis while constantly moving, washes with its light all the beings that dwell upon its planets. And within each being, small and large thoughts spin off and rotate like planets about a sun.

That is us, Quanta said. The entity whose mind is in balance is sustained and sustaining, just as is the sun. Held in place and holding in place by its planets, the thoughts, the children of its love. I love that line. Our thoughts are the children of our love. They orbit us the way planets orbit a sun, and the question of balance is not whether we think, but whether we hold our thoughts or our thoughts hold us.

For when the mind is not in balance, Quanta said, then do the thoughts become confused and go awry, for the Creator's hand is not in the midst of them. And the creator in question is your own consciousness. When that which has been created achieves ascendancy over the Creator, then are things truly out of balance. It is a strange and gentle diagnosis. Nothing outside you is blamed. Only the inner order has slipped, the way planets would scatter if the sun forgot its place.

The remedy is older than all of us. How blessed it is, they said, to seek the balance of love and light in daily meditation, for meditation is a wellspring of balance, light and love. Not a technique for emptying the mind or winning some prize of stillness, but a wellspring. You sit down beside it every day, and it gives you what it gives.

There was a question that evening about guides and the higher self, asked by one of the newer instruments, who said she had yet to feel truly connected to them. Quanta's answer is one of my favorites in the whole archive. The contact is always available, they said. But the conscious efforts of the seeker to establish a mystery-filled contact are often the primary obstacles to the accomplishment of that contact.

Read that twice, because it stings a little. The harder we grasp at the connection, the more our grasping gets in the way. Instead, they suggested the calm and peaceful relaxation into the knowledge that such contact is always available, and need not demonstrate itself in any fashion which is consciously perceivable. You do not have to feel the guides to be held by them. The sun does not ask its planets to announce their orbits.

And there is a final image from that night worth keeping in the pocket. The outer life and the inner life, Quanta said, need the same relationship that the Earth and the sun share. If either dominates, the balance is disrupted. Meditation is the daily practice of quietly sitting with the inner sanctuary of the spirit, not as an escape from the outer world, but as the thing that lets outer and inner coexist at all.

So tonight, if you meditate, think of yourself less as a seeker hunting for light and more as a sun already burning. The thoughts will come. They will orbit. Some will wobble, and that is what thoughts do. Your work is the older and simpler one: hold your place, and hold them in love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Electrical Desire
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: electrical desire.

Someone asked Q'uo what electricity is, and what came back is one of the strangest and most beautiful answers in the whole archive. Electricity, they said, is one manifestation of the love of the infinite Creator. One might perhaps think of it as electrical desire.

Let that land for a moment. Not a force to be exploited, though many would like to exploit it. A current of desire running through everything, the way the Creator has drawn forth the created universe from what was not yet articulate at the beginning of this creation. Love, bonded in passion to light, so that sense could form of what was before made of no consciousness. That is their account of what a current is.

Q'uo said it plainly and thrice over. Metaphysically speaking, that which is creative is that which has electricity. That which is creative is that which shapes. That which is creative is that which empowers. So wherever you find shaping and empowering, the creative act, there electricity is, whether or not a wire is involved.

Then they turned it inward, and this is where the session becomes something you can practice. A seeker, they said, can work in meditation with one galvanizing image, held with fixed intensity. Visualize something electrifying and exciting, something evocative of all that is best and highest in your life so far, and hold it until the mind tires. Practice lengthens the hold. And what the practice yields, when the focus has been sharply drawn, is what some have called the vitality of the life experience, the joy of living. Each moment seen with new eyes. Each moment felt with new sensation.

I am moved by how ordinary this is made to sound. No ritual, no special posture. Just one image you love, held until it hums.

The night closed with a passage that is practically a benediction. Whatever this day has been, Q'uo said, it is what you have made it. Whatever this night brings to you is brought to you as a favor to yourself by yourself. All is desire and the fulfillment of desire, and the more that desire is carefully considered and single-heartedly placed, the more the life experience will be heartfelt, single-minded, glad and productive.

This is not blame. It is not the claim that every misfortune is your fault. It is something larger and kinder: the claim that you are not a thing that things happen to. When a seeker views the self as one acted upon by circumstance, Q'uo said, one then sees the self lying down before the electricity of experience and having that experience burned into the self. But human desire, they said, has the strongest electricity available on this planet. The will, the heart, the soul of humankind is far more powerful than any problem.

May you become more and more imbued, they said, with the sense that electrically and creatively you shall happen to your environment and to those circumstances which greet you. Let you be the actor which decides what part to play, not one which hurriedly makes entrances and exits without ever quite learning the lines. See yourself as powerful in love and light.

Tonight, then: see yourself as powerful in love and light. Not as a wish. As a description of what is already true.

Thank you for listening.

title: Rough Diamonds
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: rough diamonds.

Quanta had been speaking of the dark earth, groping in the darkness of thoughts and mundane concerns, trying to see through thick darkness the outlines of eternity. Then they said a startling thing: though we are just a bit further along the road than are you, still we feel like rough diamonds indeed.

Rough diamonds. Not finished gems. Rough. And they asked the group to hold that image, because that spark, that light, that fire which has brought forth shape, substance, form and particularity brings forth now each of you. And each of you must then attempt to become gemlike and crystalline, that you may trap light, increase it, divert it, and become reflective illuminations of gathered light.

I love this because it is not a demand for perfection. It is a direction. A rough diamond is still a diamond. The work is to let more light in and let more light out, until the sparks keep shining out of each entity's eyes, so that those still truly in the darkness of earth and mundane affairs may see that there is joy and peace bubbling forth from the face of those who seek the light and the love of the one Creator.

You are part of the spark of the divine, they said. You are the Creator to those whom you meet and greet and speak with. Not you will become. You are. Tonight, in the rough, you are already someone's evidence that the light exists.

Much of the rest of that evening was questions from a new instrument, and the answers are quietly practical. Someone asked whether her daily work, serving tables in a restaurant, was part of some larger plan or merely a way to make a living. Quanta answered that there are no portions of any conscious seeker's life experience which are not significant portions of the incarnational plan. Each experience and encounter contains the seeds of a garden planned carefully aforetimes, and who can say when any seed shall be nourished sufficiently to take root.

So look at each moment, they said, as that which is precious and sacred and designed to provide you the perfect opportunity for your own growth and your service to others. The shift change. The tired feet. The difficult feelings that surface when old patterns loosen. All of it, garden soil.

And for the difficult feelings, they offered a technique so gentle it deserves to be quoted slowly. Take the hard feeling with you into the meditative state and enhance it until it becomes large, large enough to draw to it its opposite. Within this balance may then lie acceptance of oneself, for allowing the Creator to experience itself through one's feelings, thoughts and actions.

Magnify the feeling, do not suppress it, and let it call its own opposite out of the dark. Balance is not the removal of the shadow. It is the shadow standing next to the light, the diamond holding both.

The last question of the night was whether the pursuit of channeling itself could distract from the spiritual path. Quanta refused to decide anyone's fate, and said instead: the seeker who travels the trail most efficiently is one who moves with the lightest of touches, and does not feel overattached to any portion of the creation. Give each portion its due and move further onward.

Light of touch. Rough of diamond. Full of spark. That is the whole of it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Path of That Which Is
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the path of that which is.

This is a tender episode. The session opened with a question about why thoughts of death and suicide have been visiting so many minds, and Q'uo answered with unusual gentleness. If thoughts like these visit you, please tell someone you trust, and consider speaking with a professional listener too. The archive is old wisdom, not medicine, and what follows is reflection, not guidance.

Q'uo described two paths that run through everything. The way of that which is, the path of the positive polarity, which grows, expands and develops. And the path of that which is not, which seemingly dies, which is the grand illusion of death and separation. Both paths, they said, reach the same Creator. But the question of a life is always which path the mind is walking today.

The body, they said, is by definition both positive and negative in polarization. It grows and it ages, and as the vehicle participates more and more in that grand illusion of separation, the mind receives echoes. Thoughts about the logical end of small frailties begin to visit. Woes that once were merely dealt with as situations now take their toll. This is why, Q'uo said, it is good to stress the precious nature of positive affirmation, more than ever before.

Then came the image at the center of the whole teaching. Look at your consciousness with a cold eye, in the abstract, and you shall see at the heart a gem, invisible except by faith, surrounded by the rough shape of the unhewn, unfaceted stone. The crystal qualities are there, but they lie waiting for the skilled hand of the artisan to chip and facet until the heart of the stone is revealed in all its polished splendor.

And here is the line I want everyone to hear. Failure, my children, is completely irrelevant to the value of your attempt. Much of what you attempt will be attempted in such a way that failure is inevitable, for reasons you cannot see. Yet that which has occurred within the mind will live, and will be your new personality, as you gather yourself together again for further experience along the infinite road to the face of the Creator.

Failure is irrelevant to the value of the attempt. The attempt is the thing. The trying is the gem being faceted.

On the specific question of taking one's own life, Q'uo declined to give a simple rule, which itself says something. What matters, they said, is not any one act but the building of momentum, the biasing of the soul toward separation or toward love. And yet they made a distinction that is worth sitting with. The giving of the life for others, the laying down of one's life in service, partakes of the path of that which is. What makes any act heavy is not the act but the inward embrace of separation, the turning away from the Creator and from each other.

That is all I will say about that portion. The teaching, like the question, deserves more silence than words.

The evening turned at last to healing, and to what a healer must learn. The simplest healing, Q'uo said, is sharing. The entity with the difficulty is assured, at the most basic of levels, that it is acceptable to another and that another cares. And the one who would become a healer in truth must learn to give without condition and to see the one in need as whole and perfect, given over to the greater forces for the appropriate action. To give, and to take nothing on.

And beneath it all, the same quiet promise. The fire that lies within you can never be touched, can never be altered, but can only be eventually found, because you have honed the personality until it is brilliant and clear, and the properties of the crystal are yours. Then may you carry light, as the Creator is Light.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Covenant of Two
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the covenant of two.

The group asked Q'uo about the metaphysical meaning of marriage, and the answer begins with a definition so clean it could be carved in stone. A covenant, they said, is a promise made by two people to each other for a specified span of time and with specified conditions. Your marriage is such a promise. And a promise may be compared to a journey.

One who has no clear goal makes an aimless trip and learns many interesting things and grows from the experience. There is grace and beauty to all that happens, the traveler may be pleased, yet somehow disappointed, without being able to put a finger on the source of the disappointment. But the seeker who thought quietly before setting out, and set for himself conditions and goals, gives the journey structure and a summit, a place which, having been reached, serves as a marvelous foundation from which to look back and gather the meaning of all that came before.

Marriage, seen this way, is a destination agreed upon before the walking begins. The promises are to honor, cherish, serve and love under any conditions whatsoever, which makes the marriage ceremony, metaphysically speaking, among the most stringent possible promises. And those who prepare by visualizing and accepting the better and the worse, the balance of all things which shall come after the promise is given, are doing the real work of the ceremony before it is ever spoken.

Then Q'uo said something I have turned over many times since reading it. Those who do not marry and seek together, seek alone for the face of love. Those who seek through the covenant of marriage incorporate that which they seek into their seeking. There is a third party in every true covenant, overshadowing both, which they called living love.

And for those who seek together without marriage, there is still a path: the companions on the road, the friendship which eliminates time and space, each serving as mirror to the other. But those who wish to do spiritual work together, emotional work together, mental work and physical work together, all at once, take for themselves an added burden and an added hope. If each of you is a crystalline being attempting to hone that crystal within, so too a relationship stated clearly, spiritually and angelically, is a crystal also. Two together then seek instead of one and one.

Listen to that. Not one plus one. Instead of one and one. The arithmetic of love refuses to be ordinary.

There was a question that evening about failure in relationships, about what happens to the covenant when it ends. Q'uo's answer is one of the great mercies of this archive. The covenant, they said, is still valuable, inasmuch as the seeker was sincere in claiming the metaphysical promise. It is the nature of illusion to entrap, deceive and thwart, and often promises are broken and marriages end. Yet the failure is within the illusion, but the promise is eternal. Not a promise to be kept eternally, returning to one mate over and over, but a light which is eternal, made by two which have become one metaphysically.

And then the closing thought of the whole evening, the one that gathers everything up. All that remains from any experience within your illusion, and all that is ever recorded within the nature of the soul, is love. Whatever experience of love one is able to create and share within any relationship is remembered, and is gathered as the true harvest of the incarnation. All else is but the means to this end.

So remember and bless the promise, Q'uo urged, for it is a vehicle which may carry two to unity beyond themselves, with the face of the Creator. Whether the promise was kept in full or kept only in part, the light it made is not lost.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Four Forgivenesses
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the four forgivenesses.

The evening began with laughter. A voice called Yadda came through briefly to welcome the newcomers, and said this group makes many jokes, and that is a sign of some advancement, for so many on the spiritual path cannot make a joke, cannot laugh, and that makes the journey heavy, and mud cakes the feet of the poor pilgrim along the way. Make yourself merry, my friends. Let it bubble forth, and you will find wisdom beneath the laughter.

Then Q'uo took up the subject of the night, and it was a heavy one: forgiveness. An aspect of love and compassion very difficult to manifest while under the influence of the distortions of this density, they said. And what occurs when forgiveness is withheld? Separation, immediately. The one who does not forgive is separated from the one who is not forgiven, and that one may then choose not to forgive that, and there is further separation.

Before two who are thus separate can be patched together again, Q'uo said, four forgivenesses must take place. Each must forgive the other, and each must forgive the self. Four. Count them on your fingers sometime. It is almost never the other person's forgiveness that we are waiting on. The hardest one is nearly always our own.

If one were to visualize the tapestry of a lifetime, they said, one would see those portions of time when forgiveness was withheld from the self or another as places where the thread, the warp and woof of the tapestry of life, was coated with black, sticky substance, which stiffens and makes ugly the tapestry of existence. Forgiveness is not a feeling. It is the cleaning of the cloth.

And why is it so hard, when no one wishes not to forgive? The chief roadblock, they said, is the instinct for self-preservation. One who forgives is changed. Something dies and something is born. To hold the self or another in unforgiveness is to hold a relationship, or a self-concept, in pristine and clear condition, preserved like a specimen. Forgiveness lets it die so that something new can be born.

It is natural to fear death, they said, yet the road to joy is to rush toward whatever oblivion must be embraced in order to forgive, for the creation that springs forth from the heart of one who has truly forgiven is a beautiful and fresh manifestation.

There is a practical teaching here too, and it is subtler than it looks. The conscious mind is a kind of businessman, ordering things and moving them about, and the attempt to forgive by consciously stating that one wishes to forgive will likely fail, though the attempt itself is metaphysically important. It is within the province of the great subconscious mind that the seeds of forgiveness are sown. So they suggested this: take the object which has not been forgiven and hold it within the heart and mind, enveloped and encircled in light, light infinite and light illimitable, hoping and praying for every good for that which you cannot forgive.

You cannot force it. You cannot be taught it into existence. But you can hold the unforgiven thing in light, and let the deeper part of you begin opening doors, until that which is unforgivable to the conscious mind slowly becomes that which must be forgiven.

And one last word for anyone who sees hardheartedness, in others or in the mirror. You are powerful to serve as messengers of love, peace and joy. You may encourage, exhort, commune, or simply be with one who is having difficulty, and by mirroring forgiveness and love you connect your subconscious and your companion's subconscious in great echoes of compassion. Sometimes no word need be said.

May you find zest and joy in your inward walk, Q'uo said, and may you love life as you experience it. The time is short. The tapestry is still being woven.

Thank you for listening.

title: Every Life a Channeling
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: every life a channeling.

Hatonn came to speak about the practice of vocal channeling, but what he said applies to everyone who has ever lived a day. All of the life experience is, in essence, a channeling of some force, either within or without the self, into each action of the self.

It is the nature of humankind, he said, to be receptive, as a channel is receptive, and then to be a broadcaster, so that those who may find aid in your words may have access to them. The varieties of channeling are endless. And then the line that has made me smile every time I read it: there are those souls who channel such healing into the pie or roast that each bite taken at the dinner table fills not only the stomach but the heart with the love of the one who channeled perfect love into food.

The cook, the builder, the parent, the friend. Every life a channeling. The question is never whether you channel, only what you allow to move through you, and with what intention.

The vocal kind, the kind this group was practicing, he described with an image I love. It is like a game of pitch and catch. First one concept cluster, ranging from one word to quite a few, is thrown at the channel. The channel catches it with the metaphorical hand of consciousness and throws it on just as it was received, leaving the catching hand empty for the next concept. The whole discipline is to repeat what was heard without analyzing, doubting, or evaluating, because any of those thoughts moves one from the point of concentration.

Which is, if you think about it, a description of listening itself. How rarely any of us listen the way a channel listens, catching each concept and passing it on, leaving the hand empty for the next. Most of us are busy analyzing while the other person is still throwing.

Hatonn was honest, as he always was, about the limits of what any voice from beyond can offer. We have been wrong in the past and shall be wrong in the future, he said, for though we are many steps ahead of you upon the path of seeking, yet still we are finite and prone to error. They are humble words, and in large part their opinion only. Take what resonates and let the rest go.

And then this, the heart of the whole evening. Do you not bring to channeling the very essence of that which is to be channeled? For are you not in God and the Creator in you? Fear not the experience, nor be concerned what you shall say. What moves through you can only be built from what is already within you, and what is within you is more than you know.

He closed with an image of widening rings. You form a ring as you sit about the room. The domicile forms a ring about you, and the yard about the domicile, and the town about the yard, and the continent, then the world, then that great round the galaxy, and the timeless roundness of the creation itself. And each of you wishes to serve the roundness of the galaxy and of all creation. And the roundness of one circle sitting in light, wishing to be of aid to fellow seekers, is equally powerful.

Equally powerful. The small circle and the galaxy. The pie on the table and the stars. It is all one channeling, one broadcast of whatever love we have managed to let through.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Blessedness of Intention
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the blessedness of intention.

Hatonn opened this session with a phrase worth holding like a stone in the pocket: the blessedness of the intention to serve. And then he described the trap that intention so often falls into.

When entities discover within themselves the desire to serve, he said, they cast about for a satisfactory path of service and frequently become embroiled in the mechanics of producing the chosen service. In seeking the perfect service, life and joy are stripped from the endeavor.

You know this trap. The volunteer who becomes the committee's treasurer and forgets the cause. The helper who polishes the method until the helping disappears. Hatonn was not saying that skill does not matter. It is valuable, he said, to continually improve and refine one's ability to serve. But when the analytical mind takes over the faculty of evaluation from the deeper self, the seeker finds imperfections everywhere, becomes disappointed in the self and in the service, and that disappointment poisons future attempts.

The intention is the blessed thing. The mechanics are just mechanics. Keep them in their place.

Then he turned to what is actually happening when a channel speaks, and the description is worth hearing whether or not you will ever sit in a channeling circle. Vocal channeling, he said, is a way of linking three levels of being: the deep mind, the conscious mind, and the mind of the Logos. We speak not to your conscious mind, he said, but to your deep mind in concepts.

This conversation between the deep mind and the cosmos is going on all the time. Almost no one in the physical vehicle is aware of it. But each time the channeling is practiced, pathways are made deeper and clearer for the conscious mind to have access to the deep mind, and thus to the collected wisdom of the cosmos. Practice is not about getting better at performing. It is about widening a road that was always there.

There is a counsel here for every kind of service, not just this one. It is not necessarily one's path to be of service through any particular gift, Hatonn said. But it is always useful to have experienced the overshadowing of the self by something larger than the self. Let these experiences flow naturally, and evaluate in relaxation, at other times, the degree of attraction the work actually holds for you. Do not mistake the form of service for the service itself.

He ended with the seed image that runs through so much of this archive. It is often said among the Confederation that the seeds of creatorship dwell within each. When the seeds of the rose are planted, that which comes forth is a rose. If the seeds of the Creator are planted within you, my friends, shall your bloom and flower not be the Creator?

Shall your bloom and flower not be the Creator. The intention to serve is blessed because it is the seed watering itself. Everything else, the mechanics, the evaluation, the perfect form, is weather. The seed knows what to do.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Shipbuilder
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the shipbuilder.

This session was a story, told in pieces by several voices, and I will tell it to you the way it was told to them. It is a parable, and like all parables it is about you.

There was once a shipbuilder in an ancient land. His father and his grandfather had built the beautiful ships with their high prows. The young man had keen eyes. He watched the ships come and go and listened to tales of conquest and riches, yet he did not fancy himself a pirate, and he kept working upon the land. But within his heart there was the beginning of a desire to know more than was available within the confines of his work, his home, his friends, and his city.

One day a strange ship appeared over the horizon, tall, with red sails. The people feared an attack and took up arms. But when the ship landed, the men aboard carried no weapons. It was a merchant ship, carrying fine cloth and spices from far distant lands. And the young shipbuilder watched and listened, and knew his opportunity had come to see distant parts of the world without having to be a pirate. When the foreign ship sailed again, he sailed with them.

Far out on the ocean, farther from land than he had ever been, the journey grew long and tedious. Some of the crew fell ill. He himself was sick, and overcame it, and wondered whether the lands ahead would hold more of the same. But in the evenings he looked to the sky and saw beauty he had never seen on land, in the sky.

And as the boy gazed upon the stars, he wondered at the vastness of the universe, and at the significance of his small self in that boat upon that ocean. And he realized, after much concentration, that the only understanding he would have of the world, of the sky, of the stars, was to seek out the wisdom which he knew was contained within himself. Only there would he find the answers to his small questions.

With that knowledge, he reached a new perspective, and it gave great joy and meaning to all that he looked upon, for he realized that he was but one small cell in the infinite vastness of the universe, yet within that small cell was contained all the knowledge and the wisdom he sought around him.

The voyage ended, as voyages do. He left the ocean at a far shore and went back to work upon the land, building ships that would send other men upon the vast ocean. He had gained, the story says, far more than any pirate could ever have plundered from any ship or shore: a knowledge of the self that no gold could ever pay for, priceless only to himself.

Years later, in that far clime, people asked the strange sailor why he had come. He would only reply, to look at the stars. What is special about these stars, they asked. He would smile and say, when one has keen eyes, one thirsts for something to see.

And Hatonn closed the story with the moral, plain as bread. It is not important under which stars you dwell, but vastly important that your gaze upward be keen and persistent. Many times in any incarnation there will be need for the dark night, for only in the deepest darkness can one truly see at their very best those starry dominions which are symbols of light and love.

Find the deep sea within yourself in the waters of meditation, in the strong ship of your builded soul. Take the tiller and take responsibility for your seeking. Never apologize, however, for dwelling upon the land, for that which you do in the midst of your fellow human beings is that which builds the ship that carries your soul upon the stretches of the inner deep.

You do not have to sail to the horizon to make the voyage. The ocean is within you. The stars are above everyone. All that is required is the keen eye and the willingness to look.

Thank you for listening.

title: Channel Your Own Divinity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: channel your own divinity.

Hatonn said something this evening that quietly reframes the entire channeling project. We are only attempting, he said, to aid you in learning to channel your own divinity.

Your own divinity. That impersonal, caring, life-affirming portion of the self which, with great compassion and justice, gazes upon a fruitful and beautiful creation. The voices from beyond are not the point. They are training wheels for hearing what is already within.

Channeling is actually a fourth-density commonplace, he said, as each entity there is aware that within it lies the glory of the Creator, and naturally makes the choice to channel that energy. Those of us here often cannot see with physical eyes the seeds of wonder and godhead in ourselves and each other. Yet that resource, pure and undistorted, lies full-blown within each consciousness's heart. The work is not to import light from elsewhere. It is to learn to transmit what is already there.

There was a question that night about guidance, about how to tell in meditation whether what one receives is one's higher self or some other entity. Hatonn's answer applies to anyone who has ever sat in silence and wondered what to trust. Give the seeking a proper respect and a personalized ritual, he said. Prepare the place within your meditative state to which you shall repair only for the seeking of contact with a greater portion of your being. The visualization of white light, words that are meaningful to you, any regular manner of preparing the inner place. Repeat it each time, and the ritual itself will provide a cleansed and protected place of working.

The attitude with which one attempts this kind of meditation, and the regularized manner of focusing that attitude, are the qualities which are most important. Not the technique. The attitude. The sincerity of the approach is what draws the answer.

And there was a deeper teaching folded into the questions, one about why the unseen ones bother speaking to us at all. An entity working with one of the new instruments, Hatonn explained, seeks to utilize yet another means to be of service to the one Creator by sharing the fruit of its seeking. It is the case with positive entities, he said, that after the choice is made to seek in the positive sense, it becomes apparent that further progress upon this path is achieved not through personal gain of knowledge only, but more especially through the sharing of this knowledge and experience with others.

Read that again. Progress comes not from collecting knowledge but from sharing it. The hoarder stalls. The giver grows. That is as true of an ordinary human life as it is of any discarnate teacher.

So the evening's teaching, reduced to its simplest form, is this. The divinity is already in you. The ritual is just a way of arriving at the door with clean hands and an honest heart. And the reason to open the door at all is so that what comes through can be given away.

Sit tonight, if you sit, not to receive something you lack, but to practice transmitting something you have. Channel your own divinity. It has been waiting for an instrument.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Strangled Vine
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the strangled vine.

This is another tender episode, and I want to say at the start what the archive itself would want said. Q'uo spoke of depression as a distortion of consciousness, and their words are beautiful, but they are not medicine and not therapy. If you are living with depression, please reach out to someone you trust, and please consider a professional listener. The vine needs tending, and tending is easier with help.

The session opened with a question: what is depression, and what is to be done about it? Q'uo reached for an old image. It is written, they said, that the master known as Jesus is a vine and his students the branches. Consider yourself as a cosmic citizen, and all consciousness is rooted in one vine, the life-giving vine of love. Pure living love, stemming directly from the uncreated, a force which has propelled all consciousness into being.

Depression, then, is one of many human experiences in which a branch of the vine is damaged by the cutting off of the supply of food from the root. The invisible strangling of love. And when the person looks to see what the source of the strangling might be, it is invisible, for it has taken place within the mind itself.

Then they said something I think many seekers need to hear, because spiritual language can be cruel when it is used to dismiss pain. It is not merely an illusion to say that you are experiencing depression. Indeed, they said, over-emphasis on all being an illusion is perhaps detrimental to the balanced progress of a seeker. The pain is real. The branch really is strangling. To say so is not weakness. It is honesty.

What ties the cord so tightly, they said, is a desire to hold in the mind circumstances which seem unacceptable. The subconscious stops processing the catalyst of the present in terms of the present, and begins processing everything in terms of that unacceptable portion of memory. It is as if there were a drag upon an engine, so that the engine must work harder and harder to produce the same work. Or a blockage in the fuel line, so the engine of the mind cannot be fed.

And because the rupture lies within the self, and the self can blame only itself, a disassociation begins, which adds to the inertia. Two consciousnesses, as it were: one healthy and free, which exists in our dreams and at the core of all illusion, and one come to a standstill, receiving, instead of love, a fueling supply of fear.

Q'uo's counsel was not to deny the negative feelings but to become curious about them. Depression is merely a very disturbing distortion, they said. And they offered the image of a new consciousness, the consciousness of an entity that turns each moment like a stone, to see each facet of beauty, unity and love. The new consciousness has, above all, an insatiable curiosity. Let that curiosity, they said, sink into every thought process that has been stultified by the distortion of depression.

Curiosity unblocks. Not force, not denial, not the demand to feel better. Curiosity. The willingness to look closely at the strangling and ask what it is made of.

The tape ended before the teaching was finished, which feels strangely appropriate. The vine is still growing. The supply of love is still falling, constantly, into each portion of the Creator's consciousness. Nothing you have done has stopped it. The root is intact, even when the branch cannot feel it.

Thank you for listening.

title: A Movement into Mystery
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a movement into mystery.

Someone asked Quanta how one seeks absolute truth, and the answer is the most honest thing I have read in this entire archive. It is not a method. It is a paradox, and they do not pretend otherwise.

There is, they said, that which we call the one Creator, the one absolute source of all that is. And each conscious being at some point decides to seek it in terms that can be comprehended and utilized. This is a natural function of the conscious mind. However, we have discovered that for each portion of what seems to be truth that we gather unto ourselves, the greater grows the mystery of the nature of the one Creator from which all comes.

For every piece of truth gathered, the mystery grows larger. The more you know, the more there is to not know. And yet, they said, we continue our journeys, and our steps seem sure, and our experience serves us well, and yet that which was true at one time most often gives way to a greater truth that seems in comparison far surer than any previous piece of knowledge.

So their advice is this: gather all possible sources of information, consider them in meditation and contemplation and prayerful attention, and then be moved by that which resonates with the inner being. And realize that the movement which shall be the fruit of such considerations is a movement into mystery which, as far as we can see, is infinite in nature.

A movement into mystery. Not a march toward certainty, but a walking deeper into the unknowable, with better and better questions.

And there is a gentler promise inside this paradox. That which is of the greatest truth for each seeker seems to reside within the being of that seeker, and comes forth as that which is felt and then that which is known, as it begins to resonate with that which is sought. The desire of the seeker draws from many sources that which is most appropriate for that time, and draws from within the seeker that which is already there, ripening at the appropriate time according to the seeking that is expressed.

You do not find the truth so much as the truth finds you, timed to your ripening. The seeking is the watering. The fruit arrives when it arrives.

The evening also touched on the seasons of the soul. A questioner wondered about attachments falling away, about a life being rearranged from the inside, and Quanta spoke of testing, of initiation. The attitude with which the seeker views these rearrangements is what matters most. If it can be discovered within the seeker's point of view that each situation has a metaphysical implication revolving about the concept of love and acceptance of that which is, then the seeker can take advantage of the lessons that orbit that primary concept.

The testing is accomplished, they said, by the fires of experience touching the incarnation in such a manner that the greatest possible attitude of acceptance and peace then colors the mind. Not the removal of the fire. The coloring of the mind that walks through it.

And the foundation of it all, praised in this session as the primary quality of any instrument of service: dedication and perseverance. Without the dedication to continue and the will to persevere, no talent, no matter how great or varied or inspiring, can continue to burn as a beacon to others.

So gather your truths, let them grow the mystery, ripen in your own time, and keep walking. The mystery is infinite, and it is waiting for you the way the ocean waits for the river.

Thank you for listening.

title: Every Day a Birthday
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: every day a birthday.

The group had gathered around the idea of a special occasion, a moment when the energies of the planet were said to be unusually transparent, and they asked Q'uo what to make of it. The answer is classic Q'uo: yes, and also, every day.

There is a continuing daily need for the planetary seeking of harmony, they said. The recognition of special occasions is appropriate and efficacious to a certain extent, but it is the faithful seeker which marks each day as a day of harmony who shall create as a gift to the Creator the fuller fruit and the more universal spirit.

Imagine, they said, that each day was celebrated as a birthday. Not the gifts in ribbon and paper, but that special holiday feeling that comes with having your day be your very own special Earth day. Is not each day your very own special day? The occasion you are waiting for is the one you are standing in.

That does not mean special moments are nothing. There are hours, they said, when an unusually high degree of transparency exists, when that spirit which is love is more easily apprehended and shared, and it is well to recognize and cooperate with those moments of opportunity which are given by circumstance. But the deeper importance of any such occasion, they said, is archetypal. It is a chance to practice the balance between celebration and nothingness, for both of these things are the self. Both are the universe. Both are a portion of what may be said about the Creator.

They suggested a meditation for such times, and it is one of the most exacting practices in this archive: a meditation which asks no questions and seeks no answers, a meditation rich in nothingness, in darkness, in stillness of thought. No mental processes of the conscious mind. Just the willingness to surrender to the utter silence within. And they promised something startling about that surrender. One's surrender creates a joyful sense of freedom, and one then begins to dance within the mind and within the life.

The emptiness dances. That is the promise.

And for those whose gift is not silence but service, there was this: to those whose skills and love lie largely in dreaming, hoping and loving, take those dreams and hopes and love with the utmost of seriousness, that you may offer yourselves as channels of light in a dark world. For sending love is perhaps the most powerful action of a seeker.

Perhaps the most powerful action. Not the grand gesture, not the perfect meditation. Sending love.

The session closed with a teaching on pain that I want to leave you with. Each has behaviors born of pain and sorrow, Q'uo said. These pains, held to the breast, create strife evermore. Held instead to the light of love and accepted, it is then possible to have them let go, so that pain and sorrow become transformed into compassion, the strong compassion that shares the deep awareness of the oneness of sorrow in all peoples, and beyond that, the ultimate rhapsody of oneness in living love.

So mark this day as a day of harmony. Not because the stars aligned, but because you did. Happy birthday, by the way. It is yours.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Receiver Is On
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the receiver is on.

Hatonn was teaching the mechanics of channeling this evening, and in the middle of the technical talk he gave a definition of meditation so simple it stops you. But first, the teaching.

He explained that it is helpful for a new instrument to begin before the process is mature, to speak whatever words seem to come, garbled or not. From our point of view, as those who are sending to a receiver, he said, we find it helpful that the receiver be turned on. It is as simple as that.

The receiver must be on. You cannot calibrate a radio that is switched off. Until a new instrument has had some experience of what happens when the instrument is on, it is impossible to know whether the receiver is actually working. So you begin by beginning, imperfectly, and the imperfection is the calibration.

Then comes the deeper part. As the instrument becomes more experienced, the concepts offered can be longer and more detailed. But at the start, what the instrument must unlearn is the multiplication of detail, the human habit, when attempting creativity, of multiplying concepts with detail rather than honing them into simpler and simpler terms. And the conscious mind, that governor, must be damped down, so that external thoughts are allowed to flow away, keeping the concentration upon the most simple thing: listening within.

Channeling becomes, then, one way to experience an improved meditation, Hatonn said, for when the channel is busy listening for the next concept, the mind is stayed upon that point, becoming one large receiver.

One large receiver. And when the conscious mind is turned down and the inner ear listens, then it is that the Creator speaks in whatever way is creative at that time and place. That, he said, is in brief a satisfactory definition of meditation.

Forget emptying the mind. Forget achieving anything. Meditation is the receiver turned on, the inner ear listening, the mind stayed upon a single point. Everything else is commentary.

There was a second voice that evening, Laitos, who spoke with a bluntness the group found refreshing. Someone wanted proof that the contact was real, and Laitos was sorry to disappoint. There is no proof, they said. Any sort of objective proof of our presence would be an infringement upon the free will of those who are at this time making their choice. You are choosing, in this density, what to create with the mystery. Proof would end the choosing.

And Laitos added the line that gives this whole session its warmth. Five seconds or five minutes is enough time to move into contact with that Being which is the Source of all beings, and within which each being has its being.

Five seconds. You do not need an hour and a cushion and the perfect conditions. Five seconds of the receiver turned on, the inner ear listening, is enough to touch the Source.

So tonight, try it. Five seconds. Turn the receiver on.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Finest Offering
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the finest offering.

Laitos came this evening as a teacher's teacher, and the heart of the session is a sentence about service that deserves to be set apart and memorized. The attempt to be of service, empowered by the desire to serve, is the finest offering which one can make.

Not the successful service. Not the perfectly delivered help. The attempt, empowered by the desire. When this attempt is made and given with a full and whole heart, Laitos said, then one has done the best that one can do. This is to be applauded in any entity and any effort.

The context was a question from Carla, who teaches channeling and had given advice to a student about cleaning up her channeled language. Afterward she doubted herself. Had she interfered? Had her well-meant correction become a stumbling block? Laitos would not decide for her, because to do so would infringe upon her free will. But they gave her the frame in which to decide, and it is a frame worth keeping for every act of helping.

The response, they said, should find the blend of the honesty and truthfulness of wisdom with the nurturing of compassion, and that blend should form the parameters of your final response.

Honesty without compassion is a blade. Compassion without honesty is a fog. The finest offering is both, held together: the truth, delivered in a way that nurtures.

There is a quiet mercy in this teaching. Carla's doubts, Laitos said, were themselves grounded in the desire to be of the most service possible. Even the worry about having served badly is a form of service, because it is love checking its own work.

The session also touched on the discipline of challenging, the practice of demanding that any unseen contact declare its nature. One of the new instruments wondered whether his own alignment was enough, whether the formal challenge was necessary. Laitos answered plainly. For most, channeling stays shallow and runs its course. But for any entity desirous in the extreme to be of service by serving as an instrument, in as pure a manner as possible, a certain caution is centrally necessary, because this avenue offers the potential of real metaphysical power, and power attracts attention.

So each instrument must gather about itself those qualities which it feels are its essence, and form them into the challenge of the spirit, so that the contact may know who you are and what your desire is in a clear fashion. For this, they said, is your first communication with it.

Know who you are. State what you desire. That is the challenge, and it is not only for channeling. It is the proper posture for every encounter with the unseen, including the unseen parts of your own life. Declare the highest you can stably hold, and refuse what is less.

And then return to the sentence at the center. The attempt to be of service, empowered by the desire to serve, is the finest offering one can make. You do not have to succeed to have given your best. You only have to mean it, wholly, and try.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Inner Room
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the inner room.

Q'uo spoke this evening about two verbs that seem simple and are not: being and doing. We, as you, they said, are students of that great mystery which hides the face of the Creator from all of us. And the tension between being and doing is felt by many seekers, and can be a stumbling block. For one desires, in doing spiritual work as in any other work, to be occupied, to have accomplished something, to have gotten somewhere. Yet consciousness is ever and always at the base a being, not an activity.

You know the feeling. The day's cares are many, and the less important a detail is, the more time it takes to accomplish it. You sit down to meditate and the thoughts are scattered, pleasantly or not, but scattered, and the consciousness lies as your foundation, largely unnoticed in the flurry of activity. Then, slowly, the merging begins, into a harmony of seeking, into a consciousness felt by the self and shared about the circle.

That is the movement from doing to being. And the doing, Q'uo was gentle about this, all happens within an illusion. Your physicists will tell you this. All that looks solid is not. All that looks still is moving. The system of illusion was created, they said, so that you may play and work and do all manner of activity until you have decided upon a certain choice: service to others or service to self. The nature of the illusion is imperfection, so each thing done within it participates in imperfection. Good deeds don't turn out right. Relationships go awry. A word quickly said is long regretted.

Which is why they gave the teaching I want everyone to carry home. Avoid the emotion of discouragement, they said. And perhaps the best way to avoid it is to give encouragement to others. It is only our opinion, but we believe that good intentions, a true desire to do well, is far more important than how things actually come out in the illusion.

The intention outweighs the outcome. You are not graded on the results, which were never fully in your hands. You are known by the direction of your wanting.

Then a word about being. There is a place within the mind and heart of each of you which the Bible describes as the inner room, that place where you are at last alone with the self and with the Creator. Here lies the ground and essence of your being. Here, indeed, lies the entire universe, for each of you is a seed of the divine spark, and that portion within you in the innermost space is a hologram of all that there is, so that you contain universes, and all that you see dwells within you also.

At that level, they said, you never learn but only remember what you already knew, and recognize it once again.

They recommended the daily practice of meditation, the tabernacling in the inner room of the silent consciousness, so that the consciousness, touched often enough, may begin to shine through what you do, and you may become radiant, a more and more pure channel for the love of the infinite Creator. And if you cannot find time each day, still create a short time. It may be done momentarily, when the clock strikes. Open the door to that inner room, and just for a moment close it behind you, and say to that great mystery which lies in darkness all round the heart: here am I.

Here am I. Three words. The whole of prayer, the whole of meditation, the whole of being, in three words.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Present Moment
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the present moment.

The group asked Q'uo what they, the teachers, actually learn from us. And the answer is one of the most moving passages in the whole archive, because it turns the whole arrangement upside down. We gain more from our contacts with you than you gain from us, they said.

We were as you, they said. Within a third-density illusion, with dense chemical bodies that required daily fuel, gradually becoming aware that what was occurring was not what it seemed. Gone are those days for us, the days when the great choice between service to others and service to self was hidden in veils upon veils of mystery. Our choice is made. We have walked many steps on a path that is straight and narrow.

And here is their definition of that path. The path of seeking consists in one present moment and then another. Not the present moment with burdens of the past. Not the present moment with digressions about possibilities not yet explored. Each footstep upon the path of seeking is a step into the enormous depth, power and richness of the present moment, and to this realization we are committed.

What they learn from us, then, is the thing they can no longer do the way we do it: dive into the moment while hampered, while confused, while carrying the weight of a body. We find it incredibly moving, they said, that entities which labor as if underwater, hampered by a clumsy physical vehicle, can still look past the shimmering surface of the passing of time and dive deeply into the moment and gather treasures of love from it.

Time, they said, is not a river. Each present moment is plangent and brilliant and full to overflowing with a deeply moving kinetic upsurge of deeper meaning. If perception is of the present moment, then one may see in a vase of flowers far more than one who sees the vase as a thing moving upon the river of time. Scent, beauty, death, birth, growth, love of light. All of these echo from those flowers, and perception becomes capacious and generous.

And the greatest fruits of sinking into the moment, they said, are gifts of opened ears, opened eyes, opened hearts, and opened lives. Not every perception needs to be executed or manifested. Some moments are simply to be entered, the way one enters a cathedral.

There was a second teaching that night, about service, and it is worth hearing plainly. Another way you serve us, Q'uo said, is very simply that you call for us. If no one calls us, then we stand idle, sending our love to those who have not asked for it. There is little we can do without the request of those who wish the aid. And who knows what may make the difference for someone who seeks. The right word at the right time is enormously powerful.

Ask, in other words. The universe is polite. It knocks, but it waits to be invited in.

And the closing image of the whole session, the one I will not forget: we see in you the Creator in a way which is kept from you by the limitations of your organs of perception. What beautiful jewel-like beings you are, my children, and how deeply grateful we are to be working with you, to be learning from you, and to be sharing meditation.

Jewel-like beings. That is what the teachers see when they look at us, laboring underwater, gathering treasures. Remember that the next time you feel small.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Timeless Moment
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the timeless moment.

The group's questions this evening were about time and purpose, money and suffering, and Q'uo answered with a teaching about two kinds of time. The first you know well. Time in its mundane, river-like existence moves on inexorably, rhythmically, cyclically, sweeping all immediacy before it. Busy time upon busy time, and no respite from the chores and details that make up the day.

But there is another kind of time. It is the time of the timeless moment, a moving vertically upward and downward upon the moment, to feel the echoes of love, meaning and manifestation in one moment. That removes from time its horizontal inexorability, its forced progress, and makes for the seeker opportunities of timelessness.

Horizontal time carries you forward whether you like it or not. Vertical time is the depth you can drop into at any instant.
