Its purpose is to open the heart portion of the mind, for the analytical mind carries you through your culture's activities, but the mind-heart has a deeper way, a more centered truth.

Then they turn to vocal channeling specifically, and they are sober about it. Many poets have written modest pleasant verses, they say; what this instrument would call Chopsticks can be taught to any pianist. But is the simple tune decisively important to share with others? Not everyone, perhaps not even most, need seriously consider a life lived as a vocal channel.

There is a certain temperament that finds its reward in being used as a vocal channel — willing to undergo difficulties, misunderstandings, inconvenience. And the honor of being a channel grows in direct proportion to the responsibility of living that which is channeled.

The entities which began as excellent vocal channels and later disintegrated their contact are many, they say — far too many. By following not the heart within but the ambition without, they condemned themselves to much disappointment. If you are to be a vocal channel, you shall not be able to resist the search, the practice, the ponderings.

How do contacts find their instruments? We are those who listen to a certain vibration of request, they say. This group became one, lost its self-consciousness, joined in a circle of light — and within that creation placed a call. And we answer that call, and that right gladly.

And their desire, they say, is not just to make more vocal channels, but to make each aware of the channeling he or she is already doing. The conscious mind is so very small a part of your minds. The great depth and beauty of the connection with deeply impersonal sources is by far the greater extent of the mind.

A weaver channels the beauty of the cloth, they say. One who works with people channels a love and acceptance, a true listening ear. The cooking, the washing, the smiling at the sun, the enjoyment of water — all the little things which are like flowers in a bowl in unexpected corners of your daily life. You channel your daily life.

Honor yourself, they say, and honor the Christ consciousness in each and every face that you see. Fill the blank pages as you will — but write them in love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Channeled Life
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the channeled life. Q'uo returns to the channeling question — and takes it deeper, to the life of the minister, the shepherd, the one on the watchtower.

The circle had felt that Q'uo had more to say after the previous week's long session, so they asked again: should everyone channel, and what determines the contact? Q'uo obliges, and the result is one of their most sustained meditations on what it means to live as a channel.

They begin where the last session left off. Each is an equal, considerable and infinite portion, they say, of the cumulative channeling of the one great original Thought of humankind. And it is not the finely tuned sensibilities on whom the fate of humankind rests — nay, far more is it the hard-won capacity of the busy, overworked, underappreciated man and woman of lesser circumstances, whose response to difficult environments generates the love and the light of the one infinite Creator for all of mankind.

I love how they keep returning to this: the ordinary life, faithfully lived, as the engine of the world's light.

Then they turn to the vocal channel specifically. Some few there are, they say — in forest glade, in mountain cave, in comfortable dwellings and uncomfortable ones — who have devoted their lives to being a channel in service to the one infinite Creator.

But all those who quickly learn the mechanics are not thereby ready for the life of discipline which follows. The Confederation, they say plainly, does not wish to create channels through which to comment on physical disasters. What they rejoice in is the clear statement of the channel's personality, in a disciplined and unified way — for channeling is a two-way conversation, based very largely on the level of commitment the channel offers at the time of challenge.

The channel is not the entertainer, they say, nor the one with a job to do. The channel is rather a kind of person. Your closest word would perhaps be minister or priest.

This minister gazes upon the face of the illusion and chooses to live in a loving, caring and openly spiritual way — bragging not one word, celebrating not one virtue, but learning the true humility of one who knows that what one wishes to be, one is only by will and faith.

And there will be testing. If the new instrument thinks at first there is some ongoing trickster designed to test the channel, they say, this instrument is not only accurate but has foreseen the mere beginning of a long series of challenges — of seeming heartlessnesses to bring love to, of seeming dreadful inadequacies to enfold — until finally the one who seeks to serve aches and cries with the agony of compassion in such a dark world, and yet trembles with the ecstasy of the limitless light.

The channel, they say, has been intending to die to the self for time out of mind. And when finally the poor ragged flags of personality flutter and lie limp, the channel rises with lightsome step and glorious enthusiasm for the light and companionship ahead.

They speak then to the shepherds — to you on the watchtower, mending fences, gazing into the heavens as sentinels of the lights of the cosmos. Find within the self, they urge, that fundamental character which can offer the highest praise, the deepest felt purified emotion.

If that means you must function on your own, then it is that you shall be lonely. So may you find those who comfort you — those able to share the darkness, the misunderstandings, the despair and the doubt which accompanies a life lived in hope but executed with human error.

And to all the shepherds there is sent a glorious company, they say, who surround you and love you. Call upon those helpers — Holy Spirit, guardian angel, inner guides. Rest back into the recollection of the enormous web of caring, trusting, hoping and loving which your most mixed-up planet does indeed send out greatly.

May you be comforted by all your failures, they say — for how could you succeed each time were there not a crying need for effort? May each of you find your rejoicing in each other. May you love each other. May you see the Creator in each other.

May your channeling become a channeled life.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Gentle Warrior
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the gentle warrior. Q'uo on negativity — the kind that comes from other people, and the kind that comes from within.

The circle asked about negative polarity in all its forms: the magically powerful entity sending a greeting meant to disable, the person who simply wishes you ill, all the way to the impersonal systems that control the many for the gain of the few. How does a seeker deal with these?

Q'uo begins with a distinction. There is no ego or negativity, they say — there are egos and negativities. To assume a good and an evil, a positive and a negative, is to set up the parameters of a game. There is no constant that has bias.

The biases which each of you bring to experience are those things with which you place values of good and negative on what you experience. Your own biases, your own thoughts, your own nature take an unbiased illusion — far too great for that computer which is your mind to analyze — and your nature orders that computer to assess certain data.

That which is within your mind and heart is that which determines your creation, they say. Each of you is co-Creator, as powerful as the deity whose mystery you seek to plumb.

So the first consideration in dealing with negativity is to examine the probability that the biases creating your world contain what you yourself would call negative elements. Were you to have no negative bias, each entity you met would appear as the entity actually is: a perfect unique prism of white light, a child of the Creator.

The name you have for one of all positivity is saint, they say. Saints do not feel threatened by outer circumstance. They are few among your peoples.

Then they walk through the energy centers. Much of your people's work at this time, they say, is orange-ray work — personal relationships, the difficulties of the person within the self. When the orange ray becomes blocked in relationship to another, the negative feelings can be very intense. Yet the blockage is blocked within the individual self first — so when a stranger infringes upon it, you receive an unwelcome mirrored picture, and the stranger is disliked upon sight.

The yellow-ray blockages — the societal energies — are why the news all seems bad. Fear not, they say: we are not saying the problems of the world are your fault. We are saying that your perception of the world is absolutely and completely your choice.

The point of freeing the red, orange and yellow centers from blockage is that the fullness of the one great original Thought may rise to the level of the heart.

And then they name the seeker's stance. Those who are negatively oriented, whether incarnate or discarnate, have an automatic battle with spots of positivity that glow too brightly. So it is the normal experience of one on the journey of seeking through love that a large percentage of the time there will be elements of negative intrusion — the productive deserts of testing and temptation.

In these, they say, it is necessary only for the pilgrim of positivity to remain peaceful, loving, gentle, harmless — and warrior-like.

Warrior-like in a very specific way. They ask: do you wish to live a life that is in the end a gift to the one infinite Creator, made day by day, moment by moment? Then know that all those positive presences in the universe await your call. You are never alone. There is always a solid backing of love, courage, patience — and the instinct for the proper time to walk away.

As a warrior of light, they say, you use no weapon but what may be called the armor of light, the sword of truth, and a wide open heart chakra — loving without stint, without expectation of return, and most of all with no judgment.

It is not difficult to love negatively oriented individuals, they say, once you can connect into that portion of the deep mind which sees each person, whatever the vagaries of trouble and circumstance, as a holograph of the one infinite Creator. All threat disappears. All separation vanishes.

And when negativity is viewed, stop — and give that entity the honor of an unstinting love, a generous prayer that it may be held upward, protected, cherished and loved as a child of the one infinite Creator.

There is no control such an entity may have over you, they say, if you but know who you are, if you but know the choice you have made.

My children, your job is to live a life. Positivity and negativity are passions — frames of mind which engage the heart totally. Ask to be shown where the center of love in this experience is. This is the function of hope and faith.

Peaceful, loving, gentle, harmless — and warrior-like. That is the gentle warrior.

Thank you for listening.

title: Pilgrims on the Road
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: pilgrims on the road.

A Sunday evening in January of nineteen eighty-eight, and someone in the circle asks Q'uo about the most ordinary and the most holy of questions: how to raise a child. How to discipline. How to love well the small soul that has been trusted to your care. Q'uo begin, as they often do, by quietly turning the whole question around.

You think of yourself as the teacher and the child as the student, they say. But look again. The parent is a soul with more experience in this illusion. The child is a soul with less experience. And before either of you was born, you chose each other. You chose whom you would teach and whom you would learn from, and Q'uo add that these roles do not stay put. They move back and forth through the years of the relationship. The one who guides is also being guided. The one who disciplines is also being disciplined. You are both, they say, pilgrims upon the road.

I love that they start there, because it changes everything about discipline. If the child in front of you is not a blank slate but an old soul who has lived before, who brought with her into this life her own biases and beliefs and unfinished work, then your job is not to build a person from nothing. It is to meet a traveler. And she, this young traveler, is watching you far more closely than she is listening to you. Children learn from imitation, Q'uo say. The talk helps a little. The actions are everything. If she does not see you engaged in an earnest and persistent seeking of your own, in a genuine search for what is true, she will be open to any voice that comes along loud and certain.

Listen to how they put the practical part. Live as you would suggest your children to live. Be honest in your dealings with them, meaning what you say and saying what they say, keeping your word in the good times and the bad. And when correction must come, let it sting the pride, if it must sting, in private. Never in a way that lets the world watch the small soul being corrected by the parent who loves her. The keynote, Q'uo say, is that the elder soul shall never take away the worth of the younger. Only those corrections that help her find her place in the world she will one day walk alone in. Never one that makes her less.

There is a passage in this session that I have never forgotten. Q'uo describe how learning works where they come from. In the higher densities, they say, a young entity is allowed to play for as long as it wishes. The teachers simply wait. They wait until the small one grows curious, hungry, fascinated, and comes of her own choosing to ask to learn. Then the teacher teaches, and is a hard taskmaster, but the student accepts the difficulty gladly because she chose it. Every learning different. Every entity accepted as different. And then, gently, they turn to us: your culture assumes that every child who has circled the sun six times is ready for first grade, and lines them all up in rows. The young soul knows true knowledge is exciting, not boring. But with a sigh, she puts that knowing away, and submits to the regimentation.

So what does Q'uo ask of the parent, in the end? Not perfection. They know parents and children will fall and climb up again many times. Mistakes upon mistakes. But there is one deep and fathomless thing that binds parent to child, and that is love. The parent cannot help but love the child, nor the child help but love the parent. Let this love be communicated, they say. Let it be celebrated. Never let it be taken for granted. Love each other, for you are both pilgrims upon the road.

And then this, as a resting thought. The whole of this illusion, Q'uo say, was designed for one learning activity, and it runs from our earliest memories until the fullness of age: learning how to love. The family you were given, the child who chose you, the arguments and the apologies, all of it is the outworking of a plan you made together before you came. Trust it, even in the hard times. You came here to learn the greatest lesson this density has to teach.

Thank you for listening.

title: The One Great Thought
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the one great thought.

One week after speaking about parenting, Q'uo return to the same circle, and this time the question is reincarnation. Why do we come back, again and again, into lives we cannot remember choosing? Their answer starts very far away, at the largest scale they can describe, and it is one of the most beautiful passages in this whole archive.

The Creator, they say, is a vast infinity that is also intelligent. And this Creator chose to make a universe that could hold entities who were, in their words, as a holograph of the Creator. All that was in the Creator was in the conscious entity. All conscious entities were the Creator. You are, each of you, a spark, an infinite part of an infinite whole. And the nature of this Creator, Q'uo say, is one singular thought. That thought is love.

Let that sit for a moment. Not love as a feeling you have on a good day. Love as the single original thought out of which everything is made. The rocks are still learning the lesson of existence itself, they say. The plants turned toward the light. The animals learned to grow. And then, in each portion of consciousness, there came a turning not only toward the light but toward the love that lies behind the light. That is who you are. That turning is you.

So why the forgetting? Why come into a life with no memory of the lives before? Q'uo are tender about this. The veil of forgetting is intentional, they say, because ever-new are the opportunities to make and remake the choice: to serve by loving others, or to serve by loving only the self. If you remembered everything, the choice would not be a choice. And what is kept from your past lives is not lost. It lives in your deep mind, in your promptings and recognitions, in the feeling that some difficulty cannot be explained by this life alone. When you need a past life, it will float up through dreams, or through meditation. Chasing after past-life details is not the work. The work is becoming sensitive to the promptings of your own heart, right now, in this life, with the people in front of you.

There is a line here that answers a question someone asks later in the session, about the hermits and contemplatives who sit in mountain caves and seem to serve no one. Q'uo say those solitary ones broadcast. Like a radio station sending out a frequency, they nourish the whole species on levels beneath consciousness, the way a gardener feeds the soil for all the plants. I love that line. Nobody's seeking is wasted. The quietest life is feeding someone.

And then the passage the whole episode is named for. You have heard of karma, they say. The end of karma is forgiveness. If you find one person in your life particularly difficult, seek the seeds of forgiveness in the infinite love within you, for as you forgive the other and forgive yourself, you balance in love what once blocked the flow. That is the whole mechanism, laid bare. Not punishment. Not debt. Forgiveness.

Here is my resting thought. Q'uo say that your time in this density is growing short, and that what shapes whatever comes next is the decision you are making now, in these final lifetimes of the cycle, to serve the cause of love. You have been choosing for thousands of years. Believe in your strength as one who has chosen. And keep a light touch about it all. Laugh together in the joyful times. Find the light side in the sad ones. You are learning to be love, and love, they remind us, was the thought that started everything.

Thank you for listening.

title: Branches and Roots
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: branches and roots.

Early February, nineteen eighty-eight. Hatonn comes to a small circle of friends who want to heal. Not to be healed, exactly, though that too, but to become healers themselves. One of them is learning to channel, and is struggling with the process. Hatonn speaks to both longings at once, and gives us one of the great images of this archive.

First, the healer. Hatonn asks each person in the room to think of herself first as a healer and only second as a teacher or a channel or anything else. And then he says what a healer actually is. Not someone with the right technique. Not someone with herbs or crystals or kind words, though all of those can help. A healer is someone who has hollowed out a place within the heart where the light is acknowledged, so that at all times she can function as what Hatonn calls a living crystal. The healing itself is not done by the healer. The healer acts as a catalyst, arranging things so that for a short while, the one to be healed can see a new balance, a new possibility. And then it is the other person's free choice whether to claim it. Even the most powerful healer, Hatonn says, is not expected to use her will upon another. Simply to be the crystal. Simply to offer the light.

And the warning that comes with it is just as important. A healer must never let the one who comes for help become dependent. Never present yourself as the answer. Always call upon the will and the hope and the power within the individual herself. The tools are not the healing. This is a line worth carrying: never mistake the tools of the trade for the wisdom, the compassion, and the intuition of the trade.

Then Hatonn turns to the mind itself, and gives the image this episode is named for. Do not see the critical mind and the intuitive mind as two sides of a coin, he says. See a tree. The conscious mind, the part that analyzes and decides, is the part above the ground, the branches that blossom in summer and stand bare and proud against the winter cold. The intuitive mind is the great underground system of roots, drinking in nourishment from the earth and water, in contact with the Creator in every season. And then this astonishing line: there are far more roots to the mind than there are visible branches, and the ends of the roots lie in the center of the Sun. The deeper mind, Hatonn says, has the opportunity to contact eternity itself.

I love how gently he holds both parts. The critical mind is a wonderful tool, he says, for gathering data and making decisions, and he would not speak ill of it. But a tool can become the master of its user. Working with intuition alone, without the intellect, produces an entity lost in a sea of wonder with no way to express or refine what she has received. So the practice is balance. Glory in your branches, he says, in your thoughts and distinctions and conclusions. But let your faith be in the root system that links you to eternity, and let your will be, more and more, to place the tree above ground in service to the greater consciousness that lies within the nurturing dark.

A resting thought, from near the end of the session. Hatonn is speaking to the new channel, the one who keeps stumbling, and his tenderness is almost physical. The service of channeling, he says, and the learning of its practice, is of much practical help in learning how to live within the illusion. To channel the life. To let the infinite love move through. Whatever your work is, healer, teacher, parent, friend, the principle is the same. Hollow the place. Be the crystal. Let the light do what it does.

Thank you for listening.

title: Gifts and Limitations
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: gifts and limitations.

Early February, nineteen eighty-eight. A question comes in about a friend who has been told he has narcolepsy, and who, in his seeming sleep, appears to leave his body and travel. The question is really about all the strange gifts: the out-of-body experiences, the sensitivities, the abilities that do not fit neatly into an ordinary life. What are they for? How do we use them to grow? Before I go further, a gentle note, in the spirit of this whole series. These voices speak as teachers of the soul, not as doctors of the body. Nothing here is medical counsel. What Q'uo offer is a way of thinking about the strange things that happen to us, and I want to hold that frame with care.

Their answer begins before birth. Before you incarnated, Q'uo say, you chose the manner in which you would prefer to learn each lesson. Every circumstance of your life, the usual and the unusual alike, contains exactly the catalyst you need to bring your attention to one choice: whether you will find love and offer compassion, or use control and make separation. A gift like leaving the body is not a prize. It is a tool you selected, like a student selecting a particular course of study. And the question to ask of it, in meditation, is simple: what may I do to serve the Creator with this gift? Or, if the gift feels more like a burden, what may I give as a result of what I learn from this condition?

Listen to how they put the deeper point. All the gifts you can name, and all the limitations, were not given because they are your true personality. Personality is a thing of this illusion. Gifts and limitations are the tools you have to work with. The more honestly you identify your gifts, the more clearly you assess your limitations, and the more readily you accept the discipline that lets you use that self in compassion toward others, the faster you grow. And the confusion you feel about a strange gift is not failure. Q'uo say confusion is an uncomfortable but very productive state, the very soil in which new thought grows. Sometimes that confusion lasts an entire lifetime. What matters is not that you understand the gift intellectually, but that you move through enough acceptance and forgiveness to come into full love of the self as a part of the Creator.

There is a second teaching tucked into this session that I want to lift out, because it answers a question about service. Someone asks how we can consciously contribute to the spiritual growth of others, and Q'uo answer with a line that stops me every time. The force that moves you to serve, if it is compassion, has far more effect than the most carefully planned service that lacks compassion. The mind alone can attain wisdom and discern what is appropriate. But without compassion, even the wisest service finds no fertile ground. Compassion is what lets the seed take root.

The session ends with a visit from Yadda, the rough-voiced entity who drops in from time to time like weather. He speaks of winter, of the joy of the seed gathering food in the roots, of water showing its crystalline magic in the cold. Warm your winter heart, he says. Be silly and playful in the cold. Every season happy, no season sad, for all work together. Be merry.

So here is my resting thought. Whatever you were given, the shining gift or the heavy limitation, it was chosen by a self wiser than the one reading these words, and it was chosen for love. Meet it face to face. Offer it back in humbleness. And let compassion, not cleverness, be the quality that moves through everything you do.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Catalyst of Healing
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the catalyst of healing.

February of nineteen eighty-eight, and the circle asks Hatonn a question that sounds like a paradox. If our lives are unfolding as they should, if there are no mistakes, then how can anyone who wants to heal actually be part of healing? If all is well, what right have we to change anything? Hatonn's answer is one of the clearest statements of his whole teaching on service.

You came here, he says, because you wanted to aid each other. That is the entire reason for the incarnation. All things are as they should be, and that in no way inhibits the action of free will. You came to this Earth hungering to feel and sense and wonder, knowing that through those sensations you would learn, more and more, the omnipresence of love and the joy of choosing to serve others, each in your own way. Help between brother and brother lies in the present moment. Not in yesterday's scorched ground. Not shot like fireworks into tomorrow's mist. Now.

And what does the healer actually do? Hatonn is precise. The healer acts as a catalyst. Whether the tools are herbs or kind words or hypnosis or simply presence, the tools are in the end not necessary. They are a way of focusing the mind while the deeper connections open. The real catalyst, he says, is the healer as she is: the degree of crystallization of her own energy, and the depth of her desire to serve. The one to be healed is then shown, for a little while, a new balance, a new vision of wholeness. And then it is entirely the other's free choice whether to claim it. If it is not claimed, it does not happen. That is how free will is honored even in the act of healing.

I want to linger on the ethical warning Hatonn gives here, because it is so practical. It is possible, he says, for a sincere healer to create not freedom in the one who comes for help, but dependence. Some who seek are confused and disassociated, and they want someone to lean on for the answers. The healer must always, always call upon the will and the hope and the power within the individual herself, and present herself as nothing but a catalyst through which healing may pass. Not the source. Never the source. Only the space where the other's own healing becomes possible.

And then the line that gathers the whole session up. Seek your teachers, Hatonn says. Study your books. Apprenticise yourself to those you deem worthy. But remember always that the true work of the healer lies within: in the healing of the self, in the steadying of the fire of love, in the willingness to be open to the compassion that stands unmoved before life and death and wishes only that the highest will be fulfilled. A gentle note, as always with these teachings on healing: this is a voice speaking about the soul's work. It is not medicine, and it does not replace the care of those trained to tend the body.

My resting thought is the simplest one in the session. All is as it should be, and you are still free to help. Those two truths do not contradict each other. They are the two hands of the same love. Be the crystal. Offer the light. Let the other choose.

Thank you for listening.

title: Blissful Within Sorrow
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: blissful within sorrow.

Mid-February, nineteen eighty-eight, and someone asks Latwii the question every seeker eventually asks. If we were in bliss before we came here, why did we leave it? Why would anyone willingly trade paradise for this, for the grief and the confusion and the long tired days? Latwii answer with unusual tenderness, and they admit something first: they themselves still ask this question, with even less reason than we have.

The short answer, they say, is that this density is a peerless place to learn. You cast yourself into the illusion the way you might cast yourself into deep water, to use it, to be shaped by it, to suffer and in time to revise the biases you brought with you. But then they set the short answer aside and reach for the true one, and the true one is about joy.

When the veils are lifted and the soul rests in union with the Creator, there is bliss. Latwii do not deny it. But into that bliss, they say, there comes a restlessness, as if pulled by the moon. A sadness begins to stir in those who are blissful, because within them is a desire built in from the beginning: the desire to go forth and act. To serve. And so the blissful one chooses, willingly, to move into what will make her sorrowful, in order that the wellspring of joy brimming within her may be poured out in service to others, instead of kept within.

Listen to how they put what happens next, because this is the heart of the session. The long years of service that does not look like service, the sorrowful seasons upheld only by blind faith, will in time, as faith grows stronger, allow a reversal. As one was sorrowful within bliss, they say, now one may become blissful within sorrow. That is the balance the whole journey is aimed at. Not the removal of suffering. The discovery of joy inside it.

And then the most practical teaching in the session, the one I keep returning to. Stop hunting for your vocation, Latwii say. What is directly before your face, what comes with each day's coming, is the work at hand. Whether it is simple or complex, menial or grand, within that work lie the seeds of joy and the opportunity for service. A seeking entity cannot help but do the work it came to do. The plans you made before this life are part of the very field of your being, and they will attract exactly the work that needs your attention. So the pressure comes off. You do not have to find the grand purpose. You have to live this Tuesday.

Each entity, they say, is a story within the mind of the Creator, and each incarnation a small gift, a bouquet, a scent upon the wind, by which the infinite One learns ever more about itself. If your life is a gift, then to live, to love, to feel, to be, is the true vocation. One who expresses joy from within, they say, is doing the greatest work in consciousness it is possible to do.

My resting thought is for anyone in a long season where the joy cannot be seen. Latwii urge you to nurture yourself inside the sorrow, and to nurse the faith that even when joy is invisible, the light within is still moving forward, still learning, still drawing closer to a joy beyond this one. You left bliss to find this. One day you will be blissful within the sorrow, and the circle will close.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Veil as Ally
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the veil as ally.

Valentine's Day, nineteen eighty-eight, and the question is about the veil. The veil between the conscious mind and the deeper mind, the forgetting that makes this life feel so lonely and so vivid. Is the veil our enemy? Should we tear it down? And what does it have to do with the way the brain itself is built, the old idea of the bicameral mind, the voices of the gods the ancients heard? Q'uo take the question seriously, and their answer is one of the most clarifying in the archive.

First, they say, the veil is not a punishment. It is not some petty trick of the Creator to make the game harder. It is the precondition that makes learning possible at all. Here is why. Without the forgetting, your choices would not be choices. You would see too clearly, know too much, and the decisions that this life is designed to sharpen would go soft and vague. With the veil in place, every feeling lands harder, every catalyst cuts deeper, and the system of biases that is your soul gets worked on with a precision that no unveiled existence could manage. Yours, they say, is a valley of decision. You dwell in the darkness of unknowing, and there, in honest unknowing, you spend your years deciding how to love. What a great decision, my friends. What a pivotal one. And for it, the veil is necessary.

I love that they refuse the dramatic version of enlightenment here. People imagine illumination as a burst of light, the veil shattering all at once. Q'uo say the goal is not to remove the veil but to build, slowly, a shuttle through it, a protected passage woven by faith and will, so that the deeper self can speak in language clearer than dreams. And the way to build it is almost embarrassingly simple: daily meditation. Not heroic meditation. Just daily. The meditation moves into the deep mind, they say, as the lover moves to the beloved, to woo and win it. An atmosphere of love for the Creator and for that deeper part of yourself where the Creator dwells. What you touch, reaching in with love, is exactly what you most need.

They are honest about the shortcuts, too. The veil can be torn open by certain substances, by extreme fasting, by frenzied ritual. But what pours through an unguarded tear is not all wisdom. The deep mind contains the universe, and not everything in the universe is gentle. Those who force the opening move at risk, and may find themselves possessed not by insight but by the louder, harsher portions of what lies within. The slow way, the daily way, is the safe way. It is well, they say, to work toward the growing transparency of the forgetting. Just do it the way the lover does it, not the way the burglar does.

There is a passage near the end I want to read to you almost whole, because it gathers everything. Each of you, Q'uo say, is a priceless gem in an uncut form, and as you seek, the facets begin to appear. And what you are seeking is not in phenomena, not in feelings, not in thoughts, but in what one of your holy books called the still, small voice. The silence that speaks within. Trust the process. By your meditations you are able, in the focusing of desire, to become the light upon the hill that shines for all to see the Creator within.

So my resting thought is this. Do not curse the forgetting. It is not your enemy. It is the dark room in which the photograph of your soul is being developed. Sit daily. Build the shuttle. And know that the mystery you seek is the only concern you will carry with you through eternity, a beautiful mystery Q'uo have learned to call love itself.

Thank you for listening.

title: Young Gods
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: young gods.

Late February, nineteen eighty-eight. The question is a strange and modern one: do the negative thoughts of whole societies create something real? Do the fears and angers we generate together gather into forms that linger, that feed on us, that make everything worse? Q'uo say yes, and then they give one of the most practically useful teachings in this whole archive. A gentle note first, because this session touches depression and anxiety by name. These voices speak to the life of the spirit. If your mind is in a dark season, please reach for real human help alongside any teaching. Hold both.

Here is the picture Q'uo paint. Strong emotion, positive or negative, creates a kind of aura, a nimbus of weak thought-forms. Left unfed, they dissolve. But fed by more of the same feeling, they grow bolder, and they begin to feed on the very emotion that made them, the way a fire feeds on the wood that lit it. Negatively polarized ones drink fear. Positively polarized ones drink awe and love. And then comes the image I cannot shake: there are places thick with them. Hospitals, where pain and fear hang in the air so densely that those already suffering must breathe it in. And there is a subtler one, an immense thought-form centuries in the making, that Q'uo call the husband and the wife, the accumulated dissatisfaction of countless mated pairs, waiting to intensify every quarrel it touches.

It would be easy to read this as frightening. Q'uo mean it as liberating. Because if thought-forms feed on what you express, then you are not helpless before them. You are their keeper. The solution, they say, and the instrument transmitting even laughs at how simple it sounds, is the conscious turning of the mind and heart toward positive thought. Toward the remembrance of service offered and love given. That turning is the one weapon of mind and heart that starves what feeds on darkness. A mind stayed on what is true dwells in unity and peace, and there is simply no entrance for the surrounding shadows.

Listen to how they describe the moment of turning, because it is so honest about how it feels. If you feel a wrench and a pull and a tearing loose when the turn is made inside the mind and heart, they say, know that you have broken the bands of those who had you neatly arranged for consumption, and they have had to go away quite hungry. Change does not always feel peaceful at first. Sometimes it feels like tearing. That tearing is the sound of freedom.

And they do not pretend that sorrow itself is the enemy. Sometimes, they say, the sorrow is long, because the spirit needs the long burning to survive and heal. Suffering borne in nobility of mind and greatness of heart creates, in their image, a somber bright beauty that flames among the other stitches of the tapestry of a life, giving it a richness it would otherwise not have. Never mistake the difficulty itself for what you must put into your own tapestry. You choose the stitches. You are, they say, a sovereign being, an image of the Creator. And then the line this episode is named for, spoken with enormous tenderness: my friends, we are young gods. Let us search together for the face of our true identity.

My resting thought is the simplest instruction in the session. Moment by moment, when you find yourself discouraged or afraid, know in your heart that you have a choice. The universe is full of energies, but they must not all come to you. Turn to the source. Turn, and keep turning. And the thought-forms of light will come with angel wings, take food from your joy, and give you back the hunger for more.

Thank you for listening.

title: Channeling the Life
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: channeling the life.

Early March, nineteen eighty-eight. A short session, and a new instrument who is struggling. He wants to channel Hatonn's thoughts clearly, and the harder he tries, the more the contact slips. Hatonn's response is not a technique. It is a whole philosophy of living, told as a game.

Imagine, Hatonn says, that life is a ball game. The balls keep coming, thought after thought, circumstance after circumstance, and your part is simple: catch the ball and dispose of it according to the rules of the game. There are the rules of society, which you may or may not accept. But underneath those, as you prosper in your studies, you begin to discern the backbone of your own nature, the skeleton of ethics and compassion and caring that is unique to you alone. When you stop grasping at outcomes and concentrate only on the accuracy of the catch, on seeing each circumstance clearly, then the knowledge of the self moves the ball, by instinct, to its rightful place. Love itself, Hatonn says, prospers in such an atmosphere.

I love what he says about the dropped balls, because there are always dropped balls. Thoughts fumbled. Perceptions misplaced. Moments chewed over past the point of any use. When the flow stops, Hatonn says, the experienced player does not walk off the field in disgust. He sits patiently upon the mound, still in the ball game but between innings, doing work just as difficult and just as important as the active play. That work is waiting. Waiting, in the certainty that the game of love and life and service always goes on. It is those who walk away, disappointed in themselves or in others, who lose their balance and their faith.

And here is the turn that gives the episode its name. Hatonn says the practice of channeling is of great practical help in learning how to live, and then he asks for something larger. Attempt, he says, to channel the life as a whole. Not in the technical sense of speaking another's words, but in this sense: to move through your days with the same release you practice at the instrument's chair, unconcerned with all else save the portion of the game that is your responsibility. Let the infinite love that you touch in the inner silence move through you the way the contact moves through the channel. Join your infinity of love within to the infinity of love without, and let the channeling of infinite love occur. In the checkout line. In the argument. In the quiet kitchen at night.

He closes with encouragement for the struggling new instrument, and it reads like encouragement for anyone learning anything hard. Each entity has a unique voice, Hatonn says, and this voice too shall be a gift. Ours is a very simple message, he reminds them. We speak of the one great original Thought, which is love. Language is a poor thing when it comes to superlatives, but that is the message, and every life is one more way of expressing the inexpressible.

So my resting thought is small enough to carry. You do not have to get every catch. You only have to stay in the game. Sit on the mound between innings when you must. Trust that the game goes on. And let your life, ball by ball, become the channel.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Chord of Recognition
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the chord of recognition.

Mid-March, nineteen eighty-eight. The question is about the strange lights in the sky, the visions, the presences people feel and cannot explain. How do we make contact with these unseen energies? How do we become friends with them, and use what they teach us to serve? Q'uo answer at length, and their answer is both more cautious and more beautiful than the question expects.

First, the caution, and it is blunt. Phenomena are nothing but dust and ashes, they say, holding no meaning whatsoever, unless they strike within the heart of the perceiver the chord of recognition. That is the test. Not how bright the light was, not how impossible the vision seemed, but whether something in you answered. You are, in truth, light formed by divine consciousness, containing a gem that was, as your holy books say, before the world began. You do not need the phenomenon to give you what you already carry. You shall not learn, Q'uo say, but remember and recognize the truths that are already yours.

I love that line, the chord of recognition, because it puts the authority back where it belongs. Inside you. And it reframes the lights themselves. Many lights in your skies, Q'uo say, are there to advertise the mystery. To remind a sleepwalking humanity that it knows nothing. That science itself is built on what has been observed, not what has been understood. Some of these visitations are greetings from friends, they say, delegations come to wish a lonely wanderer well. Some are signposts. And some, they warn plainly, come from those on the negative path, and arrive wrapped in terror and control. The light is not the message. The feeling it leaves in your heart is.

Then Q'uo turn to the real question underneath the question, which is about service. How do we lighten the consciousness of this planet? And their answer is so undramatic it almost disappoints, until you sit with it. The most efficient tool, they say, is meditation. Prayer. Contemplation. The daily, persistent listening to the still, small voice. Within meditation the work is done. The entity more and more becomes a kind of being, glowing brighter in mute witness to the beauty of love. You may not notice the change. But those around you will. They will be blessed by the light that shines through you, by the focus that sees into the heart of each.

And right livelihood, the work you do with your hands all day? Q'uo say there is no gift, no thought, no action that cannot be sanctified by its dedication to the will of love. The service is the same whether you love one person or ten million, because the service is in the preparation of consciousness. Serve in gladness, in whatever capacity you find yourself, so that those near you may witness a peace that cannot come from within this distressing illusion. Human faculties fail, they say. The love of the one infinite Creator is infinite.

The session closes with a question about Jesus, about whether he is the only way, and Q'uo answer the way they answer everything: the pattern he gave was unconditional love, and every road, however distant it seems, meets at last in that one place. So my resting thought is this. Do not chase the lights. Tend the chord within you that answers them. Do the quiet daily work. And let your life become the phenomenon.

Thank you for listening.

title: Ask for the Truth
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: ask for the truth.

Mid-March, nineteen eighty-eight. Another short session, and the new instrument is struggling again. Tired. Doubting himself. Angry at his own slowness. Hatonn's response to him is one of the kindest things in this archive, and it contains a sentence I want you to carry away with you.

First, the encouragement. Hatonn tells him, and tells all of us who are learning anything difficult, to be our own taskmaster in the best sense. Bring to your practice a honed singleness of purpose. Move harmoniously with your own requests. And then, on the other side of that high-sounding coin, keep the cheerful laughter of imperfection. The channel, Hatonn says, is like the color sparkling off the facets of a diamond. Each glint is unique in its spectrum. So are each of you distortions of the white light, and so is every attempt you make. The falling down is guaranteed by the illusion. Laugh at it. Forgive yourself for it. Then look upward again.

I love how Hatonn refuses to let the student confuse the answer with the truth. Ask for the truth, he says, not the answer. For that which your peoples call the answer is never the truth. What is true is infinite, and your peoples measure and weigh the finite. An answer closes the question. The truth keeps it open and keeps you growing. When you sit down to learn, to meditate, to ask anything that matters, ask for the truth and let the answers be what they are: small cups drawn from an endless well.

There is a moment of pure delight tucked into this session that I have to share. The instrument challenges the contact, as she always does, and this time something in Hatonn's energy makes her laugh. She asks, half teasing, whether she is speaking with a woman of Hatonn today, because the presence feels so feminine. And Hatonn answers, with what I can only hear as a smile, that in this particular contact they are indeed of a feminine nature, an individualized portion of the larger group. We are pleased, they say, to assist old instruments as well in renewing the ability to be patient, and also to giggle. The whole group laughs. It is a good reminder that the holy and the playful are not opposites.

And to the new instrument, berating himself for his doubts and his impatience, Hatonn offers the reframe of the session. There is much to learn, he says, from that which you call failure, and much to learn from that which you call success. Do not let the efforts that fall short disconcert you. Do not let the efforts that flow make you overconfident. Each new instrument finds times when the speaking is difficult, when the mundane world has drawn away the vital energy. That is not the end of the path. It is the path.

My resting thought is the sentence I promised you. Look upward to eternity, Hatonn says, and ask for the truth, not the answer. Whatever you are learning, whatever you keep stumbling over, bring it the singleness of purpose and the laughter both. Be the diamond, glinting in your own color. And let yourself be a beginner as long as you need to be.

Thank you for listening.

title: Two Kinds of Change
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: two kinds of change.

Late March, nineteen eighty-eight. A very short session, and Hatonn uses it to draw a distinction I have found enormously clarifying. There are, he says, two kinds of change moving through your life, and most of your suffering comes from confusing them.

The first kind is circumstantial change. The job shifts. The relationship ends. The money comes or goes. The weather of your outer life. The second kind is deeper, and Hatonn calls it by an unusual name. He calls it genetic change, meaning not your DNA but the organic, structural change happening in the depths of your being, the slow reprogramming of the whole person as you grow. These two kinds of change often arrive at the same time. And when they do, the mind does something very human: it takes the deep, weighty feeling of the inner change and glues it to whatever outer circumstance happens to be occurring. A small event gets loaded with enormous emotional weight that does not really belong to it.

Listen to how practically he puts the remedy. Sort the two out, he says. Determine, for any given upheaval, which level you are actually dealing with. The outer circumstance is a drama, an illusion, a play, lovely or not so lovely, put there to offer clues and hints and parables. The inner change is the real movement, and it is, in itself, quite neutral. It has little to do with happenstance. And if you can perceive that deep emotional content clearly, separated from the story the mind has wrapped around it, you can use it as clear energy, as fuel. Hatonn calls it a catapult for speeding the spiritual process. The same feeling that was muddying your judgment becomes the very thing that launches you forward.

The difficulty, he is honest about this, is that once the two get linked in the mind, the lessons get muddied and progress slows. You cannot think your way out of a deep inner shift by fixing the outer circumstance, because the outer circumstance was never the point. It was the costume the inner change wore when it knocked on your door.

So what do you do instead? Hatonn's answer is the one he gives in almost every session, and I never tire of it. Practice the daily, spiritually directed inner silence. The listening ear, tuned to words that cannot be heard, concepts deeper than any clothing of vocabulary. In the short run, he says, with a paradox I love, this source of peace becomes the facilitator of strife in the long run, because the one who meditates is speeding up the very process of inner change. You sit in stillness, and the stillness accelerates the transformation. The physical being, he says, is finely tuned to respond to the needs of the whole spiritual entity that you are.

My resting thought is a question to carry into your next upheaval. When the wave hits, ask yourself: how much of this storm is the weather outside, and how much is the deep water moving underneath? Honor both. But do not ask the weather to explain the ocean. Sit in the silence, let the inner change do its work, and let the outer drama be what it is: a play, full of hints, staged for your learning.

Thank you for listening.

title: Not My Will
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: not my will.

Late March, nineteen eighty-eight, with Easter approaching and the story of Jesus heavy in the air. The circle asks Q'uo about the right use of will. Not willpower in the ordinary sense, but the deep faculty by which a soul directs itself. Q'uo answer by gazing at the one they call the teacher with the most enormous and generous will they have ever seen.

Think of Jesus, they say, moving through the final days of his story. The palms. The hosannas. And then, late in the night watch, alone, begging for release from what is coming, and praying the prayer that has echoed for two thousand years. Yet not my will, but thine. In worldly terms, Q'uo say, this was the wrong decision. It led directly to his death. In metaphysical terms, it was the moment will and faith became one, and the man became a crystallized being. The turning of the will toward the greater love did not weaken him. It completed him.

I want to sit with that, because it inverts everything we are taught about strength. We think of will as the clenched fist, the refusal to bend. Q'uo describe the highest use of will as the open hand. The will, yoked to faith, yoked to love, becomes something larger than stubbornness. It becomes alignment. And they are precise about what to have faith in. Not the social order, which is unstable. Not science and technology, which cannot explain the ground of their own field. The one thing every incarnate soul has implicit faith in, whether she names it or not, is love. You have all known love and the loss of love, joy and sorrow. It is more tangible than anything you can touch. And the love Q'uo mean is not the small loves. It is the unconditional love that created all that there is.

So the practice is this. When you would use your will purely, call upon love itself to teach your spirit that will and faith may be united. Let the thought live in the back of your mind through every decision: not my will, but thine. And know, Q'uo add with great tenderness, that the love to which you pray is your own self in a greater manifestation. It may have crossed your minds, they say, that you are all gods. We acknowledge with joy the truth of this. Only remember that we are all very young gods, and God's will is sometimes hidden from the surface of the young god's mind. Be patient with yourself as you learn.

There is no encouragement here toward blind obedience. Q'uo are explicit. They do not want you surrendering your judgment to any authority, including them. What they describe is subtler: as you meditate, as you grow thirsty for the presence of the Creator, you will find less and less paradox between the will of the self and the will of the infinite. The two were never really opponents. They were the same river, seen from different banks.

My resting thought is for anyone facing a decision where every option looks like a loss. Think back over the things in which you have faith, Q'uo say. You must have faith in something. Put it, then, in the one thing that has never failed you and never will: the love that made you. Intend. Desire. Want to be, as they put it, a not-so-very-young manifestation of love. That is all that is necessary. That, and the prayer: not my will, but thine.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Sacrament of Suffering
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the sacrament of suffering.

Easter Sunday, nineteen eighty-eight. The question the circle brings is the oldest one: what is suffering, why does it exist, and what can we do with it? Q'uo answer at unusual length, and with unusual fire. A gentle note before we begin, because this session speaks of chronic illness, of prejudice, of addiction, of the long sorrows people carry in their bodies. These voices speak about the soul's journey. They are not medicine, and nothing here replaces the care of those trained to heal the body or tend the mind. Hold that alongside everything that follows.

Q'uo begin by distinguishing two kinds of truth. There are the relative truths, the ever-shifting social and cultural agreements we use to slide through life with the least friction. And then there is Truth with a capital letter, absolute and unchanging, which cannot be seen but only known through the experience of love. Most human suffering, they say, does not live at the level of Truth. It lives at the level of the relative, where we measure ourselves against standards the culture invented. Q'uo are unsparing here. They speak of the suffering caused by prejudice of every kind, by rigid theologies that mark people unacceptable, by the judgments passed in the very name of the teacher who came to call the mocked and the despised. They could weep at it, they say. Ours is a planet of sorrow, even upon the joyous day of Easter.

But then they turn, and the turn is everything. Move out of the realm of the relative, they say, and into the absolute. Release the opinions of the world, and especially your own opinions about yourself. What is left when the wanting and the liking and the disliking fall quiet? Something naked. Something difficult. And something true. Beneath every relative truth shines the absolute: you are love. Not you have love, not you earn love. Each of you is love. This is your reality, your absoluteness, your unchangeable nature.

Listen to how they speak of Jesus in this session, because it reframes the whole Easter story. His kingdom, they say, was never the world of experience, of opinion, of cultural demands, of theological limitations. When he stood before his judge and was asked, are you a king, he answered, for this one purpose came I into the world, to bear witness to the truth. And when the judge asked, what is truth, Jesus only gazed into his eyes, and the judge saw the great I AM of love. The kingdom is within you, Q'uo say. It always was.

And suffering? Here is the sentence the episode is named for. Suffering, they say, is the sacrament, the food of spiritual evolution. Not a punishment. Not a debt to be paid for a reward later. Each difficulty is something arranged so that some distortion in our understanding of love may be examined and revised. Without the challenges there would be only a naive, unschooled joy. With them, rightly met, the soul grows. May you bless each wound, they say, each limitation, each pain. May you roll the stone away from the tomb of your limited acceptance. May you rejoice in your troubles even as you suffer.

The session holds one more exchange I cannot leave out. The instrument herself, who lives with constant physical pain, asks about the guilt she feels, the voices telling her she created her own illness and should be able to think her way out of it. Q'uo answer with extraordinary care. Before this life, they say, a wiser part of you chose the shape of this one, the way an oyster takes in the grain of sand that will become the pearl. Your limitations have let you turn inward more deeply than the outer life would ever have allowed. And the counsel they give her is not to strive harder for healing. It is to lay down the guilt. You chose this, they tell her, and it has served your purposes well. Let the guilt go.

My resting thought is their final image. Your heaven lies waiting within you, just as your hell waits to embrace you. The choice, moment by moment, is whether to follow the truths of the world or to enter the holy ground within, where you may see the face of your God, your Christ, your love. Bless the wound. It is feeding you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Inner Road to Peace
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the inner road to peace.

Early April, nineteen eighty-eight. The circle asks about the thing everyone was afraid of in those years: nuclear war. What energies build toward such a catastrophe? Are we capable of turning away? Q'uo answer, and their answer goes somewhere the question did not expect. Not to treaties or strategies, but to the human heart.

They begin with a startling claim about the past. Many walking the Earth now, they say, carry the memory, buried deep, of planetary catastrophes before this one, times when humankind destroyed itself and its world. The mass of group thought about that ancient error was never fully healed, and it still moves beneath our politics like an underground river. These energies, they say, will need healing until every soul involved has had the chance to balance the old misaction through self-forgiveness and the forgiveness of others. Listen to that. The road away from the bomb runs through forgiveness. Not the forgiveness of nations first, but of selves.

And they bring news, of a kind. The pattern, they say, is more hopeful than at any time since they began watching our nuclear age. More and more of those karmically entangled are finding their balance. The crisis may pass. They will not prophesy; they refuse to. But they encourage every effort at the conscious balancing of passion and wisdom within the individual mind, because that is where the war actually ends.

Here is the turn, and it is the heart of the session. This illusion, Q'uo say, including any catastrophe within it, was not designed to destroy or to build according to human whim. It was designed to offer opportunities for learning. And the most fertile ground for growth is often the unsettled times, the traumatic times, the confrontations. So do not check out of the world because it frightens you. Engage it. Be active within it. Not to overcome the illusion or to ignore it, but to meet every part of it in which you feel you have something to offer.

Then the sentence I want to set down carefully, because it is both a promise and a responsibility. When you are truly self-forgiven and at peace within, Q'uo say, you are doing planetary healing work. You are averting war. Your inner peace is not a private luxury. It is the road every person must travel, and when one person's inner peace meets another's, boundaries drop, hostilities end, and the realization of oneness occurs. Peace on Earth, they say, is possible, because humankind wishes to progress. Whether the possibility becomes reality, they will not say. They only ask each of us to hold peace within the mind, to take it into meditation, and to open the self to allowing self-forgiveness.

The session also holds a smaller teaching on fear that belongs here. Fear, Q'uo say, begins in the perception of separation, in seeing some part of creation as other than yourself and therefore threatening. It can motivate you for a while, and that is not nothing. But it is a distortion of the greater motivation available to you: the feeling of harmonious flow between you and your world, and the natural desire to move toward what you are in harmony with. When fear appears, do not flinch from it. Approach it the way you would approach any gift. Look until you find the moment the separation began, and meet it with acceptance, until the feared thing can be seen in a more compassionate light.

My resting thought is the one Q'uo leave us with. This little planet, with its wars and rumors of wars, is not, as the teacher said, the kingdom. The kingdom, the absolute, the truth, lie within, whole and perfect and dimly perceived. Through crisis and contemplation, each seeker ripens. And each time you forgive yourself, truly, you are voting for the world to continue.

Thank you for listening.

title: Rosa Mystica
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: rosa mystica.

Late June, nineteen eighty-eight. Hatonn comes to speak about love, and he begins with a line of poetry. My love is like a red, red rose. He gives the thought to the channel knowing she will question it, and then he unfolds it, petal by petal, thorn by thorn.

That which is created is pure beauty, he says. Yet its attainment is often moot. Weeding around roses, the instrument knows the sore fingers that come from the thorns. So it is with love. Not an easy beauty, but a beauty that may create both infinite joy and temporal pain. Such is the nature of love's expressions within your density. Each of you is a hunter in search of its prey, and the prey is love. The trail begins with the shallowest images the word has been given, the sentimental versions, and leads somewhere far beyond them.

Listen to how he widens the frame, because this is where the session becomes extraordinary. Love is not only in the sentimental, not only in the romantic, not only in the sufferings that prick the finger. Love is to be seen in every possible substance in the universe, no matter what it is. Not only the fresh fruits you eat are divine love, he says, but also what the body casts off after it has taken what it needs. The whole illusion is a swirling mass of love, constantly rearranging itself into patterns, coherent and intelligent. The question is never whether love is present. The question is whether the eye has learned to see it, in peace and in war, in richness and in poverty, in saintliness and in the blackest soul.

And then the turn inward, the one that gives the episode its name. So many seekers, Hatonn says, ask the Creator to show them love as though it were something brought in from outside, to be beheld like a picture on a screen. But if the whole of love is infinite, then each of its parts is also infinite. You are not only the beholder of the rose, he says. You are also the rose. The mysterious rose. The rosa mystica. This is your inner nature. This is your seed.

How do you tend such a seed? Not by chasing it into higher and higher realms, farther and farther from your own imperfections. You encourage a seed, Hatonn says, the way you encourage any seed: with the manna of sunshine and water. The seeds of love will grow in you as you pay attention to the most mundane duties and responsibilities, the pleasures and the pains of an ordinary day. The suffering you meet is the dead matter sloughed off, returning to the larger infinity of impersonal love. The attitude informs the eye, not the eye the attitude. See rightly, and the world renews itself before you.

There is a practical teaching here too, about romantic love, which the session treats with unusual honesty. The emotional intensity that draws two people together makes the catalyst between them more vivid, more deeply driven into the conscious mind, so that each may learn more pointedly from the other. But disappointment follows those who expect that intensity to remain steady forever. It was never the destination. It was the doorway. And beneath every form of love, Hatonn keeps returning to the one that matters most and is hardest to practice: the love of the self. So many, even those who pour love out to others, fail to accept the Creator's example toward themselves. Love the self, he says, as the Creator loves. Let the flower blossom inward first, and it will heal you.

My resting thought is his closing image. Gaze at the incarnation before you, quietly and realistically. Find the bubbling spring of love within, the God-self that calls to infinite love. Such enthusiasm is infectious, Hatonn says. Love may be transmitted from person to person. And as one after another joins the host of those who move in harmony with universal love, the face of the Earth is renewed, and the Creator is gladdened.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Outward Turn
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the outward turn.

Late June, nineteen eighty-eight. Hatonn looks at the circle and names what he sees: a malaise, a lack of passion. He is quick to say he does not mean it as criticism. He knows each of them is deeply passionate underneath. He is holding up a mirror. And then he speaks about passion in a way I have never heard anywhere else.

Passion, he says, is the fusion of two powerful forces: purified emotion, and the free will that chooses to stand behind it. Not raw feeling alone. Not willpower alone. The two fused. The most familiar form is the physical kind, and Hatonn honors it plainly. Because the body cannot speak, passion is most often felt in the body first, and this, he says, is as it should be. It is the cornerstone of the illusion that physical passion brings people together. But the same fusion lives at every level. Each of you, he says, is passionately devoted to pursuing the mysterious face of a beloved but invisible Creator. That is the great affair underneath all the smaller ones.

Listen to what he says about time, because it reframes the whole spiritual life. In third density, you are learning to use time. And in time, there is the capacity to intensify what you think, or to disperse it. To intensify a feeling, or to let it scatter. Your life is the slow art of finding your own passion, your own heart, your own true ground. And the way to feed it is simpler than the seeker wants to believe. The most efficacious exercise, Hatonn says, as always, is meditation. The will that drives you to sit daily is itself the free choice intensifying the emotion of love. Where there is the will, the meditation follows, and not only in the sitting. Again and again through the day, and sometimes in the night watches, the heart turns back to the fire.

Then he gives the image this episode is named for. Picture a circle of people holding hands, facing inward, each gazing into another's eyes. The energy moves around the circle, hand to hand. That is beautiful, he says, and it is necessary. Never stop holding hands with the companions you have been blessed with. But those who truly wish to serve will do one more thing. They will turn outward, still holding hands, still connected, and let the energy move in the other direction, out toward the world. Facing outward and offering, without expectation, whatever they feel they can give. Vulnerable. Open. The Creator shining through, that light may be seen in a dark world.

I love the permission inside this teaching. What is your passion, Hatonn asks. Let each ask, and then pursue it deeply, persistently, daily. And if on some morning you can find no passion within, do not be discouraged. It is simply time for the comedy, the laughter, the lightness, the bubbling over which is the easy side of passion. When you laugh, he says, you are the Creator. When you serve others, you are the Creator, his face to another who knows the Creator not, but who knows you.

He closes with counsel for the doubtful, and it is tender enough to speak aloud to yourself. Encourage yourself. Speak well of yourself to yourself. The statements you make about yourself to yourself determine your incarnational experience. If there are wounds to be healed, pray without ceasing, communicate persistently, until there is peace. Let that blocked energy move, for it is the deepest part of your passion. And for every serious thought, he adds, laugh at the absurdities of the illusion, the dear eccentricity of humankind. Hone your passion like a weapon, he says, a weapon to pierce most sweetly the hearts of those ready to receive love and light and life and joy.

My resting thought is a question and an invitation. Where does your passion lie? Not the borrowed enthusiasms. Yours. Turn outward with it, hands still joined to those you love, and offer it without asking what comes back. That is what service to others is all about.

Thank you for listening.

title: The One Message
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the one message.

The first of August, nineteen eighty-eight. A bright noon session, unusual for this group, with television lights glaring and a room full of new instruments learning to channel. Laitos comes to work with them, and most of the session is practice: adjustments, pauses, first contacts, the awkward beautiful beginning of learning to speak for another. It would be easy to call this a session about technique. But running underneath the logistics is a teaching about what channeling actually is, and it is worth hearing.

Laitos open with the sentence I have built this episode around. There is only one message, they say. There is only one truth. But there are an infinite number of ways to express that truth. And therefore each new channel is, to them, an infinite treasure. Not a mouthpiece. A treasure. A unique collection of biases and experiences and notions through which the one message can be spoken in a way no one else could possibly speak it. The contact supplies the concepts, Laitos say, but the conscious channel makes a substantial contribution of vocabulary and thought. It is a true partnership. I love that framing, because it honors both sides of the mystery: the source beyond, and the very human instrument through whom it must pass.

There is tenderness here for the beginner's doubt, and I want to linger on it, because it is really about any beginning. Again and again the new instruments falter. One hears the name but cannot speak it. One's heart races. One stutters, repeating the contact layer upon layer to be sure it is real. Laitos are endlessly patient. The beginning of the process is not the end of the process, they say. The first contact is not the ultimate contact. Allow the ambiguity to continue without concern. Doubts will return even in experienced instruments, and each return is another foundation stone being set more firmly. The whole art, they say, is learning to surrender the self in the faith that there is a service of a positive nature to be rendered.

Two smaller teachings from the question period deserve keeping. Asked whether humanity will one day become a social memory complex with a name of its own, Laitos smile at our fondness for naming. Names, they say, are chosen only when they are needed, fitted to the vibration the name must carry. In the density toward which you are moving, naming will be unnecessary, for all thoughts will be transparent. And asked what tires an instrument, they answer with the concept of vital energy, the elan vitale, the sum of mind and body and spirit. What drains it, more than anything, is unprocessed catalyst, the difficulty you keep circling without learning from. Process your days honestly, they suggest, and the energy returns.

My resting thought is the question Laitos leave for every new instrument, and it applies far beyond channeling. Examine the desire, they say. Find within yourself the primary reason you want to serve, and if you can heartily endorse that reason, build upon it everything you are. Let that purpose become the signpost of your inner being, the thing you offer as your challenge to every spirit you meet. Whether your service is speaking for the unseen or raising children or mending what is broken, begin there. One message. Infinite voices. Yours among them.

Thank you for listening.

title: Know Your Muse
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: know your muse.

The second of August, nineteen eighty-eight. A special session, recorded on video, though the video never survived. The question is the one this whole series quietly asks: what is channeling for? What is it worth, weighed against every other way of seeking truth? Q'uo answer with unusual fullness, and at the center of their answer is a word you may not expect. Muse.

First, the partnership. Channeling, Q'uo say, is the collaboration of the highest and best within the channel with a deeply impersonal source of love. The two are equal partners, growing in friendship and mutual respect. The channel brings discernment, the challenger’s care, the unique vocabulary of a lived life. The contact brings the larger point of view. And the message, when it is real, is always the same simple one: unity, perfect compassion, the reality of peace and joy woven through the illusion and transcending it. We urge people first into meditation, Q'uo say, into the quiet where the seeker learns to feel well about the self. Only then does service come, and it comes naturally.

Now the muse. Each seeker, Q'uo say, will discover within herself certain avenues of inquiry that hold a special power and glory, interests that grip harder and longer than others. The poet hearkens to words. The artist to the canvas. The parent, they say beautifully, hears the muse of Mary in the raising of children. Some few hear a stranger call, an odd philosophical muse with no name among our peoples, and those are the ones drawn to this work of channeling. Know your muse, Q'uo say. Whether it be justice, honor, beauty, or fairness, know it, and ask what relation it bears to truth. For truth is what we are here to discuss and to dwell in, not a truth of words, but a feeling tone, a validity that begins to be created within each person. Truth is not without you. Without you is illusion. Truth lies within you.

I love how unsentimental Q'uo are about the difficulties. They do not hide that this path attracts opposition. As a seeker polarizes toward service, the light becomes visible on levels most of us never see, and there are those who would dim it or turn it to their own uses. But Q'uo refuse fear as a response. These temptations, they say, are the normal balancing mechanism of growth, the desert every serious seeker must cross. Meet them the way the teacher met his: firmly, without hatred, and let them strengthen your resolve. And understand this mercy: even the negative path ends. At the far end of wisdom, the separate self must at last see other selves as itself, and turn. In the end, they say, there is only one path.

The session closes with two images I want to leave you with. The first: as the conscious entity opens its eyes, the love of the infinite shines through, and as it holds out its hand, the Creator touches person to person in intimate caring that the infinite cannot effect by itself. Yours is the manifestation. Yours the experience. Now is your time to choose. The second is from Yadda, who bursts in at the end with his rough joy to underscore what the long session kept circling: do not be solemn in your seeking. Laugh. Find the jolly times. Believe whatever you believe passionately, wholly, without the hunger for reputation.

So my resting thought is Q'uo's question, turned back to you. What is your muse? What is the voice within you that speaks most clearly of truth? Follow it. Let your work become your joy and your joy your work. And know, as they promise, that the kingdom of heaven lies within you, and has been waiting there all along.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Rough Voice
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the rough voice.
