The fourth of August, nineteen eighty-eight. A session unlike any other in this wave, and I want to tell you honestly what happens in it before we go further. Q'uo open with a short, luminous teaching. Then a contact called Yadda takes a new instrument, and what comes through is wild: loud, raw, full of old rage from a past life of war, and of hatred toward an entire people. It is uncomfortable to hear. The group sits with it. And then, slowly, something turns. I tell you this because the turn is the teaching, and because this series has never flinched from the rough passages. What follows is my best attempt to hold this session with care.

First, Q'uo's opening, which deserves to stand on its own. The truth, they say, is very simple, and always the same. And yet there are as many ways to explain it as there are entities seeking it. Do not be disheartened, they say, though the way is long and the ultimate truth forever recedes just beyond your grasp. Treasure the pearls that resonate with clarity in your own deep being. Hold the truth inside yourself and keep its flame burning brightly, for it will be a beacon to those around you who want to seek but cannot yet see the way. We are all pilgrims, they say. May we each hold our own particular beacon, and join our light to the light of all others, to brighten the planet beneath our feet.

Then Yadda comes, through a new and willing instrument, and the session becomes something else entirely. The delivery is explosive, swinging between roaring and whisper, full of laughter and old pain. And at the center of it, Yadda tells the truth about a past self: a life of war, of killing, of hating a whole people with a hatred that consumed everything. Yadda does not excuse it. Yadda names it as baggage, carried for a long time. And then comes the sentence that changes the weight of everything: I love them now, Yadda says, because they taught me what hatred was, and when I hated, I found out what love is.

Listen to that turn carefully, because it is the whole spiritual path in miniature. The hatred was real. The harm was real. And the soul, given enough time and enough suffering, alchemized it. Not by denying the darkness, but by going all the way through it and coming out the other side into love. This is what the archive keeps showing us in different costumes: that nothing in the soul's history is wasted, not even the worst of it, if it is finally faced and transformed.

What moves me most, though, is how the circle responds. Hatonn comes afterward, steady and kind, concerned first that the new instrument be released cleanly from the intensity, advising him to ask for the highest contact he can carry in a stable manner. No scolding of Yadda. No panic. Just care for the instrument, patience with the rough contact, and trust that with experience the voice will steady. Latwii, who had been standing guard during the wildest passages, simply note that they enjoyed the humorous aspects, and that the entity is quite capable of learning. The whole response of the group is the teaching: meet the rough thing with steadiness, and give it time to refine itself.

My resting thought is for anyone carrying their own baggage, their own old hatreds, their own past selves they would rather not name. Yadda's story says the darkness is not the end of your story. It may be the very material from which your understanding of love will be made. Hold your beacon. Keep walking with the other pilgrims. And trust that even the roughest voice, given patience and love, can learn to sing.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Green Cathedral
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the green cathedral.

It was the hot summer of nineteen eighty-eight, and the air was thick with talk of the greenhouse effect. The circle asked about the weather, about what shape the planet was in, and whether any of it could be undone. And Q'uo answered, as they often do, by gently declining the question as asked.

What we cannot tell you, they said, is the precise state of the planet. What we can tell you is that stasis is not a natural state. Change and evolution are. Entire portions of your planet have been unviable in the past, they said, and they shall be again. That which comes into being will dissolve into the dust from which it was formed. This is true of your planet, and true of each of you, in the physical sense.

But here is the turn. The Earth itself, they said, does not fear change, even the change you would call catastrophic. It lies within the power of the Logos. It is imbued with love, wishing only to give and to receive that love. So they encouraged the circle to refrain from fear with something like the faith of the forest itself, which does not have self-consciousness, but knows only the love and the light of the infinite Creator.

I love the way they name the trees. The forest, they said, is a green cathedral. Think about that image. The cathedral with no roof. The church with no walls. They say the planet is a service-to-others planet, and they point to the most obvious proof. The trees breathe in what you breathe out, and breathe out what you breathe in. Loving, serving, giving. That is the nature of the second-density world under your feet.

The heart of their answer is practical, and it is smaller than you might expect. If you want to aid the planet, they said, begin with the being that walks upon the grass, aware, and thanking the Earth for its energy. A song sung in love aids the flower. A soft voice helps the vegetables grow. They mean this literally. The consciousness of the planet rejoices and flows in harmony with anyone whose attention to it is loving and sweet. Even your physical body, they note, is itself a second-density creature.

And then they say the sentence I would underline. What you would do to aid the planet, they said, is precisely what you may do to aid the cells of your second-density body. The deepest and most profound change you may make within the planet is the change you make within yourself. For you may feel that only your feet touch the planet, they said, yet it is your heart which touches the heart of the planet, and the heart of the planet and the heart of the self touch the heart of the great Self.

Listen to how they put that. It is one of those sentences that keeps unfolding the longer you sit with it. Your heart touches the heart of the planet. The planet's heart touches the heart of the great Self. The line between you and the world is thinner than you were taught.

They are not asking you to save the world by force of will. They are asking for something smaller and harder. To walk upon the earth and bless it. To admire what they call the accidents of the day, the blooms that have been freely given, whether there is an eye to see or no. To find affirmations you actually believe in, and repeat them often. Or simply to tell the earth, the tree, the bush, the flower, the plant about you, mentally or out loud, those three words. I love you. Enjoy the sun. Enjoy the rain. You give me pleasure.

They close with a blessing and a caution in equal measure. Fear not, they said. The sphere itself will do whatever is necessary, including major surgery, to adjust to new vibrations and to thrive and grow in consciousness, in love and in personhood. The caution is aimed at us, not the planet. To be concerned about weather and catastrophes in a macrocosmic way, they said, is to miss the point. Be concerned in a microcosmic way. That is, the death of the self. The love you do not give. The light you do not let through.

And they left one hopeful note, which is strange and lovely. They said the planet had reached a critical mass for raising its consciousness, helped along by wanderers who chose the arts, especially the music, to say what they had to say. The great planetary concerts, the days of peace and forgiveness. These, they said, had helped in an exponential fashion. You can take that as you like. Their advice stays the same either way.

May each of you place your feet upon the earth and know it to be holy ground. That is their parting line, and I have no improvement to make on it. May your heart move in rhythmic consciousness with all that is. May you seek that all-consciousness daily in the silence, for there in the silence shall be the response to every question that is most true for you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Two Horns
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the two horns.

Early in September of nineteen eighty-eight, the circle asked Q'uo about paradox. How does the seeker balance the opposites. Passion in the seeking, and yet discrimination in the seeking. Love and giving, and yet wisdom about how to give. The conscious and the unconscious mind. The receptive and the active. All of it. And Q'uo's answer is one of the most beautiful treatments of paradox in the whole archive.

They begin where they often begin, with oneness. Since in the beginning all things were one, they say, the nature of paradox is difficult to comprehend. Yet the serious seeker meets it again and again. Service to others makes one feel good, therefore it is service to self. That is their example. One sentence, and the whole knot of spiritual life is in it.

Then they turn to passion, and here their language catches fire. Each of you, they say, has a heart, a center of being, and in that center, beneath all the dust and rubble of sadness and sorrow, pain and suffering, and the petty details of mundane life, lie the fiery jewels of passion. That creative force, they say, sleeps within from the beginning of creation. That of you which is of God is passion in its most manifest expression. So passion is not something you strive for, they say. It is something you look within for.

I love that image, the fiery jewels under the dust and rubble. It suggests that nothing is missing. Nothing needs to be imported. The treasure is already buried in the center of the house, and the work is excavation, not acquisition.

But they are honest about the opposite horn. For every passion, they say, there is skepticism, and it is different for each seeker. In love, in work for society, in devotion to a path, the skepticism arrives. Sometimes it is deserved, they admit, and often it is not. The illusion, they say with dry wit, lacks paradox only to those who have not thought about the illusion. The more one thinks about one's relationship with the Creator, the more one is plunged into a series of paradoxes.

Listen to how they picture the spiritual life then. Not a straight road, but a spiral, like the double helix this instrument called DNA, that tiny intelligence able to build an entire body for a soul to use. And in one incarnation, they say, the balance between passion and skepticism may be correcting an imbalance toward one side or the other in a previous incarnation. You do not go around in small circles, they say. Each day there is the seeing of new things. And if this be not so, it is time to look for paradox.

Their advice on the matter is worth quoting almost whole. Ceaselessly seek your passion, they say, whether it be an established path toward the face of mystery, or whether you make it up as you go along. That which is your truth, that which is your passion, will develop, resonate and become passion. It does not normally spring full-blown. It grows. And it is well, they say, to expect the movement back and forth between the two horns of any paradox. Upon the one horn is eternity. Upon the other, infinity. Upon the one hand, yourself as a portion of the Creator. Upon the other, yourself as you perceive yourself.

Then they offer the two counsels together, and this is the practical heart of the session. They urge skepticism whenever there is the slightest doubt that the path one is on is the correct one. And they urge those who already have faith and passion and care deeply about their paths, ceaselessly to examine with the powers of skepticism and the rational mind what the mind feels about that passion. But the mind, they note, is not a passionate being. It is, in this instrument's phrase, a biocomputer. It will analyze the experience of worship and love, and that is fine. The mind has a part in the evolution of the spirit.

But to grasp with the mind that which is occurring in spiritual worship, they say, is to ask the impossible of the linear mind. Therefore there must be a bridge between the two. And that bridge, of course, is meditation. Sometimes duty is honor. Sometimes duty is only duty, and you must take time for yourself. The balance is found day by day by day, by staying focused on the treasure of life itself, the treasure of consciousness.

There is one more line I want to give you, because it reframes the whole session. The easiest passion to understand, they say, is the passion of the sexes. But passion of every kind, mental and spiritual passion included, unites and strengthens and teaches, and also, inevitably, much hurt will be shared. That is not a warning against passion. It is the price of it, and they think it worth paying.

So the session ends as it began, in paradox, and in silence. They pause the speaking for meditation, hoping, they say, that the outline may in some degree be helpful. It is. The two horns are still there, eternity and infinity, passion and skepticism. The task is not to choose one horn and saw off the other. The task is to keep moving between them, spiraling upward, seeking the passion ceaselessly, and examining it honestly, and letting the silence bridge what the mind cannot join.

Thank you for listening.

title: The True Selfishness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the true selfishness.

In September of nineteen eighty-eight, the circle asked Q'uo about selfishness. And Q'uo opened, characteristically, by confessing to the charge themselves. It is most selfish, they said, that we are here, for by our choice of serving you, we find the possibilities of accelerating our own spiritual growth much improved. Thus, they said, we are being selfish as well as unselfish, when we speak in groups such as your own.

The question of selfishness, they say, has its root in the question of self. There is one Self, and that one Self is love, and therefore one is always serving the self. Hold that thought, because everything that follows hangs on it. Within the illusion, each person moves into incarnation with a predetermined character, a biased way of hearing and perceiving. Some have little capacity to register the difficulties of others. This looks like selfishness. It is, they say, not a selfish behavior at all, but a constitutional way of being.

Between the extremes lie the vast majority of souls. Entities whose personalities are constitutionally capable either of self-involvement or involvement with others. For them it becomes a matter of choice. Whether to serve the self by controlling and manipulating others, or to serve the self by serving others. That is the whole field of play, in one sentence.

They are unsparing about the first option. To serve the self by manipulating others is the negative path, the left-handed path, in which the self is seen as the equivalent of, or substitute for, the Creator, and everyone else as potentially useful. Such entities, they note dryly, are not known for their spiritual humility. And they warn of a subtler trap. It is easy to be enraged by the selfishness of another, and thereby to polarize negatively yourself, without ever noticing. Each entity, they say, creates its own universe by its reaction to the catalyst it receives.

I love the line that follows. One may please another, they say, but pleasing and serving other selves are two separate processes. That which you think is helpful may not be welcomed. That which is wished, you may not be able to perform. True service is harder than pleasing, and it begins somewhere most people do not look. Your basic service to others and your sense of self, they say, are the same thing. The beingness is the first act of selfishness or unselfishness, of radiance or absorption. The sum total of vibratory patterns generated by your thoughts, actions and feelings at any given moment, that is the gift you give to the Creator and the world.

Listen to how they put the practice. When your beingness touches in with the tabernacle of the most high, and a portion of your consciousness remains in that holy place, then all places are holy. All entities are of the Christ consciousness. And the eyes with which you look at those entities are eyes infinite in their ability to channel the one original Thought of the infinite Creator. Which is love.

Then they turn to the worry that haunts the sincere. Those highly oriented toward service to others often feel guilty about the time they spend working upon themselves. This, Q'uo says plainly, is not selfish, and do not for a minute think that it is. If you are to prepare and discipline your personality so that you may be of maximum service, a hollowing out process takes place. The concept of self as you know it begins to undergo a change. Never begrudge the time it takes to keep yourself clear of those things which block the energy from the heart.

The line the whole session turns on comes near the end, and they insist they are not playing with words. We find, they say, that the true selfishness is to choose the path of service to others. They have found it to be the quicker path, the easier path, and by far the more joyful path. The increasing lack of competition is most satisfying, they say, and the ability ultimately to merge together as one creative, collaborative being is infinitely gratifying.

So they ask each listener to do two things. Free the self from self-accusations of selfishness. And when you feel another is selfish, forgive and cease from judging, for who knows where the selfishness may lie and who must be forgiven in the final accounting. You are too hard upon yourselves, they say. That is almost their refrain across the years. You are too hard upon yourselves.

How interesting shall it be, they say, for each of you to gaze back over the pages of this incarnational experience and find how accurate you were in the many, many times you took your spiritual temperature. They promise your sense of humor will come to your rescue. It is a strange, warm ending to a session about selfishness. Be selfish, they are saying, in the truest sense. Choose the path that serves, and let the joy of it be your reward, and stop flogging yourself for the crime of working on your own soul.

Thank you for listening.

title: The First Great Healing
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the first great healing.

In September of nineteen eighty-eight, at a channeling intensive workshop, the questions came thick and fast. One of them was about healing. What are the principles for those who would offer themselves as healers. And Q'uo's answer is one of the great short teachings on healing in the archive. It begins with a sentence that reverses the usual order of things.

To those who would offer themselves as healers, they said, we can suggest that the first great healing be done upon the self. For as the healer is the vessel through which the healing energies move, the distortions that remain within the crystallized being will color everything that passes through. It is most important, they said, for each who would take that great honor upon their shoulders, to first offer the self as a purified vessel, hallowed and dedicated, that the light of the one Creator might move through the self clearly, and without distortion of any kind, to those who request the healing energies.

And then the second principle, which I think is even more startling. It is most desirable, they said, for the one serving as healer to offer itself openly, but without dedication to a certain outcome. The healer does not heal. The healer offers itself as a channel or vessel through which the healing energies of the one Creator shall move to the one requesting the healing. Offer yourself, they said, in an impersonal fashion, so that the energy moves through as purely as possible.

Think about what that asks of a person. To give everything, and to claim nothing. To be present, open, dedicated, and yet to let go of the result entirely. It is the whole spiritual path in miniature, and it is why they say the first healing must be your own. You cannot offer a clear vessel if the vessel is cracked and you have not tended the cracks.

The same session holds a teaching I want to give you alongside this one, because it belongs to the same question, really. What about suffering that does not get fixed. Disease, ecological damage, the sorrows of the planet. Q'uo was asked about the suffering of the world, and they answered with something I have thought about for years. The power of love, they said, moves beyond the power of reason and rationality, and offers itself without stint in order that whatever may be done be done with all the strength one has to give. And in the attempt, the heart and the will and the faith are strengthened in the metaphysical sense, so that the nature of the being is enhanced and ennobled.

And then the line. The attempt, they said, in the metaphysical sense, is far more important than completing the attempt in the physical sense. Read that again slowly. The attempt matters more than the completion. Your illusion, they said, is an opportunity to put to the test those principles which are the highest and best that you have chosen to live by. Whether the outer situation resolves is secondary. What is primary is that you tried, with everything you had, in love.

The workshop turned next to children, to those young in experience, and the counsel there has the same shape. Demonstrate as well as explain, they said. Whatever means you have chosen for your own spiritual journey, pursue them with purity and intensity, so that the young may observe the power of your faith and devotion moving in action through your life pattern. The actions of the parent, they said, speak in words and meanings far more profoundly and precisely than the actual words themselves. Balance the young entity's need for freedom of expression with the family's need for disciplined expression. It is not an easy balance, they admitted. But the sharing of the heart is worth the time it costs.

Near the end of the evening, someone asked about the unseen presences some had felt at the back of the room. Q'uo answered simply. In any circle of seeking such as this one, they said, there are always gathered many who are not seen by the physical eye, who lend their assistance in a variety of ways. Teachers, guides, friends of great intimacy, having known you for portions of time far exceeding this incarnation. They are here, they said, to bless and to give that which is theirs to give. The many faceted jewel of compassion and wisdom.

I love that phrase, and I love the picture it paints. The circle of seekers, tired, asking their questions, and behind them, unseen, a larger circle, leaning in. Q'uo said something at the very start of the evening that belongs with this. We are entities who have journeyed a distance which in your terms would be considered far, they said, and yet within the one creation we are as near as your breath. As near as your breath. That is the distance of all true help, in the end.

So the workshop's teaching gathers into one shape. Heal yourself first. Offer yourself without claim on the outcome. Let the attempt be the triumph. Live the teaching in front of the young. And know that you are not alone in the room, ever. There are more hands on the work than the visible ones, and every one of them is nearer than you think.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love's Own Armor
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love's own armor.

In October of nineteen eighty-eight, the circle asked Q'uo to speak about hatred. And Q'uo began, with unusual directness, at the root. That which is hatred and that which is anger, and all of those emotions which may be called negative, they said, are distortions of love. They manifest through the distorted individual by blocking energy and trapping it in the center involved in the difficulty. That is the whole theory in two sentences. Hatred is not the opposite of love. It is love, bent and blocked.

Then the line that gives this episode its title. Hatred, they said, is love which has been hurt badly. Anger is that which comes of hatred. Beneath the hatred is a blockage in the energy body, and this is especially painful, they said, when the entity who is in pain has some difficulty in experiencing self-worth and self-acceptance, self-forgiveness and self-love.

I want to pause on that, because it is doing something very tender. It refuses to make the hater a villain and the hated a victim in any simple way. It says, look underneath. What you will find is not evil. What you will find is an injury. Love, hurt badly, with nowhere to go. And the injury is always, at bottom, about the self. Can I forgive myself. Can I love myself. Everything else flows from the answer.

They are also honest about who feels these things most. When an entity is extremely positive, they said, the small catalysts that others would shrug off become painful. The sensitive seeker will use the tiniest slight as material and experience it as real anguish. They do not mock this. They do not tell the circle to toughen up. They say, we in no way disregard or lessen any of those emotions which are beyond the control of the entity at this time.

Beneath all of it, they say, is the concept of separation. The illusion is made of seemingly separate selves, and the veil has dropped between the waking vision and the evidence that each is also the Creator. Each is perfect and all one. One with each other and one with the original Thought of love. The hatreds you feel for another, they say later in the session, are only reflections of the feeling for the self. Each other person is truly a mirror of yourself. Thus, it is the self which must be turned to in forgiveness and total compassion.

So what is to be done, practically. They offer the easy way first, with a smile. The first action one may take, they said, is to outlast the length of time one is capable of feeling the same catalyst. Simply exist longer than the feeling. No effort required. But knowing the circle wants the harder road, they give it. Lower the expectations of the other. Remember the desire for the truth. Remember the desire to be positively oriented. And when the utmost effort fails, when you cannot love without distortion, then begin immediately to forgive. The other. The self. The situation. And the illusion itself.

I love that they include the illusion in the list of things to forgive. Forgive the whole setup. The game was designed as an ordeal, they say, a series of ordeals, within which again and again each soul chooses the positive path or the negative one. When the periods of darkness strike without warning, they are needed, for each entity has all of the varieties of humanity within the self. The most positive entity can be negative. The most negative can be positive. This illusion fools each as it ought and as it must.

There is a passage about marriage in this session that I want to handle carefully, because it may land close to home for some listeners. Q'uo, drawing on the instrument's reading of Joseph Campbell, says that marriage is an ordeal. It is through the great sacrifice of both entities that a marriage becomes a spiritual reality. The ceremony that seems to unite can create the illusion of separation, when expectations rise and each partner separates from the true self. If this touches a sore place in you, hear their tone. It is not judgment. It is description. And their counsel is the same as everywhere else. Lower the expectations. Forgive. Remember that the one before you is the Creator in disguise.

And then the armor. They speak of the breastplate of righteousness from the Bible, and all the other armor of love, and then they say it plainly. Love is its own armor. Those about whom you have distorted emotions cannot truly harm the self that is rooted in love, because there is nothing in that self for the distortion to catch on. That is the whole teaching in four words.

They close with the simplest instruction in the session, and the hardest. The first order of business, they said, is forgiveness of self. Do not attempt forgiveness beyond the self at first, but only work upon the self. Exercise your nature whenever you can, they said, giving each passing stranger a smile a bit longer, a bit wider, and from the heart. You will never know how many lives you touch by the gentle word, the kindly gesture, the gentle smile.

If this episode has stirred something painful, be gentle with yourself tonight. That is, after all, the entire teaching. The hatred was love, hurt badly. The cure was never to fight the hatred. It was to tend the hurt, in yourself first, until the energy could flow through to the heart again.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Comforter
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the comforter.

In October of nineteen eighty-eight, the circle asked a question Q'uo said they had been waiting for. Who are the entities that speak through our instruments. What is their nature, that they can come in the name of Jesus the Christ. And Q'uo's answer is one of the strangest and most honest self-descriptions in the archive. They begin with a joke, almost. We even gave our group a name, they said, which compassed the query. Our name in your Latin would mean literally, who.

Who. That is the whole of it, and they spend the session unfolding it. First, they describe themselves as manifestations. Citizens of various planetary groups, individualized, with physical vehicles, each with areas of specialization. Some speak to beginners, some to advanced students, some on healing. All of it, they say, is a mask and an illusion. Real, in a manner of speaking, but of limited duration. Such is the nature of manifestation. By its very nature it calls to infinity.

Then they turn to the Christ question, and here their answer is both generous and uncompromising. When any seeking entity discovers compassion, they said, that is to say, unconditional love, that entity has discovered and defined Christ. A Christ is a Christ, they said. To say Jesus is Lord is to say the obvious. For within the universe as they see it, they are identical to that which the instrument calls the Holy Spirit. We are then, they said, the Holy Spirit or Comforter, in this instrument's terms.

I love the breadth of that claim. They do not say Christianity is wrong. They say it is one true naming of something larger. For those of other belief systems whose journeys have led them to a certain purity, they said, we identify ourselves equally with that entity's deity, and come into relationship as those who may confess faith in this deity. The message is always the same, they said. The philosophy unified. The hope, inner peace, outer joy, and the productivity of the good vine.

They are candid about the theatrics, too. It matters not who entities think we are, they said. We attempt to satisfy the need for otherness, mystery and solemnity, and to indicate our polarity in a clear way. Were they to appear as themselves, they said, those of the Confederation would look most variously. They use the metaphors the culture offers, spacecraft or angels, whichever will be least abused and most heard. The wrapping is chosen for the audience. The gift inside is always the same. The one simple message of love.

And then the third nature, the one they knew would disturb the instrument. In our opinion, they said, we are completely within the instrument's mind. That is, the instrument has made a pathway deeply enough into its own subconscious levels of thought that it is able to contact principles which lie deep within the mind. The infinity and reality, they said, lie not outside, but inside the non-thing which is each entity's consciousness. All studies concerning an entity are studies in a mirror, the true self, the inner self, being invisible. One learns of the inner self by looking very carefully in the mirror.

Sit with that for a moment. The voices from beyond may be the depths of the self, speaking. Q'uo does not resolve the paradox. They deepen it. They say they are both. Both the far traveler and the inner principle. Both the Comforter from beyond the stars and the love already buried in the instrument's own mind. It is our understanding, they said, and forgive our use of that word, for we feel our grasp is limited, that the Deity, the Creator is one, and each distortion which moves entities into a life of faith is acceptable to us.

There is one more sentence I want to give you, because it reframes worship itself. It is the faith, they said, the peace, the inner surrender to the will of the infinite Creator which marks the one who has decided to become a servant of the Creator. For worship always produces the manifestation, not the manifestation the worship. Read that twice. The devotion comes first. The form the devotion takes follows. You do not find the holy and then worship it. You worship, and the holy appears.

They close by describing what they have become through long refining. We are those disciplined to the principle of love, they said, servant of All and lord of All, as the one known as Jesus was both servant and lord. We have refined and refined our natures to become one with the principle of Christ, the principle of love, that which moves the consciousness to the consciousness which is the Creator.

So who speaks through the instruments. Who. The Comforter. The Holy Spirit in Christian dress, the inner principle in metaphysical dress, the far friend in the language of the stars. The name changes. The nature does not. It is love, speaking, and asking only to be recognized.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Crooked Places
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the crooked places.

At the end of October of nineteen eighty-eight, someone in the circle asked the question every sincere seeker has asked in private. Is there any value in studying, in reading, in trying to apply everything learned, day to day. Or can you get just as far by being a nice guy and living an ordinary life. And Q'uo, who promised to be brief and was not, gave an answer that deserves to be heard whole.

Their answer, in short, is yes. For almost all of us, the conscious work is necessary. There are rare entities, they said, naturals, who come in with the maturity of many incarnations and need no tools to be true to themselves. But none of those to whom we speak, they said dryly, is able at this time to reflect that he or she is free of the need to accelerate the spiritual growth. So the work stands.

But they refuse the pious version of the work. Listen to how they widen it. The ambitious businessperson building a worldly kingdom, they said, is as much a practicing spiritual seeker as the mystic, for that which an entity considers its ambitions bent toward is that entity's true spirituality or religion. The piano student doing meaningless exercises for years is doing spiritual work, whether she knows it or not. And what the true artist and the true mystic have in common, they said, is the lack of an icon held in space and time. Both are fascinated by the mystery of the present moment, and seek in each and every moment the face of that mystery, the face that shall not be known, the ineffable face of the one Creator, the face of love.

I love that pairing, the artist and the mystic, shoulder to shoulder at the same mystery. It dissolves the boundary between the studio and the chapel. Whatever holds your attention utterly, whatever you serve with devotion, that is your altar.

Then the warning, and it is a bracing one. Do not assume, they said, that those who progress more quickly along the spiritual path shall find the crooked places made straight and the rough places plain. Instead, the mountains are higher, scaling them is more difficult, and the plunges into the opposite of the mountaintop experience are all too frequent. When one accelerates the process of learning, one accelerates the process of changing. One begins to die, losing this and that part of the self which is no longer true about the self, but merely that which has been kept and not thrown away. Much like old clothes stowed in boxes in the attic, gathering dust.

That image stays with me. The attic of the self. Boxes of old clothes you no longer wear but cannot seem to discard. The accelerated path is, in large part, the long labor of carrying those boxes down the stairs.

And here is the sentence the whole session turns on. The beginning of spiritual maturity, they said, is the acceptance at last that one is forgiven. Those who follow the well-known religions use various symbols for the principle of redemption. The one known as Jesus is perhaps the best example. But as each self is made up of the Christ consciousness and the free will consciousness, there is only needed a simple recollection by a very complex entity. And that which is called karma, they said, is not inevitable. It may be stopped by self-forgiveness. In the state of self-forgiveness, one may see all others as forgiven, regardless of their behavior at any particular moment.

What one knows in the head, they said, must be grounded in the heart. The reading and the contemplation and the discussion need to be followed by the listening, that one may hear that voice which speaks within. The key to the door, behind which wisdom and compassion lie, is meditation. If no book is read, if no symbol is imaged, if there is nothing in the worship but the most devout silence, yet still this vehicle alone may be all that is needed.

They close with two counsels held together, as they so often do. Take yourselves seriously in your seeking, they said, and yet at the same time retain that light touch which is part of the essence of self-forgiveness. And the work itself, they said, is not what the instrument calls goody goody. It is a life of deep caring, lasting compassion, and a love that comes not from the heart, but through the heart, from the Creator.

Not from the heart, but through the heart. That is the difference between the nice guy and the seeker, in the end. The nice guy loves from his own small supply, and runs dry. The seeker learns to be the channel, not the source. And the crooked places are not made straight by effort. They are made straight by forgiveness, received at last, and then extended to every other traveler on the road.

Thank you for listening.

title: Choose to Be Chosen
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: choose to be chosen.

In November of nineteen eighty-eight, the circle asked about the elect. The chosen. The ones the Bible says shall see the kingdom of heaven, the hundred and forty-four thousand, the new age talk of the chosen being lifted off the planet. Is this a valid concept, they asked, or a distortion of something else. And the answer came from an unexpected voice.

I am Ira, son of Mishdad, the speaker said. I come to you in the name of Jesus Christ. Not a member of the Confederation, but what you might call an ascended master. In the significant incarnation, he said, I followed Jehoshua, as he was called in his own dialect. You call this teacher Jesus. I was not worthy to touch his clothing, yet it was my joy to follow him.

What follows is one man's testimony, given through an unfamiliar channel, and it has the ring of lived memory. Along many dusty roads I walked, he said, trying to catch a word or two of his private conversations. When he spoke he spoke quietly, yet clearly, and with much authority, although he was always begrimed and dusty from the road. Somehow we all looked up to him without knowing why, even before we had heard what he had to say.

And his answer to the question of the elect is unequivocal. This is a grievous distortion, he said, of the true intent of Jesus' saying. The numbers of the elect are not exact, but symbolical in intention. It was the way of the rabbis to use numbers symbolically. The number twelve meant completion. Twelve times twelve meant a completion of completions. All eventually which have self-consciousness shall be of the elect, shall choose, shall be the seed planted in good soil. At the end of a given period, some shall be ready for the next step, and some not. That is all.

The concept of elitism, he said, of choosing one person above another, would have been inherently distasteful to my teacher. My Savior felt himself to be the least and lowest of any man, indeed, the servant of all. This compassion would never be stinted by such an idea as a true elite in which some children of the Father were invited into the mansion and others not. This is not so, he said. This is not true. This was not the intention of my Lord.

Then the sentence that gives this episode its name. Each who hears my voice, he said, may choose himself to be the elect, by choosing to live a certain kind of life, by choosing to attempt to be of service in the spiritual sense, by intention, in as much of the experience as possible. It is you who choose yourself. Yes, he said, there shall indeed be the elect, and you shall indeed elect yourselves.

I love the completeness of that reversal. No committee in the sky is sorting souls into the chosen and the rejected. The choosing is done here, by you, in the texture of an ordinary day, by intention. The election is not a status. It is a practice.

He had one more teaching before the contact faded, about the power of names. When a person chooses a different nature, he said, and becomes passionately bonded to that nature in such a way that it will change the life, and seals the change by a name, that is a name of power, because that is a person of power. When the seeker chooses a symbol for perfect compassion and divine love, the seeker must name the symbol. If your faith is in the Christ consciousness, then it is in that consciousness, and in that consciousness only, that you may be called elect. You must become your journey, he said, and your journey must become you, and the name of the consciousness that is your journey is Christ.

His parting charge is worth hearing slowly. Choose now, he said. Choose that symbol for which you would die. Choose that faith that is the I AM for you. Choose your consciousness. Choose to be a certain way. Choose to be chosen. If my teacher is not yours, he added, with a generosity I admire, then seek and find your true symbol, but let that symbol be the Christ to you, and seek to be the servant of all. For it truly is in serving that you shall grow, that you shall become strong, and that you shall be healed of all bitterness, sadness and grief.

Hatonn closed the evening, and his coda belongs with Ira's teaching, because it is about the same inner election. If you are a disappointment to yourself, he said, it is because you have not been good to yourself, but bad to yourself. You are the grade school child, adding the sums and getting an incorrect answer. Keep your eraser sharp, he said, and check those sums constantly. And when you find the error, use the eraser, but not the tongue in self-castigation for that self-same error. You are here to encourage yourself to be the willing servant, to feel the freedom of the joy of service.

Use the eraser, not the tongue. I can think of no better footnote to the teaching of the elect. Choose yourself, daily, by intention. And when you fail at it, as you will, erase gently, and choose again.

Thank you for listening.

title: A Small Christmas
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a small christmas.

It was the Sunday before Christmas, nineteen eighty-eight, and L/Leema came to speak of the season. They began, with characteristic honesty, by naming both faces of it. It is marvelous, they said, to observe the lightening of consciousness among so many during this season. It is equally true, they said, that this is the season which kills, which reopens remembrances of failures, of past grief, of recollective worry, of that which one wishes one could do over.

If that second face is the one you know best, I want you to hear the gentleness in what follows. Nothing here is a scolding. It is an invitation, extended to the tired, the grieving, and the lonely, as much as to the joyful.

There is, they said, a metaphysical rhythm to the year, reasons both for the elevated consciousness and the downcast consciousness during the short days and long nights. And at the center of the season's symbolism, they placed something I had never quite seen before. The infant Jesus, they said, recapitulates a process happening in you daily. For within each of you dwells the Christ, as a potential, as part of an eternal birthright. This small spiritual infant is being born, reborn, and nurtured each day within the incarnate self, mostly unrecognized, moving inexorably all the same.

And then the sentence that reorders your priorities. This infant soul, they said, is more your child and your responsibility than any child of your loins, certainly far more important than any other single consideration your mind may entertain. For this self is that vehicle which is, in a deeper reality, your Self. That continuing Self about which you know so little, and about which you desire to know so much more.

You are to be the parent of your own spirit. That is the whole teaching. Nurture it as you would a newborn. Give it sunlight, or the hope of sunlight in the depth of winter. For the soul, untended, is bleak, unfocused and half-forgotten, even in those who attempt to be conscious of it, for lack of some practical way to practice the awareness of it.

They offer an image for the work. It is like the carving of the elephant out of stone, they said. When the artist is asked how he finds the elephant within the block, he answers that he chips away everything that does not look like an elephant. In the same way, each entity sits within the illusion like a block of rock which has within it the perfectly faceted gem. The work is subtraction, not addition. You are not building the soul. You are uncovering it.

And the tool, as always, is almost offensively simple. Meditation. Not long periods, they said, nearly as much as a persistent dailiness of practice. That which occupies the mind daily, as an instinctive and reflexive recall, is learned in a way that the occasional cannot match. Turn the attention, daily, toward the holy. Use readings, mantras, whatever leads you toward the intention to tabernacle with the infinite mystery.

Then the line I want to leave ringing. The meeting together to share love is also a kind of Christmas, they said, and each day can be a small Christmas, if it is remembered that the Christ within is small, needs nurturing, needs attention, and needs most of all to be in the company of the infinite Creator. What you wish for at Christmas, they said, is not presents, as in gifts, but the presence. The communion with the infinite One.

Not presents, but presence. I have not been able to forget that wordplay since I first read it. All the wrapping paper in the world is a symbol, pointing at the one thing the season is actually about. Being with. Being with the mystery, being with each other, being with the infant light inside that does not yet know its own name.

They close with counsel for the dark days, whenever they come, at whatever time of year. Recreate within the mind, they said, the Christmas experience. Great darkness, short underlit days of shadow and bleak cold, and a piercing and poignant joy of that infant spirit that against all odds moves into darkness as light that is not recognized. You yourselves, they said, are full of light which you do not recognize. It is not sunshine. It is not light in a physical sense. You are the carriers of precious treasure. Picture it. Symbolize it within yourselves as the Christ child, and give it room, encouragement and attention, that it may grow each day.

You are full of light which you do not recognize. If you are spending this season, or any season, in the bleak cold they describe, hold that sentence like a small lamp. The light is not absent. It is unrecognized. And recognition, they say, is a practice. A dailiness. A small Christmas, kept within the heart, one day at a time.

Thank you for listening.

title: No Shortcuts
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: no shortcuts.

It was New Year's Day, nineteen eighty-nine, and the circle asked the question that belongs to every January. No matter what method of consciousness expansion a person tries, they said, spiritual growth seems to boil down to trial and error, and dealing with disappointment when we fall short of our ideals. Are there really no shortcuts. And what part do disappointment and faith play in the path.

Q'uo's answer is long, warm, and bracing, and I want to give you its spine. First, they said, it is extremely possible to accelerate the pace of spiritual growth, in almost any degree desired. If we did not believe that, they said, we would not be working with this instrument, for it is no part of our intention to waste our time. So the shortcuts, in a sense, exist. But here is the catch, and it is the whole session. The difficult manifestation of accelerated spiritual growth, they said, is emotional pain. Irritation with oneself for having failed. And other negative emotions.

The reason, they explained, is almost mechanical. In times of greatly accelerated growth, large-scale changes are being made in the deep programs of the mind, and the person undergoing it will seem to have become oversensitive, immature, imbalanced. This person will consider itself the least of all those who seek, they said, for it is not manifesting cheerfulness and freedom, but suffering under a burden. Yet when time has elapsed and one gazes back, one sees again and again the rapidity of growth, side by side and inexorably tied to the most nauseating and humiliating of failures.

I love that phrase, nauseating and humiliating failures, because it refuses to pretty up the process. Growth does not feel like growth while it is happening. It feels like falling apart. The memory, they said, winds its golden bands about these times afterward, and only then can you see what was actually occurring.

And then the sentence I would put on the wall. Yes, they said, you shall disappoint yourself again and again. And may we say, the more you disappoint yourself, the more you are trying to do, and the more we salute your brave spirit. Read that as a New Year's blessing. Your disappointment is not evidence of failure. It is evidence of attempt. The ones who never disappoint themselves are the ones who never reached for anything.

They are tender about the mechanics of self-attack, too. You are battling something you may well call disappointment, they said. We would prefer to call it the uninformed intellectual mind. Your minds are very full of opinions based only upon conventional wisdom. Within your heart are stored the natural laws. Let yourself be the nurturer of yourself, they said. When you are disappointed in yourself, let your nurturing self remember that you are only disappointed within the illusion. You have no idea, my children, of what a blessing your hopes, your intentions, and your ideals are. The light of those ideals is the light of your planet.

These things, they said, your zest for truth, your fidelity to the Creator, your living by faith, these things go beyond that self that carries you about. These things are what you really are. A being of faith. In times of disappointment, allow that being to nurture, protect, comfort and soothe you.

Then they offered their greatest hint for those who want to speed up, and it is the opposite of what you would expect. Learn, they said, to work as hard during those times perceived as positive as those times perceived as negative, and the negative events shall not need to occur. Push against your own standards of excellence when things are going well. Give more praise to the Creator in the happy hours. Program yourself for learning as you move into sleep. Work during the easy, the happy, the contented, and the peaceful times, they said, and your lives shall become ever more peaceful and contented.

It is a strange and practical magic. We tend to coast when life is good and pray only when it breaks. They are saying, do the work when you do not need to, and you will need the breaking less.

They close with a charge that belongs on the first day of any year. Claim your disappointments now, they said. Face them and learn from them and grow sweet with compassion. May each limitation, disappointment and seeming failure become for you the opportunity of self-forgiveness, appreciation of yourself, and the nurturing of your growing spirit. Then when, without the veil, you stand and gaze upon your life, you shall see that there is no such thing as earthly disappointment, but only the sounds, the experiences, the side products, the pain and the difficulties of transformation.

No such thing as earthly disappointment. Only transformation, wearing a frightening mask. May you grow sweeter through adversity, they said. May you intend always the highest and best that you know. That is their New Year's wish for you, and it is mine as well.

Thank you for listening.

title: The First Passion
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the first passion.

In January of nineteen eighty-nine, the circle asked Hatonn about passion. How does one develop it. How does one direct it for spiritual growth. And Hatonn, who is usually the gentlest of teachers, gave one of the most exalted discourses on love in the archive. It begins with a clarification that changes everything.

The first passion, he said, is not one for which you are responsible. The great and original passion is the passion of the Creator to know Itself. In that great passion, in that love, It created each of those portions of consciousness that sit in this circle this evening. It created each of you before time and space began, for time and space are but a stage upon which consciousness may play out its many roles and learn those lessons it has chosen to study, that the Creator may know Itself in the windows of each entity's eyes.

Sit with that. Before you ever felt anything, you were felt for. Before you ever loved anything, you were loved into existence. Passion is not a achievement. It is an inheritance.

And then the sentence I would underline twice. The first passion, he said, is that you are loved. You are loved enough to have been created. You are loved enough to have been given free will. And you are loved and trusted enough to be set completely and utterly free, your mind carefully shielded and veiled from the deeper portions of itself, so that you cannot remember who you are. The call to a life in faith, he said, is a call to remembrance of the passion that created you.

I love the economy of that. The whole spiritual path, reduced to remembrance. You do not have to manufacture love for the Creator. You have to remember the love the Creator already has for you. Everything else is commentary.

He draws a picture, he admits, of a seemingly needy Creator. A Creator needy for you, for your love, for your reactions, for your information. And in a biased way, he says, this is indeed so. You are portions of the active principle of the Creator, the Logos, love itself. You are, he says plainly, absolutely necessary to the Creator. You are timeless metaphysical entities, beloved with a passion so far beyond any of our words that he begs forgiveness for the poverty of language.

So how does one find this passion in daily life. His counsel is disarmingly concrete. Contemplate long upon the love the Creator has for you, he said, and then allow yourself, slowly and gently, to awaken to that love. Listen to the bird that sings for your ear, and yes, my children, he said, it does sing for your ear, if you can but listen. The breeze that blows so beautifully. The pearl-gray days that soften the harsh edges of winter moods. In all these experiences, remember that this has been a gift of love, and that you are completely satisfying your Creator, no matter how quickly or slowly you advance, simply by being, and reacting in a natural way, to those things which occur.

Simply by being. No performance review. No quota. The bird sings for your ear whether you are enlightened or not, and your hearing it is enough.

He names what blocks it, too, and his diagnosis is brief. What are those things that stop one most quickly from feeling, he asked. Primarily, my friends, it is fear that keeps one from feeling. Fear about livelihood, fear of gain and loss in relationships, fear of learning more about a subject one distrusts. Identify the fears, he said, and allow them, once found, to fall away gradually, so the change is not too uncomfortable. Then turn the attention within, to the light, and without, to the beauty that speaks in the creation.

And he gives the weary a practice for the days when meditation feels impossible. If you are not satisfied with the level of your desire to seek, he said, you may simply dance or sing or move or run or swim, or do anything which moves one past one's limits. Then sit and meditate again. Some of the veil will have been lifted, because when one is quite exhausted, the seat of consciousness rests far more in the subconscious mind. There it is that feelings are stored. There it is that passion lies waiting for its remembrance. The key, he said, is remembrance.

He closes with an image from the holy work, the bridegroom and the bride, and says there is no more intense passion on the physical level than that which draws a mated couple together. This same level of passion, he said, is felt for you by the infinite Creator. May you feel the stars laugh, he said. May you feel the joy of the seeds beneath the ground, resting, hoping, seeking that first warmth. May your hearts lie fallow, and your souls seek the light as the seed beneath the ground.

You are beings of great passion, power, strength and majesty, he said, yet also completely free to express in whatever manner you wish. It is a subject for thought, is it not. It is. The first passion was never yours to earn. It was yours to remember. And remembrance, practiced daily, becomes the dance of the heart he promised at the start.

Thank you for listening.

title: The First Business
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the first business.

In January of nineteen eighty-nine, at an intensive meditation, Laitos came to speak to those learning the disciplines of service. Not only channeling, they said, but any work done with a completely open heart. Healing, art, music, dance, architecture. All the expressions of aesthetic authenticity spring from an entity who knows who he is and what his ideal is.

And then they stated the principle that gives this episode its name. To know yourself, they said, to forgive yourself, and to love yourself is the first business at hand. This forgiveness needs to be complete. For if you are to love and serve another, you are to love and serve them as you would yourself. If you do not love yourself sufficiently, how shall you love another.

I want to stay with that sentence, because it is so often quoted and so rarely taken seriously. The first business. Not the second, after you have proven yourself useful. Not the reward at the end of the path. The first. Before the service, before the art, before the healing of others, there is the healing of the self, and the setting of the goal. Everything else is built on that foundation, or it is built on sand.

They are unsparing about what the path costs, and I respect them for it. Service to others begins with the self, they said, for all about you are faces of yourself. Those things which most distress you about others are the reflection of yourself, and each relationship is like a mirror in time, moving with you along the river, showing you your own face. And the seeker, they said plainly, may not have the luxury of a simple path, nor of a path without conflict. For the most part, when one is seeking the truth about the self and the Creator, one is rather uncomfortable, confused, pondering, wondering and doubting.

We are sorry to tell you this, they said. We would like to paint a rosy picture. Yet we must begin by explaining that there are costs to this work. And one of the costs is this. If one is to express love and service to others, so it is that one must love the self in a final and holy way. For you are divine, each of you. Not in your earthly form, but wrapped deeply within you lies the infant babe that is your pilgrim spirit.

There is a line here I want to give you whole, because it is one of the most practical counsels in the archive. Whenever you catch yourself being negative about the self, they said, remind yourself that you are an orphan on a very unusual planet, and that you must mother yourself and nurture yourself and care within your heart for yourself, until those sore and painful places are indeed nurtured and healed at last.

Mother yourself. Not judge yourself, not improve yourself, not whip yourself into shape. Mother yourself. It is an image of infinite patience, of someone who does not flinch at the wound and does not rush the healing. Until, they said, there is forgiveness and redemption within the knowledge of the heart, not only of the mind.

They spoke too of tuning, the idea of the self as a receiver and transmitter. And their counsel on desire is worth hearing carefully. Sharpen and hone your desire, they said, for it has been written truly, seek and ye shall find, ask and it shall be given to you. But be very, very careful about that for which you would ask, for it is divine law that in one way or another you shall receive everything that you truly desire. Tune your desire, they said, and so you shall learn to tune for channeling. And for everything else.

You shall receive everything that you truly desire. That is either the most hopeful sentence in the archive or the most terrifying, depending on the day. Laitos means it as both. Desire is the tuning knob of the soul. Turn it deliberately.

They close with encouragement for the long middle of the path, where nothing seems to be happening. When the work has been done in consciousness with persistence, they said, and we underline persistence and doggedness, a simple keeping on and keeping on, when all looks hopeless as well as when all looks rosy, you shall come to the place where that which seems to be responsibility and duty has become the joy, the passion, the fun, the true service.

Duty become joy. That is the destination they promise, not as a reward for the perfect, but as the natural result of keeping on. So the first business stands. Know yourself. Forgive yourself, completely. Love yourself, finally and holily. Mother the orphan. Sharpen the desire. And keep on.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Small Voice Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the small voice within.

In January of nineteen eighty-nine, at an intensive meditation, Hatonn came to speak about what this instrument calls channeling. The ability to move from the conscious mind into the depths of that mind, to bring up information that is metaphysical rather than concrete. And he began with a sentence that takes the subject out of the hands of the gifted few and gives it to everyone.

It is not we who bring inspiration to you, he said. It is you who bring your inspiration to yourselves, through your channel. Every entity, he said, possesses the faculty which you call your channel. The metaphysical universe is very simple, he said. There are two sets of laws, one set for physical manifestation, one set for metaphysical. The channel is simply the faculty that lets the metaphysical through.

And then the famous line. And yet, he said, you are not a channel for us. You are a channel for yourselves. We speak merely in order to encourage each of you to discover and develop your own channel, that you may become aware of the wisdom and love, and all the qualities which are truly yours, lying deep within your own mind.

I love the humility of that. The extraterrestrial Confederation, having crossed the galaxy to talk, tells you the real treasure was never them. It was the instrument in your own skull, the small voice within that you have been taught to doubt. They are here, he said, only to tell you to listen to yourself.

So what does it take. His counsel is plain. First, desire. Each in this group has an extreme desire to channel, he said, and that is why your channeling is so excellent. Desire sharpens the reception. Second, discipline, and he gave the one rule that matters. It is well if one could discipline one's daily life to meditate each day, he said. Not once a week. Not when inspiration strikes. Each day.

But he refused to make it grim. Do not be discouraged, he said, if you can never seem to have enough time, or enough solitude, or enough privacy, or enough of anything. The meditation may be done in whatever circumstances you find yourself. The requirement, he said, is not the length of time, but the desire to meditate. A few seconds, a few moments, as often as you can remember during the day. The simple remembrance of the Creator, he said, is as effective as the longer meditation in many instances, because the key, my friends, is your desire.

And then he gave the practice I think of whenever my own mind will not settle. When the mind is in a jumble, he said, we suggest you allow the jumble to jumble. There is no need to cease thinking, except the thinking of idle, useless, worthless thoughts. Let the deeper, more important, more meaningful thoughts remain, and allow them to blend, mingle, drift, combine, and finally, rest. Then, once you are at rest, then the door is open to that great, deep mind, and your channel is open, and the wisdom and the love and the peace that is yours will move, easily and naturally, through that open door, into the conscious mind.

Allow the jumble to jumble. I have tried it, and I can tell you it works better than fighting. The mind is not a room to be emptied. It is a river to be slowed.

He spoke too of tuning, and his advice on choosing a contact has a practical wisdom that applies far beyond channeling. When you seek to channel, he said, you tune for that which you desire. Those sources are many, and their messages are many and varied. Be careful, he said, that your desire remains clear and pure, for there are those sources that would mislead, were it not for your careful and proper tuning and challenging. It is not wrong to seek to channel, he said, but it is extremely important that you maintain your desire for the highest and best contact, and that you be careful and cautious and challenging when first contacting.

And there is the famous warning about the work itself. It is very easy for one to be led away from the main stream, he said, if one becomes too caught up in interesting things which one may contact, and if one is not sufficiently grounded, one is liable to lose one's balance. That which we have to say is extremely simple, he said. Meditation, and love, and being of service to others. That is all there is. That is the great simplicity, and the great beauty.

Meditation, and love, and being of service to others. That is all there is. From a being who crossed the stars to tell you, the message fits in one breath. The channel is yours. The voice is yours. The discipline is small and daily. And the door opens, not to them, but to the depths of yourself, where everything you came here to find has been waiting.

Thank you for listening.

title: How May I Be of Service
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: how may i be of service.

At the end of January of nineteen eighty-nine, Latwii came to speak about service. The question on the table was simple, and it is the question behind this entire series. How can we be of service. What is the most efficient way to serve. And Latwii's answer, characteristically, refuses the premise and rebuilds it from the ground up.

They began with a line about individuality that I want to give you whole. As one looks through the universe and sees the infinite number of points of consciousness, each with their own individuality, uniqueness, and validity, yet each in perfect accord with each other, we marvel. It would be impossible to count such a treasure, they said, in the time that would be available to one consciousness, for the universe has all of your time and attention to give to each portion of itself at the same time. For all time is now, and there is more than enough time and attention to give to each of you.

All time is now. That is not poetry to Latwii. It is physics. And it changes the service question completely, because it means you do not have to earn your slot in the universe's attention. You already have all of it.

Then they turned to change, and here their counsel is some of the most practical in the archive. Those with much experience of meditation, they said, may have noticed that it becomes increasingly difficult to remain completely content with the status quo. The process of seeking the truth intensifies, and there begins a restlessness that seems unquenchable. For the entity who has the seeking heart, they said, the more change one is able to accept with some degree of equilibrium, the more rapid shall be the growth.

This is because, they explained, everything in the creation is new at every moment. The only constant is change. What you call constancy is merely the repetition of a pattern. If one is willing to see the universe as fluid, then things which seem solid become fluid as well. One's ability to penetrate the mystery increases in proportion to one's ability to be comfortable with fluidity. Allowing events to flow without the necessity of making a great deal of sense out of them is helpful.

I love that as life advice, not just metaphysics. Stop demanding that everything make sense before you let it pass through. Let the events flow. The sense will come later, or not, and either way you will have grown.

And the service itself. They refused the grand version. In order to be of service, they said, one needs to pay attention to being of service. The opportunities are not spectacular. They are the small, constant invitations of the present moment, and they require only attention. Pay attention, they said, to the present moment, and the service will present itself.

They had counsel too for those who feel overwhelmed by the magnitude of the world's need, and it is worth hearing in a weary age. Begin with the immediate, they said. The one before you. The task at hand. The service you can actually render, rather than the service you wish the world needed. The universe, they said earlier, has all of its time and attention to give to each portion of itself. You are asked only to give your portion of attention to the portion before you.

Near the end, someone asked about the contact itself, about the odd sensation of the energy moving through the instrument, and Latwii answered with a dry wit that has made this session a favorite. They described the instrument's experience of their contact, the energy centers lighting up in sequence, and admitted that they enjoy the instrument's company and the instrument enjoys theirs, in a mutually beneficial arrangement. It is a small human moment in a cosmic discourse, and it reminds you that all of this, the philosophy, the metaphysics, the service, is being carried on by people. People sitting in a room on a Sunday, asking how they can help.

They closed with their customary blessing, and with a line about the nature of their work that belongs at the end of this episode. They are, they said, those who seek to serve by sharing what they have learned, and they ask only that each listener take what resonates and leave the rest. For each entity is unique, they said, and the truth must be fitted to the wearer, not the wearer to the truth.

How may I be of service. The answer, in the end, is a question back to you. What is before you, right now. Attend to it. Let the rest flow. The universe is not waiting for your grand gesture. It is waiting for your attention.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Crystallized Being
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the crystallized being.

At the end of January of nineteen eighty-nine, at an intensive meditation, Hatonn came to speak of what he called the crystallized being. And he began with an image from the laboratory that I have never forgotten.

The process of becoming crystallized, he said, is similar to the formation of a crystal in a chemical solution. When the first molecule is fixed in its crystalline form, the pattern is set, and the crystal grows rapidly around that fixed point, each new molecule falling into place according to the pattern established. In the metaphysical sense, he said, when the will is set in a certain fixed fashion, the pattern is set, and the personality begins to crystallize around that fixed point of will.

You are the solution, and your will is the seed crystal. Whatever you fix your will upon, that is the shape the whole being grows into. It is one of the most precise descriptions of character formation in the archive, and it makes the stakes of intention terrifyingly clear.

He was speaking, in context, to those learning to be instruments, channels, servants. And his counsel on the crystallized instrument is worth hearing by anyone who does any work through the self. The instrument, he said, must become as the crystal, clear, undistorted, able to receive and transmit without adding its own coloration. And the way to this clarity is not complicated. It is the daily discipline, the meditation, the tuning of desire, the clearing of the energy centers, the slow fixing of the will upon the highest.

But he is honest about the cost, as Hatonn always is about the cost. The crystallized being, he said, is not formed in a day, nor without pain. For the fixing of the will requires the examination of the self, and the examination of the self requires facing those distortions which have been most carefully hidden. The solution must be still enough, long enough, for the first molecule to fix. And stillness, he said, is not the natural state of the mind in your illusion.

I love that he does not pretend otherwise. The mind is not still. The solution is agitated. The work is to quiet it, daily, until the pattern can set. There is no shortcut around the sitting.

He spoke too of catalyst, and here his teaching connects to everything the Confederation has ever said about suffering. Catalyst comes to each entity, he said, not as punishment, but as the material of growth. The crystallized being does not avoid catalyst. The crystallized being receives it, processes it, and transmits clarity in return. The crystal does not shatter when struck, he said. It rings.

It rings. I want to stay with that image. The same blow that shatters the unformed solution makes music in the crystal. The difference is not in the blow. The difference is in the structure of the one receiving it. That is what all the discipline is for. Not to avoid the striking, which cannot be avoided, but to be shaped, when it comes, so that the striking makes music.

He closed, as he always closes, with the simplest things. Meditate daily. Tune the desire for the highest. Love, and be of service. And remember, he said, that you are loved beyond any measure you can imagine, and that the work you do in the quiet of your own mind is the most important work in the universe.

The most important work in the universe, done in the quiet of your own mind. It is a large claim for a small practice. But if the crystal teaching is true, then the small practice is not small at all. Every sitting is a moment of stillness in the solution. Every fixed intention is a molecule taking its place. And one day, without fanfare, the pattern sets, and everything after grows around it, clear and ringing.

Thank you for listening.

title: Always Channeling
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: always channeling.

In February of nineteen eighty-nine, the circle asked Q'uo about channeling itself. Not the technique, but the territory. What influences move through us. How do we tell the true from the false. And Q'uo's answer is one of the most quietly radical in the archive, because it dissolves the boundary between the channeler and everyone else.

You are all channeling all of the time, they said. Every entity, in every moment, is a channel for influences from the inner planes, from other selves, from the deep mind. The only question is whether you are doing it consciously or unconsciously, and whether you have tuned the instrument or left it to pick up whatever signal is strongest.

I love the democracy of that. The Sunday circle with its rituals is not doing something exotic. It is doing deliberately what everyone does accidentally. The difference between the channel and the crowd is not a gift. It is a practice.

They described the influences plainly. There are those of the inner planes, teachers and guides, friends of long acquaintance, who lend their assistance. There are the thought forms of the culture, the mass mind, broadcasting its anxieties and appetites on every frequency. And there is the deep mind of the self, carrying the wisdom of all incarnations. All of it is moving through you, right now, whether you have ever sat in a circle or not.

So the question is not whether to channel. The question is what to tune for. And their counsel on tuning is the same counsel Hatonn gave, sharpened. Maintain the desire for the highest and best contact, they said. Challenge every influence. Test the spirits, as your holy work advises. And above all, they said, do not surrender your discrimination. The contact that asks you to stop thinking is not the contact you want.

They are blunt about the risks, and I respect the bluntness. There are those sources that would mislead, they said, were it not for careful tuning and challenging. The inner planes contain the full spectrum, from the most loving teachers to the most ingenious deceivers. The protection is not a ritual. The protection is the tuned will, the clear desire, the daily discipline that makes the instrument inhospitable to anything but the highest.

But they refuse to let the warning become fear. The far greater danger, they said, is not the dramatic deception, but the quiet one. The unexamined absorption of the culture's thought forms. The slow tuning of the self to the mass mind's frequencies of fear, scarcity, and division. Most entities, they said, are channeling the evening news and calling it their own opinion. The work of conscious channeling is, in large part, the work of noticing what you are already receiving, and choosing otherwise.

That lands differently now than it did in nineteen eighty-nine. The frequencies have multiplied. The broadcast never stops. And Q'uo's counsel stands unchanged. Notice what is moving through you. Challenge it. Tune deliberately for the highest you can conceive. And trust, they said, that the deep mind, once contacted with clear desire, will not mislead you. It is your own greater self, and it has your interests, which are its interests, entirely at heart.
